The fifty-sixth and fifty-seventh fascicles, this "Chapter on Entering the Womb" (Ratnakūṭa-sūtra), originally titled *Buddha-nandopadeśa-pravrajyā-garbha-avatāra-sūtra*, were extracted as a separate recension by Tripiṭaka Master Yijing from the eleventh and twelfth fascicles of the *Mūlasarvāstivāda-vinaya-kṣudraka-vastu*. As Bodhiruci’s Sanskrit manuscript was checked against it and found to be identical, they were compiled into this chapter; since there was no need for a re-translation, it stands as a single text. Furthermore, its account of Nanda being compelled by the Buddha to leave the household life differs slightly at the beginning but diverges entirely later on from the corresponding section in the *Ratnakaraṇḍa-kathā* (or *Ratnāvadānamālā*). Thus, these two chapters and the preceding one, according to their literary style and content, should have been included within the Śrāvaka Piṭaka; however, they are now incorporated into the *Ratnakūṭa* collection and categorized within the Bodhisattva Piṭaka.

The Fifteenth Assembly: The Prophecy of Mañjuśrī, in three fascicles. Translated during the era of Empress Wu of the Great Tang by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan; this third translation has been collated and incorporated as a re-translation of the earlier Tang version.

This is a different translation of the same original text as the *Sūtra on the Adornment and Purity of the Buddha-land of the Original Mañjuśrī*, covering volumes fifty-eight through sixty. It consists of sixteen fascicles from the "Sixteenth Assembly:

The Bodhisattva’s Vision of Reality" (*Ṣoḍaśa-bodhisattva-darśana-tattva-parivarta*), translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Narendrayaśas of the Gao Qi dynasty. Having been verified for accuracy, it is included here as a single, previously untranslated edition.
From the sixty-first fascicle to the seventy-sixth.

The seventeenth assembly, the Pūrṇa Assembly, in three fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin dynasty; this second translation has been collated and included here as a duplicate of the old translation.
Its original title is the Bodhisattvapitaka-sūtra,
also known as the Mahākaruṇā-citta-sūtra.
It is a different translation of the same text as the Bodhisattvapitaka-sūtra translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty.
Volumes seventy-seven through seventy-nine are missing from the Jin translation.

Volume eighteen, the *Huguo pusa hui* (Assembly of the Bodhisattva Rakṣa), in two fascicles, was translated by the Sui Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta; it has been verified against the *Neidian lu* and included here. The above constitutes the old translations as single volumes.
It constitutes volumes eighty and eighty-one. The *Ninth Assembly:

The Chapter on the Householder Ugga*, one fascicle, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kang Sengyai of the Cao Wei dynasty; this third translation has been collated and included alongside the previous translations as a duplicate edition.
This is a different translation of the same text as the *Dharmādarśa-sūtra* and the *Ugraparipṛcchā-sūtra*.
It is an error to attribute the title of the eighty-second fascicle of this scripture to Kang Sengyi.
The Twentieth Assembly: The Inexhaustible Treasury, in two fascicles; newly translated by the Tripitaka Master Bodhiruci of the Great Tang.
This newly translated single-text version corresponds to the eighty-third and eighty-fourth fascicles [of the original compilation].

The Twenty-first Assembly: The Bestowal of the Prophecy upon the Illusionist Bhadra. One fascicle. Newly translated by the Tripitaka Master Bodhiruci of the Great Tang Dynasty; this is the second translation. The above is the new translation, a re-edited version.
This is a different translation of the same original text as the *Sūtra on the Former Illusionist Renxian*, corresponding to the eighty-fifth fascicle.

It consists of two fascicles, titled "The Twenty-second Assembly on Great Supernatural Transformations," newly translated by the Tripitaka Master Bodhiruci of the Great Tang. The above is a newly translated single-text edition.
Volumes eighty-six and eighty-seven;

the two volumes of the *Mahākāśyapa-parivarta*, the twenty-third assembly, translated by Prince Yueposhouna of Ujjayinī during the Northern Wei dynasty, which have been collated and included here among the previously translated single-text editions.
Volumes Eighty-eight and eighty-nine;

the twenty-fourth assembly, the *Upāli-parivarta*, one volume, newly translated by the Tripitaka Master Bodhiruci of the Great Tang, the second translation; this is the re-edited version of the new translation.
This is a different translation from the same original text as the *Jiuding pinini jing* (Sūtra on the Vinaya of Former Determinations), corresponding to the ninety-first fascicle.

It consists of two fascicles titled "The Assembly for Developing Superior Resolve and Joy" (Fashenglizhihui), newly translated by the Tripitaka Master Bodhiruci of the Great Tang; this is the third translation and a re-translation of the new version.
This is a different translation of the same text as the *Jùfā jué jìng xīn jīng* (Sūtra on the Awakening of the Pure Mind).
It corresponds to volumes ninety-one and ninety-two.

The second section, the *Shàn'ǔ púsà huì* (Assembly of the Bodhisattva Subāhu), consists of two fascicles translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin dynasty. According to the catalog of Fǎshàng, these were verified to be identical and included here among the right-hand single translations from the old editions.

Regarding the ninety-third and ninety-fourth fascicles, the *Dazhou lu* (Great Zhou Catalogue) states that these are different translations of the same text as the *Dharanidhara-bodhisattva-sūtra*, the *Lokadhāra-sūtra*, and the *Sujata-parivarta-sūtra*; however, this is incorrect. Upon examining their literary style and principles, the meaning and intent differ significantly from those of the *Dharanidhara-sūtra* and others. Furthermore, the *Sujata-sūtra* was excerpted from the *Subahu-sūtra* and is of the same category as the "Universal Gateway" chapter (*Samantamukha-parivarta*) of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra*. Because there are such differences, it is considered a standalone translation.
The Twenty-Seventh Assembly: The Good and Obedient Bodhisattva. One fascicle. Newly translated by the Tripitaka Master Bodhiruci of the Great Tang.
This newly translated single-fascicle text corresponds to fascicle ninety-five.
The Twenty-eighth Assembly: The Discourse on the Elder Ātīva-dāna. One fascicle. Newly translated by the Tripitaka Master Bodhiruci of the Great Tang.
This newly translated single-text version corresponds to fascicle ninety-six.

The Twenty-ninth: The Assembly with King Udayana, one fascicle. Newly translated by the Tripitaka Master Bodhiruci of the Great Tang; this is the second translation. The above is the new translation, a reissued version.
This is a different translation of the same original text as the *Old Udayana-rāja Sūtra*.
Regarding the ninety-seventh fascicle, the two versions—the new and the old—differ in their respective details and omissions.

This is the thirtieth chapter, the "Assembly of the Girl Prajñā," which includes one subsequent fascicle; it is the fourth translation, newly translated by the Tripitaka Master Bodhiruci of the Great Tang. This is a re-translation of the new version.
This is a different translation of the same text as the two earlier translations of the *Sūmatī-sūtra* and the previously translated *Sūtra on the Girl Prajñā* by Ratnarakṣita;
it constitutes the ninety-eighth fascicle.
From the beginning up to the midpoint, the previously translated version of the *Sūtra of Sublime Wisdom* was sought for at the Eastern Capital but was not found.

The thirty-first section, the "Assembly of the Upāsikā Gaṅgottarā," is in the same volume as the preceding [text]. This is a newly translated single fascicle by the Tripitaka Master Bodhiruci of the Great Tang.
From the midpoint to the end of the ninety-eighth fascicle, there is one fascicle titled "The Assembly of the Bodhisattva Fearless Virtue" (No.
32), translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Buddhayaśas of the Northern Wei Dynasty during his third translation; this has been collated and included as a duplicate of the earlier translation.
This is a variant translation of the same text as the *Ajātaśatru-rāja-duhitṛ-āśutara-bodhisattva-sūtra* and others;
it constitutes the ninety-ninth fascicle.

Volume thirty-three: *The Discourse on the Bodhisattva Vimaladatta’s Eloquence*, one fascicle, translated by the Western Jin layman Nie Daozhen. This second translation has been collated and included here as a reprinted version of the older translation.
This is a different translation of the same original text as the *Liǎojùshī Nǚ Jīng* (Sūtra of the Girl Vimaladattā) and the *Dédwǒujù Nǚ Jīng* (Sūtra of the Girl Vimalā).
It is an error to claim that the title of the hundredth fascicle of this text was translated by Dharmarakṣa; as will be shown below, it is the *Liǎojùshī Nǚ Jīng* that was translated by Dharmarakṣa.

The Thirty-Fourth Assembly: The Bodhisattva Puṣpadhvaja-ratna-vyūha, including one subsequent fascicle; newly translated by the Tripitaka Master Bodhiruci of the Great Tang. The above is a single-fascicle new translation.
Fascicle 111. From the beginning to the midpoint.

The thirty-fifth assembly, the Assembly of the Devaputra Śubhavyūha, is identical to the previous fascicle. Newly translated by the Tripitaka Master Bodhiruci of the Great Tang; this is the third translation, a new version based on a re-translation.

This is a different translation from the same original text as the *Adbhuta-buddha-viṣaya-nirdeśa-sūtra* (The Sūtra on the Inconceivable Realm of the Buddha Spoken by Mañjuśrī) translated earlier by Zhu Fahu;
it constitutes the one hundred and first fascicle.
From the middle to the end.

The thirty-sixth assembly, *The Assembly of the Devaputra Susthitamati*, in four fascicles, translated by the Sui Dynasty Tripiṭaka Master Dharmagupta. Recorded in the seventh volume of the *Neidian lu* (Catalogue of Inner Scriptures) as a re-translation of an old version, it has been included here after collation.
This is a different translation of the same text as the *Mayopama-samādhi-sūtra* and the *Ārya-suvikrāntavikrami-paripṛcchā-sūtra*,
spanning from fascicle 102 to fascicle 105.

The Thirty-Seventh Assembly: The Prince Ajātaśatru, together with the final three fascicles; newly translated by the Tripitaka Master Bodhiruci of the Great Tang Dynasty; this is the third translation, a re-translation of the new version.
This is a different translation of the same text as the two previously mentioned sūtras, the *Jiu taizi jing* and the *Shuahu taizi hexiu jing*.
It constitutes the first half of the one hundred and sixth fascicle.

The Thirty-Eighth Mahāyāna Session on Skillful Means, together with the preceding three fascicles, translated by the lay practitioner Zhu Nanti of India during the Eastern Jin dynasty; this third translation has been collated and incorporated alongside the previous versions. This is the re-edited version of the old translations.
This is a different translation of the same text as the *Upāyakauśalya-paripṛcchā-sūtra* (The Sūtra on the Great Skillful Means) translated by Huisang Bodhisattva.
From the middle of the one hundred and sixth fascicle to the end of the one hundred and eighth fascicle, the title of the sūtra erroneously states "Western Jin."

The thirty-ninth assembly, the *Bhadrapāla-gṛhapati-parivarta*, in two fascicles, translated by the Sui Dynasty Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta; the first translation, verified and collated, has been included herein as a re-edited version of the old translation.
The original title was *Yishijing* (Sutra on the Transference of Consciousness).

It has been newly renamed *Xianhu Zhangzhehui* (Assembly of the Elder Bhadrapāla). The opening "Certification of Faith" (*zhengxinxu*) found in the current version within the *Ratnakūṭa* collection was added later; this text is the same original work as the *Xianshijing* (Sutra on Manifesting Consciousness), though translated differently.
Volumes Ninety-one and One Hundred and Ten;

the Forty-first Assembly on the Girl Viśuddha-prasāda, together with the three subsequent assemblies in a single volume, newly translated by the Tripitaka Master Bodhiruci of the Great Tang. (The above is a newly translated single-volume edition.)
At the beginning of the one hundred and eleventh fascicle:

The forty-first assembly, "The Questions of Maitreya Bodhisattva on the Eight Dharmas," translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci of Northern Wei; this third translation has been collated and incorporated here as a re-edited version of the old translation.
Its original title is the *Sūtra on the Questions of Maitreya Bodhisattva*.
It is a different translation of the same text as the *Mahāyāna Vaipulya Essential Wisdom Sūtra*.

Within the one hundred eleventh fascicle of this [work], there is a commentary of five fascicles on these eight assemblies of dharmas; the text of the *Essential Wisdom Sūtra* is merely brief and abbreviated.

The Forty-second Assembly: The Questions of Maitreya Bodhisattva, combined with the preceding three assemblies in a single volume; newly translated by the Tripitaka Master Bodhiruci of the Great Tang Dynasty; this is the third translation and the re-edited version.
This is a different translation of the same text as the *Sūtra on the Original Vows Asked by the Former Maitreya Bodhisattva*.

It is an error to claim that the sūtra at the end of the one hundred eleventh fascicle was translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin; it is revealed later that the original *Pūrva-praṇidhāna-sūtra* was indeed translated by Dharmarakṣa.

The forty-third assembly, the *Puming pusa hui* (Assembly of the Bodhisattva Samantaprabha), one fascicle; translator lost, now appended to the Qin records. Verified as identical, it is included as the third translation. This is a re-translation of an old version.
This is the old single-fascicle *Mahāratnakūṭa-sūtra*, newly renamed the "Assembly of the Bodhisattva Samantaprabha.
It is a different translation of the same text as the two sūtras: the *Mahāyāna-ratnavyūha* and the *Buddhāvatamsaka-maṇiratna*.
Regarding the one hundred and twelfth fascicle of this *Old Ratnakūṭa Sūtra*, there is a commentary in four fascicles.

The forty-fourth assembly, the *Ratnaraśi-parivarta* (寶梁聚會), in two fascicles, translated by the Northern Liang śramaṇa Shi Daogong, has been collated and included herein among the aforementioned old translations of single-text editions.

Volumes 113 and 114; the forty-fifth assembly, the Assembly of the Bodhisattva Akṣayamati, together with the final two volumes, newly translated by the Tripitaka Master Bodhiruci of the Great Tang. The above constitutes the newly translated single-text edition.

At the beginning of the one hundred and fifteenth fascicle, the forty-sixth section, the *Mañjuśrī-bhāṣita-prajñāpāramitā-sūtra*, together with the preceding two fascicles, translated by the Liang Dynasty Tripiṭaka Master Mandaravaśa (Man-tuo-luo-xian), the first translation, has been collated and incorporated here; this constitutes the re-edited version of the old translation.
This is a different translation of the same text as the *Mañjuśrī-parivarta* from the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā-sūtra* and the *Mañjuśrī-prajñā* translated by Zhòngkǎi.
From scroll 115 to the end of scroll 116, the title of the scripture erroneously states that it was translated by Saṃghavarman.

The Forty-Seventh Assembly: The Chapter on Ratnaśikhin Bodhisattva, in two fascicles, translated by the Tripitaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin Dynasty. This is the second separately translated chapter, incorporated here after collation with the old translation; it is a reissued version of the former translation.
It is also titled the *Bodhisattva-śuddhacaryā-sūtra*.
It is a different translation of the same original text as the "Ratnacūḍa-parivarta" chapter of the *Mahāsannipāta-sūtra* and the *Bodhisattva-śuddhacaryā-sūtra* translated by Kang Senghui.
Volumes 117 and 118 contain one fascicle of the Commentary on the Ratnaśikhara-parivarta;

Volume 48 contains one fascicle of the Śrīmālādevī-parivarta, newly translated by the Tripitaka Master Bodhiruci of the Great Tang Dynasty—this is the third translation and a re-edited version of the new translation.
This is a different translation from the same original text as the *Śrīmālādevī-siṃhanāda-ekayāna-mahā-upāya-sūtra*, etc., corresponding to volume 119.

It is the forty-ninth [text], the *Vipula-rṣi-parivarta*, one fascicle, newly translated by the Tripitaka Master Bodhiruci of the Great Tang; this is the second translation and the revised version of the new translation.
This is a different translation of the same original text as the old *Viyāhapannatti* (Questions of Viyāha).

It constitutes the one hundred and twentieth fascicle. When compared with the old version, the new translation lacks slightly less than a full sheet of paper in its latter portion; some have therefore appended the old version to it, desiring to make the "Wish-Fulfilling Jewel" complete.

*Mahāvaipulya-triśikṣā-sūtra*, three fascicles; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmakṣema of India during the Northern Liang dynasty. Recorded as the first translation in the *Fashang lu*. The above sutra is an alternative translation of the same text as the "First Assembly on the Three Codes of Discipline" (*Tri-vidhi-saṃvara-parivarta*) in the *Ratnakūṭa-sūtra*.

The *Wúliàng qīngjìng píngděng jué jīng* (Sūtra of the Immeasurable Pure Equal Enlightenment), two fascicles; also simply called the *Wúliàng qīngjìng jīng* (Sūtra of Immeasurable Purity), translated during the Later Han by the Yuezhi Tripiṭaka Master Zhi Loujiachen—this is the second translation. The *Āmítuó jīng* (Amitābha Sūtra), two fascicles; the internal title reads *Āmítuó sāniè sānfó sàlóufútán guòdù rén dào jīng* (Sūtra of Amitābha, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyak-saṃbuddha, Who Transfers Humans Across), translated during the Wu dynasty by the Yuezhi layman Zhi Qian, courtesy name Gōngmíng—this is the third translation. The *Wúliàngshòu jīng* (Sūtra of Immeasurable Life), two fascicles, translated during the Cao Wei dynasty by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Kang Sengkai—this is the fourth translation. These three sūtras are as follows.

This fifth assembly, the *Amitāyus-parivarta*, is a different translation from the same original text as the *Ratnakūṭa*. Of the eleven translations of this fifth assembly, seven are missing; the Bodhisattva Vasubandhu composed one fascicle of a treatise based on the meaning of this sūtra.
The four aforementioned scriptures comprise nine fascicles in one volume.

The *Akṣobhyatathāgatasyavyūha-sūtra* (two fascicles), also known as the *Sūtra on the Training of Bodhisattvas in the Buddha-field of Akṣobhya*, was translated by the Yuezhi Tripiṭaka Master Zhi Loujiachen of the Later Han; it is the first of three translations, while one translation is missing. This is the first scripture [in this volume].
This is a different translation of the same original text as the sixth assembly, the *Ratnakūṭa Sūtra:

The Assembly of Akṣobhya Tathāgata*. It consists of one fascicle, titled the *Mahāyāna Daśadharma Sūtra*, which begins with the words: "The Buddha was dwelling in Rājagṛha. It was translated by the Tripitaka Master Saṃghavarman of Funan during the Liang dynasty and was subsequently included in the *Shiyi* (Supplementary Collection). This is the first translation of this scripture.
This is a different translation from the same original text as the ninth chapter of the *Ratnakūṭa*, the "Assembly on the Ten Dharmas of the Mahāyāna.

There is also a one-fascicle *Pumenpin jing* (Sutra of the Universal Gate), also called the *Pumen jing*, translated by the Tripitaka Master Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin; this is the first translation. Thus, there is one sutra in total.

To claim that the tenth chapter of the *Ratnakūṭa*, the "Mañjuśrī-Puṣpamāla-parivarta," is the same text as the *Mañjuśrī-Puṣpamāla-samaya* translated during the Zhou dynasty—despite being a different recension—is a grave error, as it would wrongly subsume it under the lineage of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka*. Of the three extant translations, one remains incomplete.

*The Sūtra on the Womb* (one fascicle), also titled *The Sūtra on Receiving a Body in the Womb*, translated by the Tripitaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin dynasty. This is the first translation.

The aforementioned sūtra is a different translation of the same text as the "Chapter on the Discourse to Ānanda on Dwelling in the Womb" from the thirteenth assembly of the *Ratnakūṭa Sūtra*. According to the old catalogs, this *Sūtra on the Womb* was classified as a single-text work of the Hīnayāna; it is now appended here according to its thematic category.

The *Mañjuśrī-buddhakṣetra-vyūha-pariśuddhi-sūtra* in two fascicles—also simply titled the *Vyūha-pariśuddhi-buddhakṣetra-sūtra* or the *Buddhakṣetra-vyūha-pariśuddhi-sūtra*—translated by the Tripitaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin dynasty. Of the three translations, one is missing; thus, there is one extant scripture.
The *Ratnakūṭa*, Chapter Fifteen: The Assembly on Mañjuśrī’s Prophecy, is a different translation of the same text [as the aforementioned].

The *Dharmādarśa Sūtra* in two fascicles (or one fascicle), translated by the Anxi upāsaka An Xuan together with the śramaṇa Yan Fotiao during the Later Han dynasty, constitutes the first translation. The above six sūtras comprise nine fascicles and are bound in the same volume.

*The Sūtra on the Bodhisattva Practice as Asked by Ugra*, one fascicle; alternatively titled *The Sūtra of the Elder Ugra*, or in two fascicles. Translated by the Tripitaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin. Of the four translations, three are missing. Regarding these two sūtras: [Note: The right-hand column refers to the second set of sūtras].
The *Ugraparipṛcchā-sūtra*, the nineteenth assembly with the *Ratnakūṭa*, is a different translation from the same original text.
The *Māyāśubha-sūtra* (or *Śubhamāyā-sūtra*) in one fascicle was translated by the Tripitaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin; this is the first translation. Thus, there is one such scripture.
The *Ratnakūṭa*, Volume XXI, "The Chapter on Bestowing Prophecies upon the Illusionist," is a variant translation of the same text.

The *Vinayaviniścaya-uttaragrantha* (or *Kie-tieng-p'i-ni ching*), one fascicle, also known as the *P'o-huai i-ch'ieh hsin-shih ch'un-lu*; all records state it was translated at Tun-huang, though the name of the translator and the date are not specified. It is now appended to the first record of the Eastern Chin period. This is the first translation of this scripture.
This is a different translation from the same original text as the twenty-fourth assembly with Ratnakūṭa, the Upāli-parivarta.
*The Sutra on Arousing the Pure Mind*, two fascicles, translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta and others during the Sui Dynasty; this is the first translation. The above is one sutra.
The *Ratnakūṭa*, Chapter Twenty-Five, "The Assembly on Resolving for Supreme Aspiration," is a different translation from the same original text [as the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka*].

The *Udayana-rāja-sūtra*, one fascicle, translated by the Western Jin śramaṇa Shi Faju, was added to the collection as a supplement and is listed here as the first translation. Thus, there is one such scripture.
The *Meeting with King Udayana* (the twenty-ninth assembly of the *Ratnakūṭa Sūtra*), which exists in both identical and variant translations;

the *Sūmatī Sūtra*, one fascicle—also simply titled the *Sūmatī Sūtra*—translated by the Tripitaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin (the first translation); and the *Sūmatī Bodhisattva Sūtra*, one fascicle, translated by the Tripitaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin (the second translation, included in the *Shiyi*). Of these two sūtras, there are four translations in total, of which one is missing.
The *Meeting with the Girl of Sublime Wisdom*, the thirtieth assembly of the *Ratnakūṭa*, exists in both the original text and variant translations.

There is also the one-fascicle *Sūtra of the Bodhisattva Ajātaśatru’s Daughter Arthadā*—also called the *Sūtra of Ajātaśatru’s Daughter* or simply the *Arthadā Sūtra*—translated by the Tripitaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin. Of these five translations, two are missing; thus, there is one extant sūtra.
This is a different translation of the same text as the thirty-second assembly, the "Assembly on the Virtue of Fearlessness" (*Vaiśāradyaguṇa-parivarta*), from the *Ratnakūṭa-sūtra*.

The *Vimaladattā-dārikā-sūtra* in one fascicle was translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin; it is the first translation. The aforementioned nine sūtras in ten fascicles are contained in the same volume.

The *Vimaladattā-paripṛcchā-sūtra*, one fascicle; also known as the *Vimaladattā-sūtra* or the *Dharmaparyāya of Eloquence in Discourse*. Translated by the Bactrian Brahmin Gautama Prajñāruci during the Northern Wei dynasty. This is the third translation. The above two sūtras [are included here].
This is a different translation from the same original text as the thirty-third assembly, the *Vimaladattā-parivarta*, of the *Ratnakūṭa-sūtra*.

It is the two-fascicle *Mañjuśrī-bhāṣita-acintya-buddha-viṣaya-sūtra*, translated during the era of Empress Wu of the Great Tang by the Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci of India; it is the first translation recorded in the *Dazhou lu* (Great Zhou Catalogue). The above is one scripture.
The *Sūtra on the Meeting with the Devaputra Śubhavyūha*, the thirty-fifth assembly of the *Ratnakūṭa*, is a different translation of the same original text.

The *Sūtra on the Samādhi Like an Illusion* exists in two, three, or four fascicles, translated by the Tripitaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin; this is the second translation. The *Sūtra on the Questions of the Devaputra Ārya-Suvikrāntamati* exists in three or four fascicles, translated by the Brahmin Gautama Prajñāruci of the Northern Wei; this is the fifth translation. Of these two sūtras, there are seven translations in total, of which four are missing.

The *Sūtra on the Prince Brushu* (Śuddhodana), one fascicle, translated by the Tripitaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin; this is a different translation of the same text as the thirty-sixth chapter, "The Assembly of the Well-Abiding Mind," from the *Ratnakūṭa Sūtra*.

First translation according to the *Fǎshàng Lù*: The *Sūtra of Prince Hèxiū*, one fascicle, also written as *Sīxiū*; the *Sēngyòu Lù* states that it was lost among the scriptures of unknown translators in the records of Master Ān [Dharmakṣema], and is now appended here to the Western Jin records. These two sūtras constitute the third translation.
The *Ratnakūṭa*, the thirty-seventh assembly, the meeting with Prince Ajātaśatru, is the same text as a different translation.
The six aforementioned scriptures comprise ten fascicles in one volume.

The *Upāyakauśalyaparipṛcchā-sūtra* (The Sūtra on the Bodhisattva Hui-shang’s Inquiry into Great Skillful Means), two fascicles, or one fascicle, translated by the Tripitaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin; this is the second translation, while three of the five translations are missing. Of these, the aforementioned single scripture is included.
This is a different translation from the same original text as the thirty-eighth assembly, the *Mahāyānopāya-parivarta*, of the *Ratnakūṭa*.

The *Mahāyāna-vijñapti-prakāśana-sūtra* in two fascicles was translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śīlabhadra of Central India during the Great Tang Dynasty; it is recorded as the second translation in the *Dazhou Catalogue*. The above is one sutra.

The *Jñānottarabodhisattva-paripṛcchā-sūtra* (translated during the Later Han by An Shigao, the Tripiṭaka Master from Parthia), which is a different translation of the same text as the *Ratnakūṭa*, Chapter 39, the *Assembly of the Elder Bhadrapāla*. One fascicle. First translation. The above is one scripture.
This is a different translation from the same original text as the forty-first assembly, the "Maitreya Questions on the Eight Dharmas," within the *Ratnakūṭa*.
It consists of one fascicle, translated by the Western Jin Tripiṭaka Master Dharmarakṣa. Of the three translations, one is missing. (The above is one scripture.)
The *Maitreya-paripṛcchā-parivarta*, the forty-second chapter of the *Ratnakūṭa*, is a different translation from the same original text. 1.

The *Buddhāvaivartika-maṇiratna-sūtra* (one fascicle), also known as the *Gupin* (Ancient Chapter) or the *Yirishuo banruo jing* (Sūtra on the Exposition of Prajñā by the Departed Sun). Translated during the Later Han dynasty by the Yuezhi Tripiṭaka Master Lokakṣema. This is the first translation. 2. The *Mahāyāna-ratnālaṃkāra-sūtra* (one fascicle), also titled the *Mahākāśyapa-parivarta*. Translated during the Jin dynasty; the name of the Tripiṭaka Master is lost. It was formerly included in the catalog of the Later Han period, and for now, it follows that tradition. This is the second translation. The above two sūtras [are listed here].
The *Pu-ming pusa hui* (Assembly of the Bodhisattva Samantaprabhā), the forty-third assembly of the *Ratnakūṭa*, is a different translation of the same original text.

The *Śrīmālā-siṃhanāda-ekayāna-mahopāya-vaipulya-sūtra*, one fascicle—also simply called the *Śrīmālā-sūtra*—was translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Guṇabhadra of India during the Song dynasty; it is the second translation, while the third translation is missing. The above sutra is a different translation of the same original text as the *Śrīmālā-devī-parivarta*, the forty-eighth assembly of the *Ratnakūṭa*.

The *Vyāsaparipṛcchāsūtra* in two fascicles, translated by the Brahmin Gautama Prajñāruci during the Northern Wei dynasty; the first record of the translation follows. This is the aforementioned single scripture.

The preface to the *Ratnakūṭa*, the forty-ninth assembly with the Venerable Viśvāmitra, which exists in both original and alternative translations, states: "In the fourth year of the Xinghe era of the Wei dynasty, the year being Renxu, the moon positioned in Shen, the first day of the month being Yichou, the Brahman guest Gautama Dharmaruci and the śramaṇa Tánlín translated this at the residence of Gāogōng, the Minister of the Imperial Secretariat and Grand Master of Ceremonies. It was completed on the Jiamǔ day of the Xin-si month of the Jiànchū era. In total, there are fourteen thousand four hundred and fifty-seven characters. All catalogs state that it was translated by Ratnamati or by Bodhiruci; these two claims are both erroneous. Now, following the preface, this is established as the correct version. Regarding this *Vaiśravaṇa-sūtra*, while previous catalogs classified it as a single-text work of the Hīnayāna, upon examination, it is now determined to be a Mahāyāna re-translation.
The eight preceding scriptures comprise eleven fascicles in one volume.

As for the Mahāsaṃnipāta section, all works belonging to the category of the Mahāsaṃnipāta are compiled here; in total, there are twenty-four sections comprising one hundred and forty-two fascicles arranged in fourteen volumes.

The Mahāvaipulya Mahāsannipāta Sūtra, thirty fascicles, translated at Guzang by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmakṣema of India during the Northern Liang dynasty; this is the third translation. Of the three translations, two are missing. I have carefully examined them.
The *Record of the Mahāsannipāta* by the Liang dynasty śramaṇa Sengyou states:
"There are twelve sections of discourse that together constitute a single sūtra.
The first is the 'Necklace Chapter' (*Ratnavyūha-parivarta*)."
The second is the "Chapter on the Sovereign King of Dhāraṇīs";
the third is the "Chapter on the Precious Woman";
the fourth is the "Chapter on the Unblinking."
The fifth is the "Chapter on Sāgaramati," the sixth is the "Chapter on the Wordless," and the seventh is the "Chapter on the Ineffable."
8. The Section on the Treasury of Space;
9. The Section on the Jewel Banner;
10. The Section on the Eyes of Space.
Eleventh, the "Chapter on Ratnaśikhin";
Twelfth, the "Chapter on Akṣayamati.
Now, upon examining the extant versions of the sūtra, these differ from the records of Sengyou.

Regarding the "Chapter on the Bodhisattva Sovereign King of the First Dhāraṇī," there are some versions of the scripture that divide it into the "Chapter on the Necklace" (Yingluo-pin); this is not correct, as it constitutes a single section and should not be divided into two. Furthermore, the subsequent "Sutra of Great Compassion" (Dai'ai-jing) is precisely the second chapter of this work, the "Chapter on the Precious Woman" (Baonü-pin).
Chapter Three: The Bodhisattva Animiṣa;
Chapter Four: The Bodhisattva Sāgaramati;
Chapter Five: The Bodhisattva Gaganagañja.
Chapter Six: The Bodhisattva Without Speech;
Chapter Seven: The Ineffable Bodhisattva; Chapter Eight:
The Section on the Jewel Banner.
The ninth is the *Gaganakṣayanirdeśa-parivarta*; the tenth is the *Ratnaśikhara-bodhisattva-parivarta*.

Regarding the tenth, the *Sūryagarbha-parivarta*, I have searched through various catalogs; the number of fascicles for this *Mahāsaṃnipāta-sūtra* is not fixed. Some say it consists of twenty-nine, some thirty, some thirty-one, some thirty-two, or forty fascicles. At present, most versions of the *Mahāsaṃnipāta* consist of thirty fascicles. The text of the *Sūryagarbha-parivarta* is incomplete, lacking one fascicle. The version in thirty-one fascicles should be complete, yet though I have sought it, I have not yet found it. However, in Sengyou’s record:
It is not the case that there is no *Akṣayamati-parivarta* within the *Guhyaka-vyuha*;
for although the *Akṣayamati-sūtra* is a distinct section of the *Mahāsaṃnipāta*, it is not without a translation by Kumārajīva.
Furthermore, it does not follow the sequential order of the *Samantabhadra-avatāra* (or *Anupūrva-samāpatti*).
Its *Gaganagañja-parivarta* is placed after the *Avaktavya*; the reason for this remains undetermined.
From the *Dhāraṇīśvararāja-parivarta* to the *Sūryagupta-bhāga*, there are eleven sections in total.
The *Sūryagarbha-sūtra* and the *Sūryaguhya-vibhāga* are different translations of the same original text.

Furthermore, both the eleventh fascicle of the *Sūryaguhya-vibhāga* and the first fascicle of the *Sūryagarbha-sūtra* state that after teaching the "Amṛta-gate of Ānāpāna with the Sky-Eye" (*ākāśanetrānāpānamṛtadvāra*), they subsequently teach this sūtra.

Furthermore, since the "Division on the Sun’s Secret" (*Sūryaguhya-parivarta*) is stated to follow immediately after the "Chapter on the Eyes" (*Netra-parivarta*) in the void of space, it would not be appropriate for it to be separated by the "Chapter on Ratnaśikhin" (*Ratnaśikhin-parivarta*) according to the underlying meaning; however, this chapter intervenes in the current edition of the sutra, the reason for which remains unclear.

Furthermore, although the *Sūryagarbha* and the *Candragarbha* share the same root text, the *Sūryagarbha* section is extremely abbreviated, and its subsequent portions are missing by several fascicles.

The *Candragarbha-sūtra* is the twelfth division; some manuscript editions of the sūtra are titled *Mahāyāna Mahāsaṃnipāta-sūtra, Candragarbha Division, Part Twelve*. At the beginning of the sūtra, it further states: "Having transformed the various hosts of nāgas and preached the *Sūryagarbha-sūtra*, he next preached this sūtra."

Regarding the *Daśacakrakṣitigarbha-sūtra*, the beginning of the thirteenth fascicle states that after the *Candragarbha-sūtra* has been preached, this sūtra is next expounded. This *Daśacakrakṣitigarbha-sūtra* consists of fourteen fascicles; the original manuscript of the fourteenth fascicle remains in the Western Regions and has not yet circulated here.
The *Sumerugarbha-sūtra* is the fifteenth division of the sūtra; its initial title reads: *Mahāyāna Mahāsannipāta-sūtra, Sumerugarbha-parivarta, the Fifteenth*.
The sixteenth division is combined with the *Gaganagañja-sūtra*; its beginning states that after the Dharma was given as a prediction (*vyākaraṇa*) to Śrīdevī, this sūtra was subsequently taught.
However, the *Sumerugarbha Sūtra* was spoken by the Tathāgata only after being requested by the goddess Puṇyavatī;
thus, it is known that this sūtra should properly occupy the next position.
As for the *Sūryagarbha Sūtra*, it was first preached at the Kalandaka Bamboo Grove.
Next, he ascended the summit of Mount Sumeru.
Later, at the request of the nāgas, he went to Mount Khadiraka;
the four sūtras, including the *Candragarbha*, were all preached on Mount Khadiraka.
The sequence is as follows:
although the *Bhadrapāla*, *Rājāvavādaka*, *Akṣayamati*, and other such sūtras on the *buddhānusmṛti-samādhi* are distinct sections of the *Mahāsaṃnipāta*, they are nonetheless included here.
Since the sequence is unknown, it is difficult to compile and record [the texts].
However, the monk Jiu of the Sui dynasty combined the *Mahāsaṃnipāta-sūtra* with the *Pañcāśikā-prajñāpāramitā-parīkṣā-sūtra*,
subsequently titling the latter the "Chapter on the Bodhisattvas of the Ten Directions."

It is incorrect to claim that after the *Candragarbha-parivarta* was compiled, the *Akṣayamati-nirdeśa-sūtra* was added to form fifty-eight fascicles; since there is no authoritative basis for this, one should not rely upon it.

As for the compilation of the *Mahāsaṃnipāta-sūtra* into sixty fascicles, the thirty-first and thirty-second fascicles duplicate the *Ratna-śikhara-parivarta*, thereby completing the total of sixty. This *Ratna-śikhara-parivarta* appears previously in fascicles twenty-six and twenty-seven before the *Sūryagarbha-parivarta*; it is unclear why it was duplicated here. Furthermore, as the Sanskrit originals for the *Sūryagarbha* and *Candragarbha* are not different, to compile them repeatedly is a grave error. If one wishes to merge them:
In the former *Mahāsaṃnipāta-sūtra*, excluding the *Dīrghanakha-parivarta* (Day Secret) section, there were twenty-seven fascicles.

Since the Sanskrit manuscript for the portion where the *Dīrghanakha-parivarta* (Day Treasury) was substituted is likewise the *Dīrghanakha-parivarta* (Day Secret), yet the Chinese text is slightly deficient, the *Dīrghanakha-parivarta* (Day Treasury) has been used as a replacement. This is followed by the *Candragarbha-parivarta* (Moon Treasury).
Next is the *Daśacakrakṣitigarbha-sūtra*, translated into Chinese in ten fascicles; next is the *Sumerugarbha-sūtra*;
and next is the *Gaganagañja-sūtra*.
Although the sequence of these latter four sūtras is not known, they follow in order.
If one combines them according to their intent, there will likewise be no loss.

Following the *Ākāśagarbha-sūtra*, the *Buddhānusmṛti-samādhi-sūtra* translated during the Song dynasty in six fascicles shall take the place of the ten-fascicle version translated during the Sui dynasty, as the latter lacks two chapters; next is the *Bhadrapāla-sūtra*.

Next is the *Anantamukhanirhāradhāraṇī-sūtra* (The Sūtra of the Inexhaustible Intention). At its conclusion, it totals eighty fascicles, which also nearly accords with the [original] agreement. The title at the beginning of this *Anantamukha-sūtra* reads:

"The Thirty-second Chapter, 'The Exposition of the Inexhaustible Meaning,' Spoken by the Bodhisattva Anantamukha within the *Mahāsannipāta-sūtra*. Thus, it is indeed the thirty-second division. However, it is clearly evident that its placement after the *Ratnacūḍa-parivarta* in the records of Saṃghavarman, as well as its inclusion at the end of the *Mahāsannipāta* compilation by Saṃghapāla, is incorrect. Furthermore, there is the *Susthitamatidevaputraparipṛcchā-sūtra*; upon examining its textual meaning, it should properly be a separate division of the *Mahāsannipāta*. It has already been incorporated into the *Mahāratnakūṭa*, so it cannot be recorded here twice; therefore, it is omitted from this list.

The *Mahāvaipulya Mahāsannipāta Sūtra: Division on the Sun* (*Mahāvaipulya-mahāsannipāta-sūtra-sūryagarbha-parivarta*), ten fascicles (or fifteen fascicles), one volume, section eleven; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Narendrayaśas of India during the Sui dynasty. This is identical to the *Sūryaguhya* [section] and constitutes the fourth translation. Of the aforementioned scriptures, this one shares the same original text as the *Sūryaguhya* section at the end of the previous *Mahāsannipāta Sūtra*, yet it is a different translation. The text of the *Sūryaguhya* is concise, whereas this version is somewhat more extensive.

The *Mahāsaṃnipāta-candragarbha-sūtra* (Dàjí yuèzàng jīng), ten fascicles (or fifteen fascicles), one set; the twelfth division. Translated by the Tripitaka Master Narendrayaśas of India during the Northern Qi dynasty, based on a selected manuscript of the Mahāyāna *Mahāsaṃnipāta-kṣitigarbha-daśacakra-sūtra*, ten fascicles; the thirteenth division. One set. Translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang of the Great Tang. The *Neidian lu* records this as the second translation. The *Bhadrakalpika-mahāvaipulya-daśacakra-sūtra*, eight fascicles; translator lost; currently appended to the Northern Liang catalog as the first translation. These two sutras are the same text with different translations. Regarding the old *Daśacakra-sūtra*, the *Dazhou lu* states it was translated by Dharmakṣema. However, upon examining Daofang’s *Ruzang lu*, it states that the translator is lost; thus, the *Zhou lu* is in error.

*Mahāsaṃnipāta Sūtra: The Sumerugarbha*, two fascicles; the fifteenth division, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Narendrayaśas of India during the Northern Qi dynasty, together with Fazhi. Single volume, upper part. The above two sūtras comprise ten fascicles in one bundle. *Ākāśagarbha Bodhisattva Sūtra*, one fascicle (sometimes without the word "Bodhisattva"). Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Buddhayaśas of Kapiśī during the Yao Qin dynasty, brought to the Qin state from Kapiśī. First translation. *Ākāśagarbha Bodhisattva Divine Mantra Sūtra*, one fascicle. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmamitra of Kapiśī during the Song dynasty. Third translation. *Ākāśagarbha Bodhisattva Sūtra*, two fascicles. Combined as the sixteenth division, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta of India and others during the Sui dynasty. Fourth translation. The above three sūtras share the same original text but have different translations. Among the four successive translations, one translation is missing its text.

*The Scripture on the Contemplation of the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha*, one fascicle; also titled *The Scripture on the Contemplation of Ākāśagarbha* (or without the word "contemplation"), translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmamitra of Kasmīra during the Song dynasty. *The Scripture on the Samādhi of Buddha-remembrance of the Bodhisattva*, six fascicles; also titled [without the word] "Bodhisattva," translated by the Indian Śramaṇa Guṇabhadra together with Xuanchang during the Song dynasty. These first two translations comprise eleven fascicles in total and are contained in the same volume as the five preceding scriptures.

*The Mahāvaipulya Mahāsaṃnipāta Bodhisattva Buddhanusmṛti Samādhi Sūtra*, ten fascicles, one volume; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmagupta of India during the Sui Dynasty. [Recorded in] the second section of the *Neidian lu*. The above two sūtras are translations of the same original text with different versions. Compared to the preceding sūtra, the Sui translation lacks one chapter at the end, and thus its text is incomplete.

*Pratyutpanna Samādhi Sūtra*, three fascicles (sometimes with the character "Da" [大] added, or in two fascicles), translated by the Yuezhi Tripiṭaka Master Lokakṣema of the Later Han Dynasty; the first translation. *Bapī Bodhisattva Sūtra*, one fascicle—also known as the *Babō*; Sengyou’s catalogue states that this is an alternative translation of the first four chapters of the *Pratyutpanna Sūtra* from the ancient scriptures of Master Dao’an. Fifth appearance; now appended to the Han records. *Mahāvaipulya Mahāsannipāta Bhadrapāla Sūtra*, five fascicles (also simply called the *Bhadrapāla Sūtra*, or in six fascicles), translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta and others of the Sui Dynasty; the seventh translation. The above three sūtras are different translations of the same text; there have been seven translations in total, of which four original versions are missing.
The three preceding scriptures comprise nine fascicles in one volume. The *Akṣayamati-nirdeśa-sūtra* (seven fascicles;

translated during the Jin dynasty as the *Wujinyi*, or in four or five fascicles) was translated by the Tripitaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin. The third translation, the *Akṣayamati-bodhisattva-sūtra* (six fascicles), also known as the *Akṣayamati-sūtra*, was excerpted from the *Mahāsaṃnipāta-sūtra* and translated by the Śramaṇa Zhìyán of Liangzhou together with Bǎoyún during the Song dynasty. These two scriptures are translations of the same original text with different versions; of the five successive translations, three are missing.
The first two sutras, totaling thirteen fascicles, are contained in the same volume.

*Mahāsaṃnipāta-dṛṣṭāntarāja-sūtra*, two fascicles; translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta and others of the Sui Dynasty; included in the *Shiyi* (Supplementary Collection) as a single-text edition. *Mahākaruṇā-sūtra*, eight fascicles—also known as the *Tathāgata-mahākaruṇā-sūtra*; alternatively in six or seven fascicles; translated by the Western Jin Tripiṭaka Master Dharmarakṣa. The above sutra is a variant translation of the "Dhāraṇīśvararāja-bodhisattva-parivarta" from the beginning of the *Mahāsaṃnipāta-sūtra*, corresponding from the beginning of the first fascicle to the middle of the fifth fascicle.
The two aforementioned scriptures comprise ten fascicles in one volume.

The *Ratnāvalī-paripṛcchā-sūtra* (寶女所問經) consists of three fascicles—also titled the *Ratnāvalī-paripṛcchā-prajñā-sūtra* (寶女問慧經)—or four fascicles; it was translated by the Tripitaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin. This single scripture is a separate translation of the "Ratnāvalī Chapter" from the *Mahāsaṃnipāta-sūtra*, corresponding to the section from the middle of the fifth fascicle to the middle of the seventh fascicle.

*The Sūtra of the Silent Youth* (Mūkanārāyaṇaparipṛcchā-sūtra), two fascicles; alternatively titled *The Sūtra of the Silent Bodhisattva*, or one fascicle. Translated by the Tripitaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin dynasty. This sūtra is an alternative translation of the "Chapter on the Silent One" from the *Mahāsannipāta-sūtra*, corresponding to the latter half of the seventeenth fascicle through the first half of the eighteenth fascicle.

*The Sūtra of the Bodhisattva Vaśavartin-rāja*, two fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin dynasty at the Xiāoyáo Garden; the first translation. *The Sūtra of the Questions of Vaśavartin-rāja*, two fascicles, translated by the Brahmin Gautama Prajñāruci and others of the Northern Wei; the second translation, including the preface and record. These two sūtras are the same text with different translations. Regarding the preface and record of the *Vaśavartin-rāja-sūtra*, it states:

In the fourth year of the Weixing era, the year being Renxu, the moon positioned in Shen, the first day of the month being Yichou, on the day of Jiawu, the śramaṇa Tanlin and Gautama Liuji began the work at the residence of the Duke Gao, the Minister of State and Grand Marshal.
The total number of characters translated is 18,341.
All catalogs state that this was translated by Bodhiruci, which is an error;
we now follow the preface record as the correct version.
Furthermore, the *Neidian lu* (Inner Canon Catalogue) states regarding the aforementioned two sutras:
"It is not correct to claim that these are alternative translations of the 'Dhāraṇī-īśvara-rāja-bodhisattva-parivarta' chapter of the *Mahāsannipāta-sūtra*.
Upon examining their literary style and principles, they differ by a vast margin."
It may simply be a separate section of the *Mahāsaṃnipāta-sūtra*,
or perhaps these two sūtras are not parts of the *Mahāsaṃnipāta* at all; rather,
they are merely different translations of the same text, as all catalogues of previous dynasties state.
Although the collated versions of the "Chapter on the Sovereign King of Dhāraṇīs" differ, they are recorded here at the end of the *Mahāsannipāta*.
The four aforementioned sūtras, totaling nine fascicles, are contained in the same volume.

The *Ratnaketudhāraṇī Sūtra*, ten fascicles (or eight fascicles), one set; translated by the Tripitaka Master Śīlavarman of India during the Great Tang Dynasty. This single work is recorded in the *Neidian lu*. Regarding this sūtra, the *Neidian lu* states: [text follows].
This is a separate section of the *Mahāsaṃnipāta Sūtra*.

Having carefully examined the "Ratnaketu" section within the aforementioned *Mahāsaṃnipāta Sūtra*, it is recorded that the Buddha preached this *Ratnajyoti Dhāraṇī Sūtra* once again within the Great Jewel Enclosure (*mahāratnavyūha*) situated between the realms of desire and form.
Therefore, the first section of the *Ratnaketu-dhāraṇī* states: "The Buddha was in the Great Jewel Enclosure between the realms of desire and form, and addressed the great assembly, saying:
'In the past, when I first attained bodhi...'"
He was dwelling in the Kalandaka Bamboo Grove at Rājagṛha.
At that time, there were two wise men in the city;
one was named Upatiṣya.
The second is named Kolita and so forth;
the meaning of the subsequent passages up to the end is identical throughout.
This sutra may be recited as a repetition.
It should not be translated again.
Furthermore, among the old catalogs there was a *Ratnacūḍaparipṛcchāsūtra*, which is an alternative translation of the "Ratnacūḍa-parivarta.
It has now been included in the *Ratnakūṭa* collection as the forty-seventh assembly.
Once it has been included therein, this [text] is not to be carried again.
Furthermore, there is an eight-fascicle version of the *Ākāśagarbha-sūtra* which, upon examination, has no different recension;
it is simply an excerpt from the *Ākāśagarbha-parivarta* circulated separately.
Furthermore, there is the *Ākāśagarbha-paripṛcchā-sūtra on the Merit Attained by Upholding this Sūtra*. It states: "This is an excerpt from a separate text of the *Ākāśagarbha-parivarta*.
Since it is a derivative work, it has been excluded and not recorded here.
Furthermore, within the *Neidian lu* (Inner Canon Catalogue) and the *Dazhou lu* (Great Zhou Catalogue), there is additionally an eight-fascicle *Mahāsaṃnipāta Sūtra*.
Upon examining its textual passages, it is identical to the sixth bundle of the *Hebu daji jing* (Combined Mahāsaṃnipāta Sūtra).
The first two fascicles are titled "Chapter on the Bodhisattvas of the Ten Directions.
This chapter is actually the *Pañcaśatikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*;
for whatever reason, it has been incorporated into this [text].
The final six fascicles are the *Akṣayamati-nirdeśa-sūtra*.
As they are both redundant and cumbersome, they have been omitted and not recorded here.

Within this section on the *Avataṃsaka*, including the root *Avataṃsaka* scriptures and their affiliated texts, there are twenty-six works in one hundred and eighty-seven fascicles, compiled into eighteen bundles. The *Mahāvaipulya-buddhāvataṃsaka-sūtra* consists of sixty fascicles (or fifty fascicles) in six bundles. It was translated during the Eastern Jin dynasty by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Buddhabhadra and others. This is the first translation of the Great Text. To the right, this scripture comprises seven locations and eight assemblies.
In total there are thirty-four chapters,
listed below as follows.

The first, the *Assembly at the Site of Enlightenment of Ultimate Quiescence*, comprises two chapters in three fascicles. The second, the *Assembly at the Hall of Universal Radiance*, comprises six chapters in four fascicles. The third, the *Assembly in the Palace of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven*, comprises six chapters in three fascicles. The fourth, the *Assembly in the Palace of the Yāma Heaven*, comprises four chapters in two fascicles. The fifth, the *Assembly in the Palace of the Tuṣita Heaven*, comprises three chapters in ten fascicles. The sixth, the *Assembly in the Palace of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven*, comprises eleven chapters in thirteen fascicles; this new edition is divided into two assemblies. The seventh, the *Reassembly at the Hall of Universal Radiance*, comprises one chapter in six fascicles. The eighth, the *Assembly in the Anāthapiṇḍada Garden*, comprises one chapter in fourteen fascicles. The *Mahāvaipulya Buddhāvataṃsaka Sūtra* consists of eighty fascicles in eight volumes, translated during the reign of Empress Wu of the Great Tang by the Khotanese Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda and others. This new compilation was entered into the canon as a re-translation of the Great Text. These two scriptures are translations of the same original work with different versions.
These newly translated scriptures comprise seven locations and nine assemblies,
totaling thirty-nine chapters,
which are listed below.
The first assembly, held at the site of enlightenment (Bodhimaṇḍa), consists of six chapters in eleven fascicles;

the second assembly, held in the Hall of Universal Radiance (Samantābhāsagṛha), consists of six chapters in four fascicles; the third assembly, held in the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, consists of six chapters in three fascicles;
the fourth assembly, held in the Yāma Heaven, consists of four chapters in three fascicles; and the fifth assembly was held in the Tuṣita Heaven.
The combined three sections comprise twelve fascicles; the sixth assembly, preached in the Palace of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven, comprises one section in six fascicles;
the seventh re-assembly, preached in the Universal Radiance Hall, comprises eleven sections in thirteen fascicles;
the eighth re-assembly, preached in the Universal Radiance Hall, comprises one section in seven fascicles; and the ninth assembly, preached in Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park, comprises one section.
The *Śraddhābalādhānāvatāramudrā-sūtra* in twenty-one fascicles, five fascicles [of which remain], translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmaruci of India during the Northern Wei dynasty;
a single-text edition. The *Sarvabuddhaviṣayāvatārajñānālokalaṃkāra-sūtra* in one fascicle, translator lost, now appended to the records of the Qin dynasty. The above is one sūtra.
The *Dazhou lu* states that this was translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci during the Northern Wei dynasty;

however, according to the *Changfang lu* and other records, there is no scripture by this title among the translations attributed to Bodhiruci. It is therefore classified here as a work of lost translation appended to the Qin catalog. Furthermore, the claim that it is a different translation of the same original text as the *Tathāgata-alaṃkāra-jñāna-prabhā-sarvabuddha-viṣaya-anupraveśa-sūtra* and the *Sarvabuddha-viṣaya-jñānālaṃkāra-sūtra* is erroneous. Upon examining its literary style, principles, and purport, these differ entirely. Although the titles appear similar, what they expound is distinct. Seeking their underlying intent, it is found to be a different translation of the same original text as the *Buddhāvataṃsaka-tathāgataguṇajñānācintyaviṣayāvatāra-nirdeśa-sūtra*; thus, it has been moved here for inclusion.

*The Buddha’s Flower Adornment Sutra on Entering the Inconceivable Realm of the Tathāgata’s Wisdom and Virtue*, two fascicles; translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta and others during the Sui dynasty. Recorded in the third volume of the *Neidian lu*. *The Mahāvaipulya Sutra on Entering the Inconceivable Wisdom and Virtue of the Tathāgata*, one fascicle; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan during the reign of Empress Wu of the Great Tang. Newly included in the fourth volume of the catalog. The above three sutras are translations of the same original text with different versions. Among the four extant translations—two old and two new—one version is missing.

*The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Chapter on the Inconceivable Realm of the Buddhas*, one fascicle (or two fascicles), thirteen sheets; translated during the era of the Empress of the Great Tang by the Tripiṭaka Master Tiyuṇaprajña of Khotan. Recorded as the first translation in the *Dazhou Catalogue*. *The Mahāvaipulya Tathāgata-acintya-viṣaya Sūtra*, one fascicle; translated during the era of the Empress of the Great Tang by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan. Newly included in the catalogue as the second translation. The above two sūtras are the same text with different translations.

*Mahāyāna-vajra-śikhā-maṇi-bodhisattva-caryā-prakaraṇa*, one fascicle; also titled *Vajramālā-bodhisattva-prayoga-parivarta*. Translated during the reign of the Empress of the Great Tang by the Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci of India. Recorded as a single volume in the *Dazhou Catalogue*. *Mahāvaipulya-buddhāvataṃsaka-sūtra-maitrī-bhāvanā-prakaraṇa*, one fascicle. Translated during the reign of the Empress of the Great Tang by the Tripiṭaka Master Tiyun般若 (Prajñā) of Khotan. Newly included in the catalog as a single volume. The above eight scriptures, totaling thirteen fascicles, are contained in the same case.

*The Mahāvaipulya Sūtra Spoken by Samantabhadra Bodhisattva*, one fascicle. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan during the reign of Empress Wu of the Great Tang; newly included in the canon as a single-text edition. *The Sūtra on Adorning the Bodhicitta*, one fascicle. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin dynasty; the fourth translation. *The Mahāvaipulya Bodhisattva Daśabhūmika Sūtra*, one fascicle. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kiṅkiaya of the Western Regions together with Tanyao of the Northern Wei; the fifth translation. Regarding the above two sūtras, which are different translations of the same text, there were previously five translations in total, three of which are now missing. As for this *Bodhisattva Daśabhūmika Sūtra*, the record of the Great Zhou states that it is an alternative translation of the "Ten Abodes" chapter (*Daśabhūmika*) of the *Avataṃsaka*. This is an error. Upon examining the phrasing and the essential meaning, they differ vastly; it can only be considered an affiliated work of the *Avataṃsaka*.
The eleven sutras beginning with the *Dhāraṇī-mudrā-praveśa-dharma-paryāya* (Right Faith Power Entry Seal Dharma Gate) all share similarities with portions of the *Avataṃsaka*.
They are categorized as affiliated texts rather than the primary division itself.
Because the adornments of these three types of worlds are inferior [to those in the full version].

*The Tusha Sutra*, one fascicle, translated by the Yuezhi Tripiṭaka Master Zhi Loujiachen of the Later Han. The above sutra is an alternative translation of the "Chapter on the Names of the Tathāgatas" from the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*. The old translation is found in the fifth fascicle of the old version, while the new translation is in the twelfth fascicle of the new version; compared to the Great Text, this sutra is somewhat abbreviated.

*The Sūtra on the Original Vows and Activities of Bodhisattvas* (one fascicle), also simply titled *The Original Vows Sūtra*, or alternatively called *The Sūtra on Pure Conduct*. Translated by the Upāsaka Zhi Qian of Yuezhi during the Wu dynasty. *The Sūtra on the Original Vows for Becoming a Buddha of All Bodhisattvas* (one fascicle); some editions omit the word "all. Translated by the lay believer Nie Daozhen of the Western Jin dynasty. The two sūtras above are alternative translations of the "Chapter on Pure Conduct" (*Śuddhacaryā-parivarta*) from the *Avataṃsaka-sūtra*. The old translation is found in the sixth fascicle, while the new translation is in the fourteenth. As for the version translated by Zhi Qian, it includes the "Ten Stages Chapter" (*Daśabhūmika-parivarta*) and lacks the verses. Furthermore, the *Catalogue of the Canon Compiled during the Great Zhou* lists yet another *Sūtra on the Original Vows of Bodhisattvas* (one fascicle), which is also an alternative translation of the "Chapter on Pure Conduct"; however, as its original could not be located, it has been omitted here.

*The Chapter on the Bodhisattva’s Practice of the Ten Abodes*, one fascicle; also simply titled *The Bodhisattva’s Ten Abodes*. Translated by the Western Jin Tripiṭaka Master Dharmarakṣa. Included in the *Fashang Jinglu Shiyi* (Supplement to Fashang’s Catalogue of Scriptures). *Bodhisattva’s Ten Abodes Sūtra*, one fascicle. Translated by the Eastern Jin Tripiṭaka Master from the Western Regions Gītamitra. The above two sūtras are alternative translations of the "Bodhisattva’s Ten Abodes" chapter [of the Avataṃsaka]. The old version is in the ninth fascicle, while the new version is in the sixteenth fascicle; the latter is largely devoid of verses.
*Jianbei yiqiezhide jing* (Sūtra on the Gradual Preparation of All-Wise Virtue), five fascicles or ten fascicles, translated by the Western Jin Tripiṭaka Master Dharmarakṣa;

the above nine sūtras total thirteen fascicles and are contained in the same volume. *Shizhu jing* (Sūtra on the Ten Abodes), four fascicles or five fascicles, translated by the Yao Qin Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva together with Buddhayaśas. The two aforementioned sūtras are alternative translations of the "Ten Grounds" (*Daśabhūmi*) chapter of the *Avataṃsaka*. The old version [of the *Ten Grounds*] runs from fascicle 25 to fascicle 29, while the new version runs from fascicle 34 to fascicle 39. *Daśabhūmivyākhyāna-śāstra* (Commentary on the Ten Grounds) composed by Bodhisattva Vasubandhu, twelve fascicles.

*Samādhi-sūtra Asked by the Bodhisattva Samantadarśin*, two fascicles; also known as *The Concentrated Intent of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra*, or three fascicles. Translated by the Tripitaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin. This aforementioned scripture is an alternative translation of the "Ten Samādhis" chapter from the *New Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, corresponding to fascicles forty through forty-three. The old *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* lacks this "Ten Samādhis" chapter. Although the *Zhou Catalogue* lists this *Sūtra Asked by Samantadarśin* as a separate work, upon examination it is now classified as a retranslation.

*The Scripture Revealing the Merits of Boundless Buddha-lands*, one fascicle; translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang of the Great Tang. [Recorded in the *Neidian lu*. Of the above, this single scripture is an alternative translation of the "Chapter on Lifespan" from the *Avataṃsaka-sūtra*. The old translation was in fascicle thirty-one, while the new translation is in fascicle forty-five.

*The Scripture on the Manifestation of the Tathāgata* (Rúlái xīngxiǎn jīng), four fascicles; also known as *The Scripture on the Manifestation of the Tathāgata’s Illusory Nature* (Xīngxiǎn rúhuàn jīng). Translated by the Western Jin Tripiṭaka Master Dharmarakṣa. This scripture is an alternative translation of portions from the "Jewel King" (*Ratnarāja*) and "Ten Endurances" (*Daśakṣānti*) chapters of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, spanning from the middle of the thirty-fifth fascicle to the end of the thirty-seventh fascicle.
The "Chapter on the Ten Patiences" (Daśakṣānti-parivarta) is located in the thirtieth fascicle.
This [version] lacks the verses; the reason for this discrepancy between the earlier and later versions is unknown.
In the new translation, the "Chapter on the Appearance of the Tathāgata" (Tathāgatotpatti-saṃbhava-parivarta) spans from the fiftieth to the fifty-second fascicles.
The "Chapter on the Ten Patiences" is located in the forty-fourth [fascicle].
Furthermore, the old catalog lists the *Tathāgatagotra-utpatti-sūkṣma-rahasya-garbha-sūtra* in two fascicles;
this is simply an excerpt of the "Chapter on the Arising of Nature" from the old translation, circulated separately.

The text is not different [from the original], except that the initial nidāna of the second assembly has been taken and placed at the beginning of the sūtra, supplemented by the *śraddhā-prasāda* (testimony of faith) sequence.
Since this was not a separate translation, it is not recorded here again.
The four aforementioned scriptures comprise eleven fascicles in one volume.

The *Dushi pin jing* (Sūtra on the Chapter on Transcending the World) consists of six fascicles, or alternatively five fascicles, translated by the Western Jin Tripiṭaka Master Dharmarakṣa. Of these, the aforementioned single scripture is an alternative translation of the "Chapter on Transcending the World" (*Lishi jian pin*) from the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*. The old translation covers fascicles 38 through 44, while the new translation covers fascicles 53 through 59.

*The Rāmāyaṇa Sūtra*, three fascicles, translated by the Śramaṇa Shi Shengjian of the Qifu Qin dynasty. [Recorded in] the *Neidian lu*. This aforementioned sūtra is an alternative translation of the "Entering the Dharma Realm" (*dharmadhātupraveśa*) chapter of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*. Compared to the text of that chapter, this *Rāmāyaṇa Sūtra* lacks portions and is incomplete; it translates only a small part from the beginning of the fifty-first fascicle, "The Householder Anuttaravijaya," to the start of the fifty-third fascicle, "The Night Goddess Viśeṣacintāparitrāṇa-sattvāloka. The text ends there. In the new translation [of the *Avataṃsaka*], this corresponds to the middle of the sixty-seventh fascicle to the beginning of the seventieth fascicle.

*The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Continuation of the Chapter on Entering the Dharma Realm*, one fascicle; alternatively, without the word "Continuation. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śīlabhadra of Central India during the Great Tang Dynasty; recorded in the catalog of the Great Zhou. Regarding this scripture: it is a continuation of the "Chapter on Entering the Dharma Realm" from the original *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*. Alternatively, there are versions of the scripture where it is continued within the main body of the great collection as the fifty-seventh fascicle.

The first three sutras, totaling ten fascicles, are contained in one volume. From the *Dousha* (Śūraṅgama) downward, thirteen sutras are all separate chapters from within the *Mahāvaipulya* [sūtras] that have been translated individually.
The *Nirvāṇa* section and its branch sutras are all compiled here, totaling six sections and fifty-eight fascicles in six volumes.
The *Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra* consists of forty fascicles, or alternatively thirty-six fascicles, in four volumes; [translated during the] Northern Liang dynasty.
The Tripiṭaka Master Dharmakṣema translated the fifth section, the *Ekottara-khaṇḍa*, at Guzang.
Later, during the Yuanjia era of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty, the *Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra* arrived at Jianye.
At that time, the śramaṇa Fànhuìyán of Yuzhou, the śramaṇa Cuì Huìguān of Qīnghé, and the retired scholar Xiè Língyùn of Chénjùn, along with others, [based on] the previous [draft by] Dharmakṣema...
The chapters and sections of this sutra were sparse and concise; therefore, it was supplemented with chapter titles based on the old *Nirvāṇa Sūtra*.

The Tang translation is titled *Zhixian* (Wise and Virtuous).
It is an excerpt from the Āgama Sūtras concerning the events of the Tathāgata’s nirvāṇa and cremation;
it is not the Mahāyāna *Nirvāṇa Sūtra*.
A messenger was sent from afar to India with this [text].
Upon now comparing this scripture with the *Cīvaravastu* (The Chapter on Wandering) at the beginning of the *Dīrgha Āgama*, they share some similarities but are not entirely identical.
