That is to say, there are cases where the same original text has different names,
or where what was extensive has been abbreviated; these are now all deleted as being redundant.
However, because the years have long passed, errors have been transmitted together with the text;
thus, the volumes are needlessly filled, resulting only in wasted effort.
Now, I have carefully collated the variations and distinguished between what is correct and what is erroneous.
These items, fully cataloged, are worthy of observation.

Newly compiled and extracted are sixty-seven distinct sūtras totaling one hundred eighty-five fascicles. Among them is the *Ākāśagarbha-paripṛcchā-sūtra* in eight fascicles—also known as the *Vaipulya-rāja-ākāśagarbha-sūtra*, or simply the *Ākāśagarbha-sūtra*, or in five fascicles. This constitutes one sūtra.
This is a separate excerpt from the *Mahāsannipāta-sūtra*, specifically the chapter on the Bodhisattva Gaganagañja, circulated [independently].
The *Dazhou lu* (Great Zhou Catalogue) states that it was translated by the śramaṇa Śrīghana during the Qifu Qin period; this is an error.
The original manuscript for that translation by the venerable Jian is missing.
*The Sūtra on the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha Asking about the Merit Gained from Upholding This Sūtra*, one fascicle.
The above sūtra is also a separate excerpt copied from the *Ākāśagarbha-parivarta* within the *Mahāsaṃnipāta-sūtra*.
All catalogs state that this was translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin dynasty; this is an error.
[The work] titled *The Sūtra on the Dānapāramitā Practiced by King Sarvada*, in one fascicle—this is the aforementioned sūtra.
This is extracted from the *Ṣaṭpāramitā-samuccaya-sūtra* (Six Perfections Compendium Sutra), within the section on the *Dānapāramitā* (Perfection of Giving).
All catalogs state that it was translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin dynasty, but this is an error.
*The Mahāvaipulya Tathāgatagarbha-sūkṣma-rahasya-nidhāna Sūtra*, two fascicles.

This aforementioned sūtra is a separate excerpt from the "Tathāgatagarbha-samudgama-parivarta" (Chapter on the Arising of the Nature of the Tathāgata) of the old *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, circulated independently.
First, the *Śraddhā-prasāda-anuśaṃsā-nidāna* (Testimony of Faith) was added,
and the introductory narrative (*nidāna*) from the beginning of the second assembly was taken and placed at the head;
thus do the catalogs of the Chángfáng and others all state.
The attribution to an unknown translator of the Western Jin dynasty is erroneous.

One fascicle of the *Suiyuan wangsheng jing* (Sutra on Rebirth According to One’s Vows), also titled the *Guanding suiyuan wangsheng shifang jingtu jing* (Sutra on the Consecration of Rebirth in the Pure Lands of the Ten Directions According to One’s Vows) and also called the *Puguang pusa jing* (Sutra of Bodhisattva Puguang)—the aforementioned single sutra.
This is the eleventh fascicle, the "Chapter on Universal Extensiveness" (Puguang pin), of the *Mahābhiṣeka-sūtra*.
In some versions of the scripture, it appears as the twelfth;
the catalogs of Changfang and others all state this.
It was translated by the Upāsaka Zhi Qian during the Wu dynasty;
some claim it was translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin,
but both assertions are erroneous.
The *Bhaiṣajyaguru-vaiḍūryaprabhā-sūtra*, one fascicle; also titled the *Abhiṣeka-ativipannāpatti-janma-parimocana-sūtra*.
The above sutra is the twelfth volume of the *Mahābhiṣeka-sūtra*.
There is a version of the sūtra located as the eleventh [in some collections].
The catalogs of Sengchang and others all state that it was translated by the śramaṇa Huìjiǎn of Lùnyè Monastery during the Song dynasty; this is an error.

The *Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, Second Assembly, seventy-eight fascicles; commonly titled by the world as the *New Translation of the Larger Version* (*Dapin*) or the *Prabhāsa-prajñāpāramitā*. The *Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, Fourth Assembly, eighteen fascicles; commonly titled by the world as the *New Translation of the Daoxing* or the *Smaller Version* (*Xiaopin*). These two aforementioned sūtras.
At that time, it was commonly rumored among the people that this was a translation by Tripiṭaka Master Yijing;
they altered the title and transcribed it for circulation.
I searched through Jinggong’s catalogue of scriptures and found that this sutra had never been translated separately;
moreover, upon examining its text, it is no different from the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā*.
Fearing that others might not know the full details, I have recorded this here.
The *Prajñāpāramitā-sūtra of the Most Victorious Heavenly King* in eight fascicles, also known as the *New Translation of the Prajñāpāramitā of the Victorious Heavenly King*.
This aforementioned sūtra is identical to the sixth assembly of the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā-sūtra* and the old translation of the *Prajñāpāramitā of the Victorious Heavenly King*.
This is a different translation of the same original text.
The *Mañjuśrī-prajñā Sūtra* in two fascicles—also known as the "New Translation of the Mañjuśrī-prajñā"—is one such scripture;
it corresponds to the "Mañjuśrī Section" of the seventh assembly of the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, which is the older version of the *Mañjuśrī-prajñā*.
A different translation of the same original text.
*Līlāvatī-artha-prajñāpāramitā-sūtra*, one fascicle. The above sutra is the "Chapter on the Līlāvatī-artha" from the tenth assembly of the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā-sūtra*.
*Guhyapada-vajrapāṇi-mahāyakṣasenāpati-sūtra*, two fascicles. The above sutra is as follows.
The *Neidian lu* (Record of Inner Scriptures) states that this was translated by an unknown hand, but this is incorrect.
Upon examining its original source, it is found within the five-fascicle *Miji lishi jing* (Sūtra of the Guhyapada Malla),
beginning from the fifth line of the fourth sheet at the start of the fourth fascicle in five-character verse.
The fifth character of the fifth line in the latter part arises;
continuing until the end of the fifth fascicle, the wording is entirely identical.
This is one fascicle of the *Ekottarika Āgama*, three pages long, the first sutra on the right.
Extracted from the *Ekottarika Āgama*, Volume 21;
two sūtras are excerpted herein.
The first elucidates the four merits of Brahmā.
Next, the four kinds of nutriment are explained;
subsequently, the four kinds of analytical eloquence are explained.
The *Chángfáng lù* states:
The attribution to the Western Jin śramaṇa Dharmakṣema as the translator is erroneous.

The *Xingqixingxiànbào jīng* (Sūtra on the Seven Practices with Immediate Retribution), one fascicle, one sheet, is the first sūtra; it is extracted from the thirty-fourth fascicle of the *Ekottarika Āgama*.
The *Sūtra on the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination*, one fascicle, three pages. The above sūtra is extracted from the forty-sixth fascicle of the *Ekottarika Āgama*.
It was included in the Mahāyāna canon according to the Zhou catalog.

The claim that the *Yun yu Beituo shu xia siwei shi'er yinyuan jing* (Clouds and under the Peepal Tree Contemplating the Sutra on the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination) is a different translation of the same original text is erroneous.
*Jiexiangying fa jing* (Sutra on Dharmas Corresponding to the Precepts), one fascicle. The above is one sutra.
This is from the *Saṃyukta Āgama*, Volume 30.
Changfang’s Catalogue states that it was translated by the Śramaṇa Dharmaruci from the Western Regions during the Eastern Jin; this is an error.
*The Sūtra on the Bhikṣu Asking the Buddha about Many Upāsakas Who Passed Away*, one fascicle.
The above sūtra is also found in the thirtieth fascicle of the *Saṃyuktāgama*.
The Chángfáng Catalogue states:
The attribution of this to the Western Jin śramaṇa Dharmakṣema is erroneous.
The *Ekabhadra-gṛhapati-sūtra*, one fascicle:
the above sūtra is extracted from the forty-sixth fascicle of the *Saṃyuktāgama*.
The *Chángfáng lù* states:
"The attribution to the Tripiṭaka Master An Shigao of the Later Han is erroneous.
There is one scroll titled *Yǒu zhòngshēng sānshì zuò è jīng* (Sūtra on Sentient Beings Committing Evil in the Three Times). This is the aforementioned single sūtra.
This is the eighth fascicle of the *Chūjōyō-kyō* (Udānavarga).
Changfang’s catalogue states that it was translated by the Western Jin śramaṇa Dharmakṣema; this is an error.
*The Sūtra on the Merit of Leaving Home*, one fascicle.
The above sūtra is excerpted from the "Chapter on the Merit of Leaving Home" at the beginning of the *Sūtra of the Wise and the Foolish*.
Changfang’s Catalogue states:
The claim that this was translated by the Upāsaka Zhi Qian of the Wu dynasty is erroneous.
The *Jñānasūtra on Knowing the Good and the Evil* (one fascicle), spoken by the Buddha for a young Brahmin, appears in the fourth fascicle of the *Saṃyuktāgama*.
The *Chángfáng Lù* states that it was translated by the Tripiṭaka Master An Shigao of the Later Han; this is also erroneous. [It was spoken] by the Buddha for Na... [text fragmentary].
*The Sūtra on the Ripening of the Faculties Spoken by the Householder Kula*, one fascicle. Found in the fifth fascicle of the *Saṃyukta Āgama*.
Changfang’s Record states it was translated by the Tripiṭaka Master An Shigao of the Later Han; this is an error.

*The Sūtra on Detachment from Desire Spoken by the Buddha for the Outsider Susīma*, one fascicle. Found in the fourteenth fascicle of the *Saṃyukta Āgama*. Changfang’s Record states it belongs to the Wu period.

The attribution of these to the Upāsaka Zhi Qian is erroneous. The *Sūtra on King Aśoka Giving Half an Āmalaka Fruit*, one fascicle, is extracted from the twenty-fifth fascicle of the *Saṃyukta Āgama*.
The *Sūtra on the Fulfillment of Dhyāna Contemplation*, one fascicle, is extracted from the twenty-ninth fascicle of the *Saṃyukta Āgama*.
According to the *Chángfáng Lù* (Catalogue of Chángfáng), both of these previous attributions to two separate translations are incorrect.
The five scriptures mentioned above were included among the missing texts within the Zhou dynasty catalog.
Now, having examined them, it is found that their original versions all appear within the *Saṃyukta Āgama*.
Since these are separately translated [versions], they are excluded and not recorded here.

*The Sūtra on the Causes and Conditions of the Makara Fish*, one fascicle; from the ninth fascicle. *The Sūtra on the Venerable Udāyin Guiding People to Pay Homage to the Buddha and the Saṃgha*, one fascicle;
from the eleventh fascicle. *The Sūtra on Returning to One’s Native Country to Convert the Father King*, one [fascicle].

One fascicle extracted from the end of the seventeenth fascicle and the beginning of the eighteenth fascicle: *The Sūtra on the Birth of Prince Jālinīprabha*. One fascicle extracted from the nineteenth fascicle:
*The Sūtra on Giving Things that are Lawful or Unlawful*. One fascicle extracted from the twenty-fourth fascicle:
*The Sūtra on the Instruction to Rāhula*. One fascicle extracted from the twenty-fifth fascicle: *The Sūtra on the Wheel of Transmigration through the Five Realms of Existence*.
The *Sūtra on the Causes and Conditions of the Bhikṣu Svāgata* (one fascicle) is extracted from the thirty-fourth fascicle;
the *Sūtra on Meritorious Deeds with and without Objects* (one fascicle) is extracted from the forty-second fascicle;
and the nine sūtras beginning with the *Sūtra on the Causes and Conditions of the Makara Fish* are all extracted from the *Mūlasarvāstivāda-vinaya*.
*The Scripture on the Householder Agnidatta Receiving His Retribution*, one fascicle; from the second and third fascicles.

*The Scripture of the Venerable Sāriputra and the Sound of Harmony*, one fascicle; from the fourth fascicle. *The Scripture on the Five Kinds of Water Strainers*, one fascicle; from the fifth fascicle.
*The Scripture on the Former Causes of Lady Śrīmālā*, one fascicle; from the seventh fascicle. *The Scripture on King Prasenajit’s Faith in the Buddha*, one fascicle.

The *Jūshōjūjuhōkyō* (Sūtra on the Retribution for the Slaughter of the Śākyas), two fascicles, is excerpted from the eighth fascicle. The *Daishishu Bibunin Nyūnehankyō* (Sūtra on the Great Mistress Bhikṣuṇī Entering Nirvāṇa), one fascicle, is excerpted from the eighth and ninth fascicles.

The *Butsu o Nan-da setsu shukke nyūtai kyō* (Sūtra on the Buddha Preaching to Nanda Concerning Leaving Home and Entering the Womb), two fascicles, is included in the fourteenth assembly of the *Ratnakūṭa*, excerpted from the tenth fascicle. [Excerpted] from the eleventh and twelfth [fascicles].

*Jūngǐngfǎshěshēn jīng* (Sutra on Reverently Honoring the Dharma and Sacrificing the Body), one fascicle; excerpted from the beginning of the fourteenth fascicle. *Dù èr xiéjiàn tóngzǐ déguǒ jīng* (Sutra on Two Boys with False Views Attaining the Fruit), one fascicle;
excerpted from the fourteenth fascicle. *Qīngjìng wēiyí jīng* (Sutra on Pure and Austere Deportment), one fascicle;
also called *Xǐjìng wēiyí*; excerpted from the sixteenth fascicle. *Dàmùlián shòubào jīng* (Sutra on Mahāmaudgalyāyana Receiving Retribution), one fascicle; excerpted from the eighteenth fascicle.
*The Sūtra on the Manifestation of Great Auspicious Omens at Birth*, one fascicle; excerpted from the twentieth fascicle. *The Sūtra on the Crossing of Kātyāyana*, one fascicle;
excerpted from the twentieth fascicle. *The Sūtra on the Karmic Retribution and Causes and Conditions of the Nāga King Elāpattra*, one fascicle;
excerpted from the twenty-first fascicle. This *Sūtra of the Nāga King Elāpattra* and the *Sūtra on the Crossing of Kātyāyana* [are related].

Regarding the clarification of similarities and differences in the sutras: the initial text of the former sutra contains four additional pages of introductory narrative (*nidāna*), while the subsequent sections are identical with no distinction;
why then was it needlessly duplicated and transcribed as two separate sutras?

*The Sūtra on the Causes and Conditions of Lady Anle*, one fascicle; from the twenty-first fascicle. *The Sūtra on the Causes and Conditions of Saṃpāka*, three fascicles; from the twenty-second, twenty-third, and twenty-fourth fascicles.

*The Sūtra on the Causes and Conditions of Prabhāsa*, one fascicle; from the twenty-fifth fascicle. *The Sūtra on Subduing Non-Buddhists by Manifesting Great Supernatural Powers*, one fascicle; from the [twenty-sixth] fascicle.

The *Mahābhaiṣajya-kuśala-upāya-sūtra* in twenty-six fascicles (two fascicles extracted from the twenty-seventh and twenty-eighth); the *Buddha-descent-from-heaven-to-Jambudvīpa-sūtra* in one fascicle (extracted from the twenty-ninth);
the *Sundarī-nandā-parivarta-sūtra* in one fascicle (extracted from the thirtieth); the *Hārītī-mātṛ-nidāna-sūtra* in one fascicle (extracted from the thirty-first);
the *Dharmadinnā-bhikṣuṇī-gṛhastha-phala-prāpti-sūtra* in one fascicle (extracted from the thirtieth); and the *Drumila-brāhmaṇa-māna-sūtra* in one [fascicle].

The *Disciple Serves the Teacher Sūtra*, one fascicle, appears at the end of the thirty-fourth fascicle and the beginning of the thirty-fifth fascicle. The *Sūtra on the Seven Kinds of Non-retrogression*, one fascicle, appears in the thirty-fifth fascicle.

The *Sūtra on Heedlessness Spoken by the Buddha for an Elder*, one fascicle, appears in the thirty-sixth fascicle. The *Sūtra on the Causes and Conditions of Earthquakes*, one fascicle, appears in the thirty-sixth fascicle.
The *Sūtra on the Four Seals of Black and White Dharmas*, one fascicle, appears in the thirty-seventh fascicle. The *Sūtra on the Buddha’s Impending Entry into Nirvāṇa*.

*The Sūtra on Delivering the Virtuous and Wise*, two fascicles: it appears from the latter half of the thirty-seventh fascicle to the former half of the thirty-eighth fascicle. *The Sūtra on the Minister Cāruvṛṣṭi’s Address to the King after the Buddha’s Parinirvāṇa*, one fascicle:

it appears from the end of the thirty-eighth fascicle to the beginning of the thirty-ninth fascicle. The textual content of these two aforementioned sūtras is intermingled; compared to the latter sūtra, the preceding portion of the *Sūtra on the Minister’s Address to the King* contains approximately two additional pages. *The Sūtra on the Division of the Relics by the Eight Great Kings*, one fascicle:

it appears from the end of the thirty-eighth fascicle to the beginning of the thirty-ninth fascicle. The textual content of these two aforementioned sūtras is intermingled; compared to the latter sūtra, the preceding portion of the *Sūtra on the Minister’s Address to the King* contains approximately two additional pages. As for the *Sūtra on the Division of the Relics*:

Comparing this sutra with the preceding one, the latter text contains approximately three additional pages, yet there are no differences whatsoever in the commentaries; thus, these two sutras are redundant and inappropriate.
The thirty-three sutras following the "Householder Agnidatta" section are as follows:
These are all extracted from the *Mūlasarvāstivāda-vinaya-ksudraka-vastu*,
beginning from the *Makara-sūtra* (The Discourse on the Crocodile) down to forty-two discourses, comprising forty-nine fascicles.
These are all narratives concerning the origins (*nidāna*) found within the Vinaya of the Sarvāstivāda school,
excerpted and circulated by the Tripiṭaka Master Yi Jing.
Since they constitute a separate category of birth [stories], they have all been deleted.
Among these, the *Sūtra on Giving Things Lawfully or Illegally* and the *Sūtra on the Disciple Serving the Teacher*,
though slightly expanded or abbreviated compared to the extensive versions, do not differ in meaning from the originals.
How could one laboriously divide these into separate sections and fascicles?
Likewise, various separately produced [versions] have all been deleted.

A new compendium has extracted those with different titles but identical texts; twenty such works comprise fifty-two fascicles. Among them is the *Bodhisattvaviṣayāvatāra-vikrīḍita-dharmaparyāya-sūtra* (Ten Fascicles), translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci of the Northern Wei dynasty. This is recorded in the *Baochang lu*. Of the above, there is one such scripture.
This is an alternative title for the *Satyaka-nirgrantha-sūtra*,
which is recorded separately in the Zhou Catalogue.
Furthermore, the claim that it is a missing text is an error.

*New Sūtra of the Practice of the Way*, seven fascicles or ten fascicles; translated by the Tripitaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin. [Recorded in] the catalogues of Sengchang and others. Regarding this one sūtra:
upon examining various versions in the canon, those that are entirely identical in wording and phrasing to the *Prajñāpāramitā-hrdaya-sūtra* (Small Version) are erroneous texts.

When the *New Version of the Practice of the Way Sūtra* translated by Master Hu was being produced, the original manuscript was not available. It was heard that a copy of Hu’s translation existed in the eastern capital, but despite searching for it, it could not be found.
The eight-fascicle *Mahāvaipulya Mahāsannipāta Sūtra*—the aforementioned sūtra.
It is recorded in both the *Táng nèidiǎn lù* and the *Dàzhōu lù*.
Upon examining the text now, it is found to be the sixth fascicle of the *Hebù dàjí jīng*.
The first two scrolls are titled "Chapter on the Bodhisattvas of the Ten Directions."
This is precisely the *Pratyutpanna-buddha-saṃmukhāvasthita-samādhi-sūtra* (The Sūtra on the Fifty Contemplations of the Perfection of Wisdom).
The subsequent six fascicles are the *Akṣayamati-nirdeśa-sūtra*.
As for why the *Pratyutpanna-buddha-saṃmukhāvasthita-samādhi-sūtra* was included within the *Mahāsaṃnipāta-sūtra*, its reason is unknown.
Those that exist as separate sections due to differences in their textual variations have already been recorded here; therefore, they are now deleted.
*Anavatapta-nāgarāja-sūtra*, two fascicles. The above constitutes one scripture.
It is identical in every word and phrase to the *Hongdao guangxian sanmei jing* (Sūtra on the Samādhi of Propagating the Way and Manifesting Broadly),
differing only in its title;
one copy is preserved here.
*He Dao Shenzu Jing* (Sutra on the Divine Footsteps in Accordance with the Way), three fascicles;
this aforementioned sutra has the same title but different text from the *Daoshenzu Wujing Bianhua Jing*.
*Aiqi Jing* (Sutra of Lamentation and Weeping), three fascicles, or alternatively two fascicles, in six chapters; this aforementioned sutra.
This shares the same name as the *Vaipulya-parinirvāṇa-sūtra*, though the wording differs;
since the first chapter of that *Vaipulya-nirvāṇa* is titled "Lamentation" (*Aiqi*),
this title was adopted from that chapter to serve as the title of the present scripture.
Compared to the Vaipulya Nirvāṇa [Sūtras], this latter work lacks three chapters and is thus incomplete.
*Bao Tian Hui Yin San Mei Jing* (The Sūtra on the Treasure Field and the Seal of Wisdom Samādhi), one fascicle. The above is one sūtra.
The *Huiyin sanmei jing* (Sūtra on the Samādhi of the Seal of Wisdom) is identical in its textual phrases to [the *Baojian sanmei jing*], differing only in length and detail.
The *Changfang lu* states:
"The *Huiyin sanmei jing* is also titled the *Baotian huiyin sanmei jing*."
Both versions of the *Zhou ruzang lu* (Record of Works Included in the Canon during the Zhou Dynasty) include these two texts;
it is a grave error to confuse one for the other.
*Lüzijing* (The Scripture of Mṛgāra), one fascicle. The above is one scripture.
The title of this text differs from that of the *Mṛgī-sūtra* (鹿母經).
Based on its textual meaning, it is appropriate to establish the title according to the mother.
Changfang’s Record (*Changfang lu*) states:
The attribution of the *Mṛgāraputra-sūtra* to the Wu dynasty layman Zhi Qian is erroneous.
The *Laghu-amitāyus-sūtra*, one fascicle:
the aforementioned sūtra shares the same title as the *Amitābha-sūtra*, though the texts differ.
The *Sūtra of the Lesser Immeasurable Life* translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Guṇabhadra of the Song dynasty was at that time without its original manuscript.
One fascicle of the *Womb Treasury Sūtra* appears in the *Chángfáng Lù*. To the right, this sūtra shares the same title as the *Sūtra of the Stainless Virtuous Woman*, though their texts differ.
*The Sūtra on Hearing the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination in the City*, one fascicle.
The above-mentioned sūtra has the same title as the *Sūtra on Contemplating the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination Under the Peepal Tree*, though the texts differ.
This *Wencheng jing* (Sūtra on Hearing the City) exists in several variant editions, which have yet to be located.

The *Dà ān bān jīng* (Sūtra on Great Ānāpāna), in one or two fascicles—the *Neidian lu* states it is in two fascicles while the *Chángfáng lu* states it is in one fascicle—shares the exact same title as the *Dà ān bān shǒuyì jīng* (Sūtra on Great Ānāpāna and Mindfulness); however, they differ in their length and detail.
It is a grave error to claim that two versions of this text exist among the various catalogs.
One scroll of the *Shenri jing* (Sūtra of the Day of Repentance):
the aforementioned sūtra has the same title as the *Candraprabha-kumāra-bodhisattva-sūtra* found within the Mahāyāna Piṭaka, though the texts differ.
The father’s name was Shenri (申日),
and the son’s title was Yueguang (月光);
based on these differences, the distinct titles of the sutras were established.
The *Chángfáng lù* states:
"The claim that the *Shēnrì jīng* was translated by the Wu-dynasty upāsaka Zhi Qián is an error.
*Luánzhuǎn wǔdào zuífú bàoyìng jīng*, one fascicle. The above scripture is identical in title and wording to the *Zuífú bàoyìng jīng*, differing only in its length.
*Jiàntuōyuè jīng* (The Sūtra of Cāṇḍava), one fascicle.
This sūtra is identical in title and wording to the *Jiàntuōyuè guówáng jīng* (The Sūtra of King Cāṇḍava), differing only in its length;
it was included in the canon during the Zhou dynasty and is cataloged as a single-volume work.
The *Cāṇḍālayavana-rāja-sūtra* is included among the retranslations;
its appearance in two locations is a grave error.

The *Zhenwei shashamen jing* (Sūtra on Authentic and Spurious Śramaṇas), one fascicle—also titled the *Mahābhikṣu-sūtra* or the *Kāśyapa-śīla-sūtra* according to the Chángfáng record—constitutes the aforementioned single sūtra.
This is an alternative title for the *Kāśyapa-śīla-sūtra*, with the wording being identical throughout.
Some claim it was translated by the śramaṇa Huìjiǎn of Lùnyè Monastery during the Song dynasty, but this is an error.
The *Dharmacakra-pravartana-sūtra*, one fascicle. Regarding the above-mentioned scripture, it was previously noted that its original text could not be found;

however, it was an error for all the scriptural collections to have substituted the *Dharmacakra-pravartana-śāstra* for it. Recently, the authentic manuscript was located in the Eastern Capital (Luoyang) and has now been included in the canon.

*The Scripture on Piṇḍola Preaching the Dharma for the King*, one fascicle. The above one fascicle and *The Scripture on Piṇḍola-bharadvāja Preaching the Dharma for King Udayana* are identical in their wording and names; they differ only in their length.
*Āraṇyaka-cīnadharmaparyāya-sūtra*, two fascicles. The above sutra shares the same title as the *Zuochan sanmei jing* (Sutra on the Samādhi of Seated Meditation) but differs in its text.
*Chanyao yaojue jing* (Sutra on the Essential Secrets of Dhyāna), five fascicles. The above is one sutra.
It is stated that this was translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmamitra of the Song Dynasty,
and that it is a different version derived from the same source as the *Dhyānaguhya-vidhi* translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin Dynasty.
Now, upon examining the preceding and following contexts, they are extremely disordered and are not the original scripture.
The first fascicle is actually the *Treatise on the Secret Essential Methods for Curing the Illnesses of Dhyāna*;
furthermore, it does not reach its conclusion, but stops halfway through.
From the second fascicle onward is the *Dhyāna-guhyaka-dharma* translated by Kumārajīva,
spanning from the point halfway through the first fascicle up to the end of the third fascicle.
The text was also incomplete, lacking some ten or more sheets;
these were combined into four fascicles, which together with the preceding portion formed five.
As for that translated by Dharmamitra:
At that time, the original texts were missing.

Newly cataloged and extracted from the *Chóngshàng lù jīng* (Record of Repeatedly Submitted Scriptures), there are eight sections totaling thirty fascicles: the *Bodhisattvabhūmiviniścayasaṃgrahaṇī-sūtra* in ten fascicles (or eight), also known as the *Bodhisattva-śīla-sūtra* or the *Bodhisattvabhūmi-sūtra*. This constitutes one scripture.
It is also titled the *Bodhisattvabhūmiviniścayasaṃgrahaṇī-śāstra*.
In this present catalog, it is classified as Vinaya;
its sūtra title is retained while its designation as a śāstra is removed from the records.
The *Zhou lu* states that it is an error to say the *Bodhisattvabhūmi-śīla-sūtra* is missing;
furthermore, within the *Zhou lu*, this single scripture has many titles.

There are six instances in total where the preceding and succeeding sections are inconsistent; these are cases where the text was severely displaced or misplaced: one instance in the Mahāyāna Sūtras, two instances in the Mahāyāna Vinaya, one instance in the Mahāyāna Śāstras, and two instances in the original catalogs.
These titles appear repeatedly in other sūtras more than once;
fearing that it would clutter the pages and ink, I have described them here only briefly.

One fascicle of the *Bhadradevī-sūtra*; now included [in this collection] are one fascicle of the *Ratnakūṭa-paramārtha-dharmavijaya-sūtra* and one fascicle of the *Maitreyabodhisattvapraśna-pūrvapraṇidhāna-sūtra*. These three sūtras are as follows.
It is an error for both the single-text edition and the retranslation to be recorded together in the *Dazhou Ruzang Lu*.
Now, the single-text edition has been removed and included among the retranslations.
The *Bodhicittotpāda Sūtra* in two fascicles, also titled the *Bodhicittotpāda Śāstra*: this is one sūtra.
It was an error for [the titles] to appear in both the Mahāyāna Sūtras and the Mahāyāna Śāstras within the Zhou-period Catalogue of the Canon.
Now, following the works composed by Bodhisattvas, I have removed their names from the sūtra section and preserved them only in the śāstra catalogue.

*The Scripture on Admonishing the King*, one fascicle; also titled *The Greater and Lesser Scriptures on Admonishing the King*. The above scripture was included in the Zhou-period canon, though it is missing from the original;
its appearance in both catalogs is an error. *The Dharmapada*, two fascicles; also called *The Collection of Dharmapada Verses*. The above scripture—
It is an error for both [the *Zhōu rù zàng lù* and the *Dàchéng chóngyì jíchuán nèi*] to record [this text] in two separate places;
upon examining the text, they are identical and cannot be divided into two.
Although there was once a second translation, it is now missing.
Now, this scripture has been excluded from inclusion within the *Ji* (Collection).
Regarding the twelve-fascicle *Śrīmālādevī-siṃhanāda-sūtra-śāstra*,

both versions were preserved in the *Zhongjing lu* (Catalogue of All Scriptures) compiled during the Kaihuang and Renshou eras of the Sui dynasty, as well as in the *Neidian lu* (Inner Canon Catalogue) and the *Dazhou lu* (Dazhou Catalogue) of the Tang dynasty.

It is an error to claim that the *Yun* (Cloud) [Commentary] is a different translation of the same original as the fifteen-fascicle *She lun* (Mahāyānasaṃparigraha-śāstra), both translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha of the Chen dynasty.
Upon examining the text, the sentences from beginning to end are entirely identical.
Although the number of fascicles differs, they cannot be divided into two separate sections; therefore,
only the fifteen-fascicle version shall be preserved,
while those consisting of twelve fascicles are excluded.

Newly compiled and incorporated into the Great Collection of Sūtras: fifty-two works in one hundred and forty-one fascicles. The *Suvarṇaprabhāsa-sūtra* (Golden Light Sūtra), four fascicles and eighteen chapters, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmakṣema of the Northern Liang dynasty. The *Suvarṇaprabhāsa-sūtra*, seven fascicles and twenty-two chapters—or six fascicles—translated in its entirety by the Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha of the Chen dynasty; these four chapters combined constitute seven fascicles. it is the forty-first assembly. The *Mahāratnakūṭa-sūtra* (one fascicle), of lost translation, was renamed the "Assembly of Maitreya’s Inquiry into the Eight Dharmas" in the forty-third assembly.

Translated by the Liang Dynasty Tripiṭaka Master Mandarasa; alternatively, it exists in two fascicles within the fourth sixth assembly of the Prajñā section, where it appears as a duplicate of another edition.

Since it cannot be excluded from its current position, its title is retained here. *The Sūtra on the Questions of Ratnaśikhin Bodhisattva*, in two fascicles, also titled *The Sūtra on the Pure Conduct of Bodhisattvas*, translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin Dynasty;
it is located in the forty-seventh assembly. Together with the preceding *Sūtra of the Secret-Keeper Malla*, these comprise twenty-three works totaling eighty-one fascicles.
These are all ancient translations of various assemblies from the *Mahāratnakūṭa-sūtra*.
The Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci compared them with the Sanskrit original and found them to be identical;
thus, he did not retranslate them, but simply compiled them according to their proper sequence.
Those that should be incorporated into the main body [of the canon] but are listed separately shall be deleted.
The *Tri-saṃvara-sūtra* in three fascicles is identical in text to the old *Mahāvaipulya Tri-śīla-sūtra*; it belongs to the first assembly.
The *Ananta-vyūha-sūtra* in four fascicles belongs to the second assembly. The *Amitāyus-tathāgata-sūtra* in two fascicles is [identical to the old version].
The *Old Mahā-amitābha Sūtra* and others are identical to the fifth assembly;

the two-fascicle *Sūtra of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya* is identical to the *Old Sūtra of the Land of Akṣobhya Buddha* in the sixth assembly; the five-fascicle *Sūtra of the Array of Armor* is in the seventh assembly;
and the one-fascicle *Sūtra of Mañjuśrī’s Universal Gate* is identical to the old *Universal Gate Chapter*.
The *Prabhāsa-sūtra* in five fascicles was originally in the tenth assembly;
the *Garbhāvakrānti-sūtra* in one fascicle, which is the same text as the old *Po-t'ai ching*, was spoken by the Buddha for Ānanda in the eleventh assembly;
the *Akṣayavyūha-kośa-sūtra* in two fascicles was in the thirteenth assembly; and the *Phenapa-bhadra-vidyādhara-vyākaraṇa-sūtra* in one fascicle was in the twentieth assembly.
The scroll is identical in text to the old *Rṣi-bandhudatta-sūtra* and constitutes the twenty-first assembly;

the two-scroll *Mahā-prātihārya-sūtra* is the twenty-second assembly; the one-scroll *Upāli-paripṛcchā-sūtra* is identical in text to the old *Vinaya-viniścaya-sūtra* and constitutes the twenty-fourth assembly;
the two-scroll *Adhyāśaya-saṃcodana-sūtra* is identical in text to the old *Saṃcodana-sūtra*.
The *Juejingxin jing* (Sūtra on the Awakening of the Pure Mind) is the same text as that found in the twenty-fifth assembly;

the *Shunshun pusa jing* (Sūtra of the Bodhisattva Shunshun), one fascicle, is in the twenty-seventh assembly; the *Qinshou changzhe jing* (Sūtra of the Elder Qinshou), one fascicle, is in the twenty-eighth assembly;
and the *Wodayan wang jing* (Sūtra of King Udayana), one fascicle, which is the same text as the old *Youqian wang jing*, is in the twenty-ninth assembly. The *Miao...* [text fragment].
The *Sūtra of the Wise Girl* (Hui tongnü jīng), one fascicle, is the same text as the old *Sūtra of Sumati*.

The *Sūtra of the Upāsikā on the Ganges* (Hénggēshàng yōubóyī jīng), one fascicle, is from the thirty-first assembly. The *Sūtra of the Bodhisattva Puṣpakūṭarāja* (Gōngdé bǎohuāfū púsà jīng), one fascicle, is from the thirty-fourth assembly.
The *Sūtra of the Devaputra Sudhana* (Shàn dé tiānzǐ jīng), one fascicle, is the same as the old version.
The *Sūtra on the Especially Inconceivable Realm* is the same text as [the sūtra] in the thirty-fifth assembly;
the *Sūtra of King Ajātaśatru’s Prince* in one fascicle is the same text as the old *Sūtra of the Prince Śuddharakṣita* and others in the thirty-seventh assembly;
the *Sūtra of the Girl Viśvāsā* in one fascicle is in the fortieth assembly; and the *Sūtra Asked by Maitreya Bodhisattva*... [in one fascicle].
The *Scroll* is the same text as the old *Sūtra on the Original Vows of Maitreya*, belonging to the forty-second assembly;
the *Sūtra of the Bodhisattva Akṣayamati* in one scroll belongs to the forty-fifth assembly;
the *Sūtra of Queen Śrīmālā* in one scroll is the same text as the old *Śrīmālā-sūtra*, belonging to the forty-eighth assembly; and the *Sūtra of the Questions of the Rishi Viśāla* in one scroll.
It shares the same original text as the *Purāṇa Viṣṇu-praśna-sūtra* and is located in the forty-ninth assembly, following the three Vinaya-sūtras on the right;
together they comprise twenty-six sections in a total of forty-four fascicles.
Translated in the second year of the Xiāntián era of the Great Táng dynasty by the Tripiṭaka Master and Śramaṇa Bodhiruci (translated into Chinese as Jué’ài) at Xīchóngfú Temple in South India;
these are all the various assemblies of the Ratnakūṭa compiled within the Mahāvaipulya section of the canon.

Fearing that their origins might remain unknown, I have set them out in detail:
if the new and old versions are combined, they constitute one hundred and twenty fascicles; if they are divided separately, they constitute one hundred and twenty-five fascicles.
