*The Bhikṣuṇī Prātimokṣa Sūtra* of the Mahīśāsaka school, one fascicle (also titled *The Niśraya Prātimokṣa Sūtra of the Mahīśāsaka*), twenty-nine sheets;
*The Bhikṣu Prātimokṣa Sūtra* of the Dharmaguptaka school, one fascicle, compiled by the śramaṇa Huaisu according to the Vinaya, titled "Dharmaguptaka."

The *Prātimokṣa-sūtra*, twenty-four sheets; the *Dharmaguptaka Bhikṣuṇī-prātimokṣa-sūtra*, one fascicle, compiled by the śramaṇa Huaisu according to the Vinaya, titled *Dharmaguptaka Bhikṣuṇī-prātimokṣa-sūtra*, thirty sheets;

the *Dharmaguptaka Bhikṣu-prātimokṣa-sūtra*, one fascicle—sometimes omitting the word "Bhikṣu" or titled *Mahīśāsaka-prātimokṣa-sūtra*—translated by Buddhayaśas during the Yao Qin dynasty, twenty-three [sheets].
*Ji Jietuo Jieben* (Paper Sūtra on the Code of Liberation), one fascicle; from the Kāśyapīya school, twenty-two pages.

*Sami Shijie Fa Bing Wei yi* (The Dharma of the Ten Precepts for Śrāmaṇeras and Their Deportment), also titled *Śrāmaṇera Wei yi Jieben*, one fascicle; twenty-one pages. *Sami Wei yi* (Deportment of Śrāmaṇeras), one fascicle;
alternatively titled *Śrāmaṇera Wei yi Jing*, nine pages. *Sami Ni Li Jie Wen* (Text on the Separation of Precepts for Śrāmaṇerīs), one [fascicle].
Scroll Four: *The Śrāmaṇerikā-śīla-sūtra*, one scroll (or five sheets, as the word "sūtra" may be omitted);
*The Śāriputra-paripṛcchā-sūtra*, one scroll (eleven sheets). These ten sūtras above comprise ten scrolls in a single fascicle.
*The Hundred and One Karmavācanās of the Mūlasarvāstivāda*, ten fascicles, one volume, one hundred and forty-six pages.
*The Hundred and One Karmavācanās of the Great Śramaṇa*, one fascicle; excerpted from the *Sarvāstivāda-vinaya*, also known as *The Karmavācanās of the Great Śramaṇa*, twenty-two pages.
*The Essential Karmavācanās for Bhikṣus according to the Sarvāstivāda*, one fascicle; excerpted from the *Sarvāstivāda-vinaya*.
The *Vinaya* (or *Viniya*) Essential *Karmavācanā* Dharma, either in two fascicles or one fascicle of twenty-four sheets according to Sengyou’s Catalogue;
the *Upāli Questions the Buddha Sūtra*, one fascicle, also called the *Upāli Vinaya*, twenty-three sheets;
the *Five-Part Karmavācanā*, one fascicle, titled the *Mūlasarvāstivāda Karmavācanā*, thirty-one sheets, being one part.

*Zajiemo* (Miscellaneous Karmavācanā), four fascicles; titled *Tánwúdé Lǜbù Zájiemo* (The Miscellaneous Karmavācanā of the Dharmaguptaka Vinaya School). It begins with the ritual for establishing the boundary for the precept platform (*sīmābandha*) and consists of thirty-four pages.
*Tánwúdé Jiemo* (Dharmaguptaka Karmavācanā), one fascicle; titled *Jiemo Yījuàn Chū Tánwúdé Lǜ* (One Fascicle of Karmavācanā from the Dharmaguptaka Vinaya).
It begins with the ritual for the full ordination (*upasampadā*) and consists of thirty-seven pages. *Sìfēn Bǐqūní Jiemo* (Dharmaguptaka Bhikṣuṇī Karmavācanā).

*Fǎ* (Dharma), one fascicle. Yuo says it is the *Tánwúdé Jīmó* (Karmavācanā of the Mahīśāsaka) or the *Zá Jīmó* (Miscellaneous Karmavācanā), consisting of fifteen sheets. The seven scriptures above, totaling seven fascicles, share the same volume. *Sìfēn lǜ shānbǔ suíjī jīmó* (The *Suiji Karmavācanā* Compiled from the *Dharmaguptaka-vinaya*), one fascicle.

The title of the preface reads: *Tánwúdé bù sìfēn lǜ shānbǔ suíjī jīmó*, forty-seven sheets. *Sìfēn sēng jīmó* (The *Karmavācanā for Monks* of the *Dharmaguptaka-vinaya*), three fascicles. The title reads: *Jīmó juàn shàng*, extracted from the *Sìfēn lǜ*, eighty sheets. *Sìfēn nǐ jīmó* (The *Karmavācanā for Nuns* of the *Dharmaguptaka-vinaya*), three fascicles. The title reads: *Nǐ jīmó juàn shàng*, extracted from the *Sìfēn lǜ*, seventy sheets. The three scriptures above, totaling seven fascicles, share the same volume.
*Mahāprajāpatī Bhikṣuṇī Sūtra*, two fascicles—also called *Mahāprajāpatī Ordination Sūtra* or simply *Mahāprajāpatī Sūtra*—thirty-one sheets.
*Kāśyapa Vinaya Prohibitions Sūtra*, one fascicle—also known as *Mahābhikṣu Sūtra* or *Sūtra on Being a True Śramaṇa*—three sheets.
*Sūtra on the Lightness and Heaviness of Retribution for Violating the Precepts*, one fascicle.
The *Maudgalyāyana-paripṛcchā-vinaya-sūtra* (also known as the *Zuibo jing* or *Maudgalyāyana-asked Sūtra*), two sheets;
the *Śīla-kṣaya-tsaṃvartanīya-sūtra* (also known as the *Śīla-kṣaya-paṭutara-tsaṃvartanīya-sūtra*), four sheets;
the *Upāsaka-pañcaśīla-lakṣaṇa-sūtra*, one fascicle (also known as the *Upāsaka-pañcaśīla-saṃkṣepa-śāstra*), fourteen sheets; and the *Mūlasarvāstivāda-...*.
The *Vinayakārikā* of the Mūlasarvāstivāda, five fascicles (or three fascicles), seventy-one sheets;
the *Mūlasarvāstivāda-vinaya-kṣudraka-vastu-saṃgraha-gāthā*, one fascicle, six sheets;
the *Mūlasarvāstivāda-vinaya-nidāna-mātṛkā-saṃgraha-gāthā*, one fascicle. The *Nidāna-gāthā* precedes the *Mātṛkā*.
The *Daka-gāthā* (Verses of Daka) consists of eight sheets; the *Five Hundred Questions on Matters Sūtra* (*Wubai wenshi jing*) consists of thirty-three sheets.
These nine sūtras comprise fourteen fascicles in one volume.

The *Mūlasarvāstivāda-vinaya-saṃgraha* (Fundamental Sarvāstivāda Vinaya Compendium) in twenty fascicles, or fourteen fascicles, in two bundles, totaling 277 sheets. The *Vinayamātṛkā* (Matrka of the Vinaya) in ten fascicles; its first fascicle states it is the *Sarvāstivāda-vinayamātṛkā*, in one bundle, totaling 188 sheets. The *Naiyāya-vinaya* (Naiyāya Vinaya) in ten fascicles—also known as the *Śīlahetupratyaya-sūtra* (Sutra on the Causes and Conditions of Precepts), or the *Śīlaphalahetupratyaya-sūtra* (Sutra on the Causes and Conditions of the Fruit of Precepts), or simply the *Naiyāya-sūtra*—in one bundle, totaling 155 sheets. The *Samantapāsādikā-vibhāṣā* (Vibhāṣā on the Samantapāsādikā Vinaya) in eighteen fascicles—also called the *Vibhāṣā-vinaya* or simply the *Samantapāsādikā-vinaya*—totaling 358 sheets. The *Buddha-abhidharma-sūtra* in two fascicles—also called the *Buddha-abhidharma-śāstra*—totaling 45 sheets. The above two scriptures comprise twenty fascicles in two bundles.

The *Vinayamātṛkā-sūtra* in eight fascicles, also called the *Vinayamātṛkā-śāstra*, consists of one hundred and fifty-six sheets; the *Mahābhikṣu-trisahasra-vaipulya-vidhi-sūtra* in two fascicles, also called the *Mahāsāṃghika-vaipulya-vidhi-sūtra* or the four-fascicle version, consists of forty-two sheets. These two aforementioned scriptures, totaling ten fascicles, are contained in the same volume.

The *Sarvāstivādavinayavibhāṣā* in nine fascicles, totaling one hundred eighty-seven sheets; the *Vinayaviniścaya-upāliparipṛcchā-śāstra* (also simply called the *Viniścayasaṃgrahaṇī*) in one fascicle, twenty-four sheets; these two aforementioned scriptures, totaling ten fascicles, are bound in the same volume.
The Śrāvaka-vehicle treatises consist of thirty-six works totaling six hundred and ninety-eight fascicles, arranged in seventy-two bundles (*zhì*). These include:

the *Abhidharma-aṣṭagrantha-śāstra* (Treatise on the Eight Chapters of Abhidharma) in thirty fascicles and three bundles; alternatively titled *Wulun* (Treatise on Non-existence), or *Kātyāyanīya-abhidharma*, or simply *Abhidharma*.

The *Abhidharma-śāstra* (A-pi-tan jing), eight *granthas* (sections) or twenty fascicles, four hundred and sixty-two sheets; composed by Kātyāyanīputra, the *Abhidharma-jñānaprasthāna-śāstra* (A-pi-da-mo fa-zhi lun), twenty fascicles in two bundles, three hundred and fifty-eight sheets;
composed by Mahāmaudgalyāyana, the *Abhidharma-dharmaskandha-pāda-śāstra* (A-pi-da-mo fa-yun zu lun), twelve fascicles in one bundle, one hundred and eighty-nine sheets;

composed by Śāriputra, the *Abhidharma-saṃgītiparyāya-pāda-śāstra* (A-pi-da-mo ji-yi-men zu lun), twenty fascicles in two bundles, two hundred and seventy-eight sheets. The *Abhidharma-prakaraṇapāda-śāstra* (A-pi-da-mo zang-xiang zu lun), twenty fascicles in two bundles... [text continues].
The *Vibhaṅga-vijñānakāya-pāda-śāstra* in sixteen fascicles, totaling two hundred and sixty-five sheets; and the *Abhidharma-dhātu-kāya-pāda-śāstra* in three fascicles, totaling thirty-nine sheets.
These two treatises comprise nineteen fascicles in two bundles.

The *Abhidharma-prakaraṇapāda-śāstra* in eighteen fascicles, totaling two hundred and fifty-five sheets; and the *Saṃgītiparyāya-abhidharma-śāstra* (or *Asaṃskṛta-varga*) in twelve fascicles, totaling two hundred and eight sheets. These two treatises comprise thirty fascicles in three bundles.

The *Abhidharma-vibhāṣā-śāstra* consists of sixty fascicles—or, including the title "Eight *Khandas*," eighty-four fascicles—arranged in six bundles and totaling 1,269 sheets. The *Abhidharma-mahāvibhāṣā-śāstra* consists of two hundred fascicles; it is also called the *Abhidharma-jñānaprasthāna-mahāvibhāṣā*, arranged in twenty bundles and totaling 3,169 sheets. The *Abhidharma-kośa-bhāṣya* consists of twenty-two fascicles—or, omitting the character "Bhāṣya," four hundred seventy-one sheets. The *Abhidharma-kośa-kārikā* consists of one fascicle—or three fascicles—and twenty-three sheets. The aforementioned two treatises comprise twenty-three fascicles arranged in three bundles: the first bundle contains seven fascicles, while the middle and lower bundles each contain eight fascicles.

The *Abhidharmakośa-bhāṣya* in thirty fascicles, three bundles, totaling four hundred and sixty-five sheets; the *Abhidharma-nyāyānusāra-śāstra* in eighty fascicles, eight bundles, totaling one thousand three hundred and ninety-four sheets; the *Abhidharma-prakaraṇapāda-śāstra* (or *Abhidharma-samaya-pradīpikā*) in forty fascicles, four bundles, totaling six hundred and fourteen sheets; the *Abhidharma-hṛdaya-śāstra* in four fascicles—sometimes omitting the character "lun" (treatise)—totaling sixty-nine sheets; the *Dharmatrāta-abhidharma-hṛdaya-sūtra* in six fascicles—sometimes omitting the character "jing" (sūtra), sometimes omitting the name "Dharmatrāta," sometimes in seven fascicles, sometimes titled *Dharmatrāta-abhidharma-śāstra*, or with the characters "translated by another" added—totaling one hundred and five sheets. The aforementioned two treatises [the *Abhidharma-hṛdaya* and its commentary] comprise ten fascicles in a single bundle.

The *Saṃyuktābhidharmahṛdaya-śāstra* in eleven fascicles—sometimes omitting the character "lun" (treatise), sometimes called the *Saṃyuktābhidharma-sūtra*, and also the *Saṃyuktābhidharma-vibhāṣā*—consists of fourteen fascicles and two hundred and seventy-nine sheets. The *Abhidharmāmṛta-rasa-śāstra* in two fascicles—also called the *Amṛtarasa-abhidharma* or omitting the character "lun"—consists of forty-six sheets. The *Lakṣaṇānusāra-śāstra* in one fascicle—also called the *Guṇamati-lakṣaṇānusāra-śāstra*—consists of thirty-four sheets. These three treatises comprise fourteen fascicles in two volumes.

The *Ācārya Vasumitra Bodhisattva-saṃgīti-śāstra* (尊婆須蜜菩薩所集論) in ten fascicles, or twelve fascicles, or fourteen fascicles; also called the *Vasumitra Sūtra*, comprising two hundred and sixty-two sheets. The *Tridharmaka-śāstra* (三法度論) in two fascicles—sometimes the character "lun" (論) is omitted, or it is called a "sūtra"—or in one fascicle, or three fascicles, comprising forty-nine sheets. The *Abhidharma-avatāra-śāstra* (入阿毘達磨論) in two fascicles, comprising twenty-eight sheets. The above three treatises comprise fourteen fascicles in two bundles.

The *Tattvasiddhi-śāstra* (Chengshi lun) consists of twenty fascicles and comprises two hundred and two chapters; it is also found in versions of twenty-four, twenty-seven, fourteen, or sixteen fascicles. It is arranged in two bundles and contains three hundred and ninety-eight sheets. The *Lokasthāna-abhidharma-śāstra* (Lishi apitan lun) consists of ten fascicles and is contained in one bundle. It is sometimes without the character "lun" (treatise), is also titled *Tiandi ji* (Record of Heaven and Earth), or appears in fifteen fascicles. Its title is given as *Lishi abidamo zang* (Abhidharma-piṭaka of the Establishment of the World), and it contains one hundred and sixty-four sheets. The *Vimuktimārga-śāstra* (Jietuodao lun) consists of twelve or thirteen fascicles and is contained in one bundle of one hundred and ninety-seven sheets. The *Śāriputra-abhidharma-śāstra* consists of twenty-two fascicles (sometimes without the character "lun"), or twenty, or thirty fascicles, and contains six hundred and four sheets. The *Pañcavastu-vibhāṣā-śāstra* consists of two fascicles, also called the *Abhidharma-pañcavastu-śāstra*, and contains twenty-four sheets. The above two treatises comprise twenty-four fascicles and are arranged in three bundles.

The *Vibhāṣā-śāstra* consists of fourteen fascicles; it is also called the *Vibhāṣā-abhidharma-śāstra*, or the *Vyāsabhāṣya*. It may also be in fifteen or nineteen fascicles, totaling three hundred and thirty-four sheets. The *Sammitīya-nikāya-śāstra* consists of three fascicles (or lacks the word "nikāya"), or four fascicles and thirty-six sheets. The aforementioned two treatises comprise seventeen fascicles in two volumes: the first volume contains eight fascicles, and the second volume contains nine.

The *Vibhaṅga-śāstra* (Treatise on the Analysis of Merit) in four fascicles—also called the *Vibhaṅga-sūtra*—or in three or five fascicles, totaling seventy-one sheets; the *Catuḥsatya-śāstra* (Treatise on the Four Noble Truths) in four fascicles, seventy-five sheets; the *Pratyekabuddha-hetupratyaya-śāstra* (Treatise on the Causes and Conditions of Pratyekabuddhas) in two fascicles, twenty sheets; the *Aṣṭādaśanikāya-śāstra* (Treatise on the Eighteen Schools) in one fascicle, eight sheets; and the *Samayabhedoparacanacakra-śāstra* (Treatise on the Different Tenets of the Various Schools), also known as the *Samayabheda-śāstra*, in one fascicle, nine sheets; and the *Samayabhedoparacanacakra-śāstra* (Treatise on the Wheel of the Different Tenets of the Various Schools) in one fascicle, eight sheets. These six treatises, totaling thirteen fascicles, are contained in the same volume.

The *Collection of the Worthy and Holy* (*Xian-sheng ji xian-sheng ji*), one hundred and eight sections, five hundred and forty-one fascicles, in fifty-seven bundles. Sixty-eight sections; forty sections produced [separately]: one hundred and seventy-three fascicles and three hundred and sixty-eight fascicles. The *Buddhacarita-kāvya* (translated from the Sanskrit original), five fascicles—sometimes titled without the word "kāvya" (*zhuan*) or without the word "sūtra" (*jing*); also called the *Buddha-pūrva-caryā-sūtra*, ninety sheets. The *Buddha-pūrva-caryā-sūtra*, seven fascicles, also known as the *Buddha-pūrva-caryā-kāvya-kathā*, one hundred and thirteen sheets. The above two collections comprise twelve fascicles in the same bundle.

The *Zaichibaiyuan jing* (Sūtra of the Collection of One Hundred Karmic Causes), ten fascicles, one bundle, one hundred and fifty sheets; the *Chuyao jing* (Sūtra of the Exalted Utterances), twenty fascicles—also called the *Chuyao lun* (Treatise on the Exalted Utterances)—or nineteen fascicles, four hundred and eighty-four sheets; the *Xianyu jing* (Sūtra of the Wise and the Foolish), thirteen fascicles—or fifteen, sixteen, or seventeen fascicles—also called the *Xianyu yinyuan jing* (Sūtra of the Causes and Conditions of the Wise and the Foolish), two hundred and eighty-three sheets. These two collections comprise thirty-three fascicles in four bundles: the first three bundles each contain eight fascicles, and the fourth bundle contains nine fascicles.

The *Dàodì jīng* (Sūtra on the Stages of the Path), one fascicle—also called the *Dàdàodì jīng* (Great Sūtra on the Stages of the Path)—is an excerpt from the *Xiūxíng jīng* (Sūtra on Practice); it is an abbreviated foreign version consisting of eighteen sheets. The *Xiūxíng dàodì jīng* (Sūtra on the Stages of Practice), six fascicles; its first fascicle is titled the *Yūzhējiā fùmí jīng* (Sūtra of Upagupta), or simply the *Xiūxíng jīng*; it consists of seven fascicles and one hundred thirty-five sheets. The *Sēngqiéluóchā suǒjí jīng* (Sūtra Compiled by Saṃgharakṣa), three fascicles—or five fascicles—consisting of eighty-five sheets. These three collections comprise ten fascicles in a single volume.

The *Śatavārṣika-dṛṣṭānta-sūtra* (Hundred Parables Sutra) in four fascicles, or five fascicles, or ten fascicles; its extent is not yet certain. It is also called the *Śatavākya-dṛṣṭānta-sūtra* (Sutra of One Hundred Sentences of Parables), consisting of forty-six sheets. The *Bodhisattva-pūrva-nidāna-sūtra* (Sutra on the Original Causes of Bodhisattvas) in three fascicles, also called the *Bodhisattva-pūrva-nidāna-saṃgraha-sūtra* (Collected Sutra on the Original Causes of Bodhisattvas), in either two fascicles or four fascicles, totaling fifty-four sheets. The *Mahāyāna-bhāvanā-bodhisattva-caryā-mukha-sarva-sūtra-arthasaṃgraha* (Essential Collection of Various Sutras on the Gate of Bodhisattva Practice in Mahāyāna Cultivation) in three fascicles, totaling eighty-one sheets. These three collections comprise ten fascicles in one volume.
The *Fufa zang yinyuan zhuan* (Biographies of the Causes and Conditions of the Transmission of the Dharma-treasury), six fascicles;

alternatively, it lacks the characters "yinyuan" (causes and conditions) and is also called the *Fufa zang jing* (Sutra on the Transmission of the Dharma-treasury), in either two or four fascicles, comprising eighty-two sheets. The *Zuochan sanmei jing* (Sutra on the Samādhi of Seated Meditation), three fascicles;

also known as the *Pusa chanfa jing* (Sutra on the Bodhisattva’s Method of Meditation), or simply the *Chan jing* (Meditation Sutra), or the *Aranya xichanfa jing* (Sutra on the Method of Practicing Meditation in the Aranya); alternatively, it is in two fascicles.
*The Sūtra on the Buddha as Physician*, one fascicle, fifty sheets; also called *The Sūtra on the King of Buddhist Physicians*, five sheets.
*The Sūtra on Various Difficulties Regarding the Sun*, one fascicle, fifteen sheets. *The Sūtra on Mahākāśyapa Following the Buddha to His Parinirvāṇa*, one fascicle, two sheets;
also called *The Sūtra on Kāśyapa Following the Buddha to His Parinirvāṇa*. *The Dharma for Rebuking Form and Desire*, one fascicle.
Also titled *One Sheet of Scripture, Four Chapters: A Scroll on Studying the Dharma* (1 scroll);
or *The Scripture on the Buddha’s Entry into Nirvāṇa and the Secret-Trace Vajra-Wielder’s Lamentation* (1 scroll, 6 sheets);

and *The Scripture on Kātyāyana Preaching the Verses on the Extinction of the Dharma* (1 scroll), titled *The Hundred Verses on the Extinction of the Dharma Preached by the Buddha’s Messenger, the Bhikṣu Kātyāyana*.
Chapter Twenty: *The Sūtra on the Buddha’s Treatment of the Body*, one fascicle (five sheets); alternatively titled *The Sūtra on the Treatment of the Mind*, one sheet.

*The Sūtra on the Treatment of the Mind*, one fascicle (one sheet); alternatively titled *The Sūtra on the Treatment of the Body*, one sheet. The eleven collections above, totaling eighteen fascicles, are contained in the same volume.

The *Saṃyukta-ratnapiṭaka-sūtra* (Zá bǎo zàng jīng), eight fascicles or thirteen fascicles, one hundred and fifty-three sheets; the *Nāgasena-bhikṣu-sūtra* (Nà xiān bǐqiū jīng), two fascicles—or alternatively called the *Nāgasena-sūtra*—or three fascicles, thirty-one sheets. These two collections comprise ten fascicles in a single volume.
*The Essential Methods for the Five-Gate Dhyāna Sūtra*, one fascicle, twenty-three sheets;

*Dharmatrāta’s Dhyāna Sūtra*, two fascicles—also titled *Yogācārabhūmi* (translated as "The Stage of Cultivating the Path") or *Aśubhabhāvanā Sūtra* (Sūtra on the Contemplation of Impurity)—fifty-one sheets;
*The Essential Explanation of Dhyāna Methods*, two fascicles—also titled *Canyao jing* (Sūtra on the Essentials of Dhyāna)—thirty-four sheets.
*Chanyao heyu jing* (Sutra on the Essentials of Dhyāna: Rebuking Desire), one fascicle; titled as the "Chapter on Rebuking Desire" within the *Chanyao jing*, four sheets.

*Neishen guan zhangju jing* (Sutra on the Contemplation of the Internal Body and its Phrases), one fascicle; alternatively, without the word "phrases," two sheets. *Faguang jing* (Sutra on the Contemplation of Dharmas), one fascicle, six sheets.

*Sifou lüyao fa* (Brief Essential Methods of Contemplation), one fascicle; alternatively called *Sifou yaolüe fajing* (Sutra of the Brief Essential Methods of Contemplation) or simply *Sifou jing* (Sutra of Contemplation), ten [sheets].

The *Shi er you jing* (Sūtra of the Twelve Wanderings), one fascicle, six sheets; the *Jiu za piyu jing* (Old Sūtra of Miscellaneous Parables), two fascicles, also called the *Za piyu ji* (Collection of Miscellaneous Parables), thirty-seven sheets;
and the *Za piyu jing* (Miscellaneous Parables Sūtra), one fascicle, nine sheets—these ten works comprise thirteen fascicles in a single volume.

*Zapiyujing* (Scripture of Miscellaneous Parables), two fascicles—also titled *Pusa durenjing* (Sūtra on the Bodhisattva Delivering Humans)—25 sheets. *Zapiyujing*, one fascicle—28 sheets. *Ayuwang piyujing* (Scripture of Parables of King Aśoka), one fascicle; the title reads *Tianzun shuo Ayuwang piyujing* (The Scripture of Parables of King Aśoka Spoken by the Celestial Honored One); as ancient scriptures referred to the Buddha as the "Celestial Honored One," this is a scripture spoken by the Buddha. 7 sheets. *Ayuwang jing* (Scripture of King Aśoka), ten fascicles—111 sheets. The four collections above comprise fourteen fascicles in one volume.

The *Aśokarāja-avadāna* (Biography of King Aśoka) in seven fascicles—sometimes with the character "Da" (Great) prefixed—or in five fascicles; also called the *Mahā-aśokarāja-sūtra*, totaling one hundred sheets. The *Aśokarāja-tanaya-dharmavardhana-cakṣur-vināśana-hetupratyaya-sūtra* (Sūtra on the Causes and Conditions for the Loss of Sight of King Aśoka’s Son) in one fascicle; its preface title reads *Aśokarāja-tanaya-dharmavardhana-cakṣur-vināśana-hetupratyaya-sūtra*, or alternatively *Aśokarāja-tanaya-cakṣur-vināśana-hetupratyaya* (without the character "jing" [sūtra]), totaling twenty-six sheets. The *Catuḥ-āgama-mukha-saṃgraha-bhāṣya* (Commentary on the Summary of the Four Āgamas) in two fascicles; also called the *Catuḥ-āgama-mukha-saṃgraha-sūtra*, totaling thirty-six sheets. The above three collections comprise ten fascicles and are contained in the same volume.
The *Dharmapada-sūtra* in two fascicles, also called the *Dharmapada-saṃgraha*, consists of thirty-four sheets.

From the *Śiśumāra-nidāna-sūtra* (The Discourse on the Causes and Conditions of the Crocodile) downward, there are forty-one works in forty-seven fascicles.
These are all narratives concerning the origins found within the Vinaya of the Sarvāstivāda school,
excerpted and circulated by the Tripiṭaka Master Yijing;
since they belong to a distinct category, they have not been included here.

The *Māyākāra-Acirajū-vidyā-sūtra*, one fascicle; the *Ratnagotravibhāga-śāstra*, four fascicles; and the *Ratnakūṭa-sūtra-śāstra*, four fascicles—these three works, totaling nine fascicles, were all included in the canon during the Zhou dynasty and are extant scriptures;
however, I have yet to locate their original manuscripts.
Therefore, these newly translated scriptures are not included in the catalogue. Since their original texts have not been obtained, they cannot be recorded in detail. They consist of:

the *Jingdu sanmei jing* (Scripture on the Samādhi of Purified Deliverance) in three fascicles; the *Fashu jing* (Scripture on the Dharma Society) in two fascicles; the *Piluo sanmei jing* (Scripture on the Vīra-samādhi) in two fascicles; the *Jueding zui fu jing* (Scripture on the Determination of Sin and Merit) in one fascicle; the *Yiyi jing* (Scripture on Benefiting the Mind) in two fascicles; the *Jiuhu shenming ji renbing kuye jing* (Scripture on Saving and Protecting Life and Delivering People from the Suffering and Calamities of Illness) in one fascicle; the *Zuimiaoshengding jing* (Scripture on the Most Sublime and Supreme Samādhi) in one fascicle; the *Guanshiyin sanmei jing* (Scripture on the Samādhi of Avalokiteśvara) in one fascicle; the *Qingjing faxing jing* (Scripture on Pure Dharma Practice) in one fascicle; and the *Gao wang guanshiyin jing* (The High King’s Scripture on Avalokiteśvara) in one fascicle—also known as the *Zhedaoying jing*. These ten works, following the *Jingdu jing*, comprise fifteen fascicles in total.
These are all spurious or doubtful scriptures found within ancient catalogs.
Although the Zhou Catalogue included them in its main body of texts, their principles are all tainted by human fabrication;
therefore, they have been excluded from this catalog and are not recorded herein.
The above totals one hundred and eighteen sections comprising two hundred and forty-seven fascicles.
Most of these were included in the various catalogs as having entered the canon;
however, they are now all deemed redundant or are works that have not yet been recovered despite searches.
Therefore, these are not included among the categories of definitive views.
Fearing that you may not understand the details, I have briefly described them here.
If you wish to know the underlying causes in full detail, [you must consult other sources].
This is also as extensively described in the *Shanfan lü* (Abridged Record).

Catalogue of the Mahāyāna Canon, Volume One. The Mahāyāna Sūtras, Vinayas, and Śāstras comprise a total of six hundred and thirty-eight works in two thousand seven hundred and forty-five fascicles, arranged in two hundred and fifty-eight bundles (*zhì*). This list presents the titles of the sūtras directly along with the number of pages for each label; the remainder follows the extensive catalogue. There are five hundred and fifteen Mahāyāna sūtra works.
Two thousand one hundred and seventy-three fascicles;
two hundred and three bundles.

Fifty bundles.
Mahāyāna sūtras—Mahāyāna sūtras translated through combinations of single and multiple versions—three hundred eighty-four works in one thousand eight hundred eighty fascicles.

The *Mahāprajñāpāramitā-sūtra* consists of one hundred and seventy-nine bundles (*zhì*) totaling six hundred fascicles, spoken in sixteen assemblies across sixty bundles and ten thousand three hundred thirty-one sheets of paper. It was translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang dynasty at the Yuhua Palace Monastery. The *Prajñāpāramitā-āloka-prabhāsa-sūtra* (also known as the *Āloka-mahāprajñā-sūtra* or the *Mahāprajñā-āloka-sūtra*) consists of three bundles, or twenty-one fascicles, totaling four hundred and sixty-six sheets of paper.

It was translated by the Tripitaka Master Mokṣala of the Western Jin dynasty together with Zhu Shulan. The *Mahāprajñāpāramitā-sūtra* (also known as the *Dapin Prajñā-sūtra*) consists of forty fascicles. According to Sengyou’s catalogue, it is called the *Xin Dapin Jing* (New Dapin Sutra) and comprises four bundles, consisting of either twenty-four, twenty-seven, or thirty fascicles, totaling six hundred and twenty-three sheets of paper.

The *Guangzan Banruo Boluomi Jing* (Sutra of the Radiant Praise of the Perfection of Wisdom) in fifteen fascicles, also known as the *Guangzan Mahāprajñā Sūtra*, consisting of two hundred twenty-one sheets, was translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin dynasty together with Sengrui and others.

The *Mohe Banruo Boluomi Chaojing* (Excerpted Sutra of the Great Perfection of Wisdom) in five fascicles—sometimes omitting the character "chao" (excerpt)—also titled the *Chang'an Pin Jing* (Sutra of the Chang'an Chapter), or alternatively the *Subhūti Pin Jing* (Sutra of the Subhūti Chapter), in seven fascicles and ninety sheets, was translated by the Indian Śramaṇa Dharmapriya together with Zhu Fonian of the Fu Qin dynasty.
These two aforementioned sutras comprise twenty fascicles in two volumes.

*Daoxing Banruo Boluomi Jing* (The Sutra on the Practice of the Perfection of Wisdom), ten fascicles, one set; the title is also given as *Mahāprajñāpāramitā Daoxing Jing* or *Banruo Daoxingpin Jing*. One hundred and sixty-seven pages. Translated by the Yuezhi Tripiṭaka Master Zhi Loujiachen of the Later Han.

*Xiaopin Banruo Boluomi Jing* (The Shorter Prajñāpāramitā Sutra), ten fascicles, one set; the title is given as *Mahāprajñāpāramitā* without the characters for "Shorter" (*Xiao*). Sengyou’s catalogue states it is the "New Xiaopin Jing," consisting of either eight or seven fascicles and one hundred and fifty pages.

Translated by the Yao Qin Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva. *Damingdu Wujijing* (The Great Perfection of Wisdom Sutra), four fascicles; also simply titled *Damingdu Jing*, or in six fascicles. Ninety pages.
The *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra* (or *Śrī-devī-prajñāpāramitā-sūtra*), translated by the Yuezhi Upāsaka Zhi Qian of the Wu [Dynasty], in seven fascicles and one hundred twenty-five sheets;
and the [same] translated by Prince Śubhakarasiṃha of the kingdom of Ujjayinī during the Chen [Dynasty]. These two scriptures, totaling eleven fascicles, are bound together in one volume.

The *Mañjuśrī-bhāṣita-mahāprajñāpāramitā-sūtra* in two fascicles, also simply titled the *Mañjuśrī-prajñāpāramitā-sūtra*, in one fascicle and twenty-one pages, translated by the Tripitaka Master Mandarasa from Funan of the Liang dynasty;
the *Mañjuśrī-bhāṣita-prajñāpāramitā-sūtra* in one fascicle and twenty pages, translated by the Tripitaka Master Saṃghavarman from Funan;
and the *Mṛdumati-bodhisattva-anuttara-viśuddha-piṇḍapāta-sūtra* in two fascicles—also known as the *Sarvadharmamāyopama-nirvedha-samādhi*—in twenty-eight pages.
*Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, one fascicle, eleven sheets, translated by the Song dynasty śramaṇa Shuogong at Nanhai Commandery.
*Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, one fascicle, eleven sheets, translated by Kumārajīva of the Yaoqin (Later Qin) dynasty in the kingdom of Śrāvastī.
*Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, one fascicle, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci of India during the Northern Wei dynasty.

The *Śrīmālādevī-siṃhanāda-ekayāna-mahā-upāya-paṭṭhāna-sūtra* (translated during the Jin dynasty; the name of the Tripiṭaka Master is lost), also simply titled the *Śrīmālā Sūtra*, in one fascicle, consisting of nineteen sheets, translated by Guṇabhadra of the Song dynasty.
The *Vaiśravaṇaparipṛcchā Sūtra*, in two fascicles, consisting of thirty-four sheets, translated by Gautama Prajñāruci.
These eight preceding sūtras comprise ten fascicles in a single volume.

*Mahāvaipulya Mahāsannipāta Sūtra*, thirty fascicles (three bundles), or twenty-nine, thirty-one, thirty-two, or forty-two fascicles; six hundred and twenty-one sheets. Translated at Guzang by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmakṣema of India during the Northern Liang dynasty.
*Mahāvaipulya Mahāsannipāta Sūtra: Sūryagarbha-parivarta*, ten fascicles (one bundle); titled *Mahāyāna Mahāvaipulya Sūryagarbha-vibhāga Sūtra*, or twelve, or fifteen fascicles;

two hundred and six sheets. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Narendrayaśas during the Sui dynasty. *Mahāsannipāta Sūtra: Candragarbha-parivarta*, ten fascicles (one bundle); titled *The Twelfth Division: Candragarbha-vibhāga of the Mahāsannipāta Sūtra*, or twelve, or fifteen fascicles; two hundred and nineteen sheets.
*Mahāsaṃnipāta-sūtra: Daśacakra-kṣitigarbha-parivarta*, ten fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Narendrayaśas of India during the Gao Qi dynasty; one bundle, 165 sheets.
*Mahāvaipulya-daśacakra-sūtra*, eight fascicles, 109 sheets, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang dynasty.

*Mahāsaṃnipāta-sūtra: Sumerugarbha-parivarta*, two fascicles; the internal title reads *Mahāyāna Mahāsaṃnipāta-sūtra: Sumerugarbha-parivarta, Chapter Fifteen*; 38 sheets. The translator is lost; it is currently appended to the Northern Liang catalog.
The two aforementioned sūtras, ten fascicles in total, were translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Narendrayaśas of India during the Gao Qi dynasty, together with Fazhi;

they are contained in the same volume. *Ākāśagarbha-bodhisattva-sūtra*, one fascicle—also titled *Ākāśagarbha-sūtra*, twenty-seven sheets—translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Buddhayaśas of Kapiśā during the Yao Qin dynasty. *Ākāśagarbha-bodhisattva-mantra-sūtra*, one fascicle, seventeen sheets.
*Ākāśagarbha-bodhisattva-sūtra*, two fascicles, thirty-one sheets; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmamitra of Kasmīra during the Song dynasty.

*Ākāśagarbha-bodhisattva-dhyāna-sūtra*, one fascicle (also titled *Ākāśagarbha-dhyāna-sūtra* or simply *Dhyāna-sūtra*), three sheets; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta of India and others during the Sui dynasty.

*Bodhisattva-buddhānusmṛti-samādhi-sūtra*, six fascicles (sometimes without the word "Bodhisattva," or five fascicles), ninety-eight sheets; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmamitra of Kasmīra during the Song dynasty.
Translated by the Indian Śramaṇa Guṇabhadra of the Song Dynasty together with Xuānchàng, the aforementioned five scriptures comprise eleven fascicles in one volume.

*Mahāvaipulya Mahāsannipāta Bodhisattva Buddhanusmṛti-samādhi Sūtra*, ten fascicles, one volume; the title reads *Mahāvaipulya Mahāsannipāta Sūtra, Bodhisattva Buddhanusmṛti-samādhi Section*, consisting of one hundred thirty-four pages;

translated by Guṇabhadra. *Bhadrakalpika-pratyutpanna-samādhi Sūtra*, three fascicles (also known as the *Sūtra on the Samādhi in Which All Buddhas of the Ten Directions Stand Before One*; alternatively titled the *Mahāpratyutpanna-samādhi Sūtra*), or two fascicles, fifty pages.
*The Sūtra of the Bodhisattva Bhadrapāla*, translated by Lokakṣema, one fascicle; also titled *The Sūtra of the Bodhisattva Bhadrapāla*. An’s Record states it consists of fourteen sheets;

Sengyou’s Record states it is among the "Ancient Classical Scriptures" of Master Dao’an and is now appended to the Han Records. *The Mahāvaipulya Mahāsannipāta Sūtra: The Section on Bhadrapāla*, five fascicles (or six); the title reads *The Mahāvaipulya Mahāsannipāta Sūtra: The Bhadrapāla Division*. Also called *The Sūtra of the Bodhisattva Bhadrapāla* or simply *The Bhadrapāla Sūtra*.
Eighty-two sheets. Translated by Jñānagupta and others. The above three sūtras, totaling nine fascicles, are contained in the same volume.

*The Sūtra of Akṣayamati* (A-ch’a-mo jīng), seven fascicles; translated during the Jin dynasty by Zhu Fahu as *The Sūtra of the Bodhisattva Akṣayamati*, also known as *The Sūtra of the Bodhisattva Akṣayamati*, or simply *The Sūtra of Akṣayamati*. It consists of ninety-two sheets. [Alternatively] it appears in four or five fascicles. *The Sūtra of the Bodhisattva Akṣayamati* (Wú-jìn-yì púsà jīng), six fascicles; translated by Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin. The initial title reads: "The Thirty-second Chapter on the Inexhaustible Meaning Spoken by the Bodhisattva Akṣayamati within the Mahāsaṃnipāta Sūtra. It is also called *The Sūtra of Akṣayamati* or simply *The Sūtra of Akṣayamati*. It consists of eighty-nine sheets. The above two sūtras comprise thirteen fascicles and are contained in the same volume.

*Mahāsaṃnipāta-dṛṣṭāntarāja-sūtra*, two fascicles (sometimes lacking the characters "Mahāsaṃnipāta"; *Mahāsaṃnipāta-viśeṣa-parivarta*, thirty-four sheets). Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta of India and others during the Sui dynasty. *Tathāgatamahākaruṇā-sūtra*, eight fascicles (also called *Tathāgata-mahākaruṇā-sūtra*; alternatively six or seven fascicles, totaling one hundred and seventeen sheets). Translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin dynasty. The above two sūtras, comprising ten fascicles in total, are contained in the same volume.

The *Ratnāvalī-paripṛcchā-sūtra* (or simply the *Ratnāvalī-sūtra*), also known as the *Ratnāvalī-paripṛcchā-prajñā-sūtra* or the *Ratnāvalī-samādhi-sūtra*, in three fascicles—or alternatively four fascicles comprising sixty-four sheets; and the *Avakīrṇa-kumāra-sūtra* (or the *Avakīrṇa-bodhisattva-sūtra*), in two fascicles—or alternatively one fascicle comprising forty-one sheets. These two aforementioned sūtras were translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin dynasty.

*Īśvararāja-bodhisattva-sūtra*, two fascicles (or without the word "Bodhisattva"), thirty-four sheets; translated by Kumārajīva. *Veṣṭhila-rāja-paripṛcchā-sūtra*, two fascicles, forty-one sheets; translated by Gautama Prajñāruci. These four preceding sūtras comprise nine fascicles in one volume.
*The Ratnaketu Dhāraṇī Sūtra*, ten fascicles (or eight fascicles), one bundle, 133 pages; translated by the Tang Dynasty Indian Tripiṭaka Master Śīlamitra.
*The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha’s Great Extensive Teachings*, sixty fascicles, spoken in eight assemblies; the old translation in six bundles (or fifty fascicles), 1,079 pages;

translated by the Eastern Jin Dynasty Indian Tripiṭaka Master Buddhabhadra and others. *The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha’s Great Extensive Teachings*, eighty fascicles, spoken in nine assemblies; the new translation in eight bundles, 1,327 pages.
*Śraddhābalādhānāvatāramudrā-sūtra*, five fascicles, ninety-five sheets; translated during the reign of Empress Wu of the Tang dynasty by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan and others.
*Buddhaviṣayāvatārajñānālokālaṃkāra-sūtra*, one fascicle, eleven sheets; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmaruci of the Northern Wei dynasty.
*Buddhāvataṃsaka-tathāgataguṇajñānācintyaviṣayāvatāra-sūtra*, two fascicles, twenty-two sheets; translator lost; now appended to the records of the Qin dynasty.

*The Mahāvaipulya Sūtra on Entering the Inconceivable Wisdom and Virtue of the Tathāgata*, one fascicle, fourteen sheets; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta of Central India during the Sui Dynasty.

*The Mahāvaipulya Buddhāvataṃsaka Sūtra, Chapter on the Inconceivable Realm of the Buddha*, one fascicle (or two), twelve sheets; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan during the reign of Empress Wu of the Tang Dynasty.

*The Mahāvaipulya Sūtra on the Inconceivable Realm of the Tathāgata*, one fascicle, eleven sheets; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Ti-p’o Prajña of Khotan during the reign of Empress Wu of the Tang Dynasty.

One fascicle of the *Mahāyāna-vajra-śekhara-maṇi-bodhisattva-caryā-sūtra*, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan during the reign of Empress Wu of the Tang; also titled the "Chapter on the Application of Vajraśekhara Bodhisattva," consisting of eighteen sheets.
One fascicle of the "Section on Cultivating Compassion" from the *Avataṃsaka-sūtra*, translated by Bodhiruci during the reign of Empress Wu of the Tang, consisting of seven sheets.
These eight scriptures, totaling thirteen fascicles, are contained in the same volume.

*The Mahāvaipulya Sūtra Spoken by Samantabhadra*, one fascicle: there is a separate manuscript of approximately thirty sheets which is not the original sūtra; it must be carefully distinguished [from the authentic version].
*The Sūtra on Adorning the Bodhicitta*, one fascicle, seven sheets; translated by Śikṣānanda.
*The Mahāvaipulya Sūtra on the Ten Stages of the Bodhisattva*, one fascicle, seven sheets; translated by Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin dynasty.
*Duṣa jīng* (The Scripture on the Tuṣita Heaven), one fascicle, five sheets; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kiṅkiaya of the Western Regions during the Northern Wei, together with Tanyao.

*Bōsà běnyè jīng* (The Scripture on the Original Vows and Deeds of Bodhisattvas), one fascicle; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Lokakṣema of the Yuezhi during the Later Han. It simply says *Běnyè jīng* (Scripture on Original Deeds) and is also titled *Jìngxíngpǐn jīng* (Scripture on the Chapter of Pure Conduct);

twelve sheets. *Zhū púsà qiú fó běnyè jīng* (The Scripture on the Original Vows and Deeds of All Bodhisattvas Seeking Buddhahood), one fascicle; sometimes the word "zhū" (all) is omitted; eleven sheets. Translated by the Yuezhi Upāsaka Zhi Qian of the Wu [Dynasty].
*The Chapter on the Bodhisattva’s Practice of the Ten Stages*, one fascicle, translated by the lay devotee Nie Daozhen of the Western Jin;
also simply titled *The Bodhisattva’s Ten Stages*, eight sheets, translated by Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin;

*The Sutra on the Bodhisattva’s Ten Stages*, one fascicle, five sheets, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta of the Western Regions during the Eastern Jin; *The Sutra on the Gradual Preparation for All-Wise Virtue*, five fascicles (or ten fascicles), also known as *The Ten Stages* or *The Great Wisdom Light Samādhi*, one hundred and five sheets.
Translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin: the nine preceding scriptures comprise thirteen fascicles in one volume.

*Daśabhūmika-sūtra* (Ten Stages Sutra), four fascicles (or five), ninety-seven sheets; translated by Kumārajīva together with Buddhayaśas of the Yao Qin. *Samādhirāja-sūtra* (Sutra on the Samādhi Asked for by the Bodhisattva Samantadarśin), two fascicles (or three); also known as *The Samādhi of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra* or simply *The Sutra of the Bodhisattva Samantadarśin*, fifty-two sheets; translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin. *Amitābha-buddhakṣetra-guṇavyūha-sūtra* (Sutra on the Manifestation of the Merits of Boundless Buddha-fields), one fascicle, two sheets; translated by Xuanzang of the Tang. *Tathāgatotpattisambhava-sūtra* (Sutra on the Arising and Manifestation of the Tathāgata), four fascicles; also known as *The Sutra on the Manifestation of the Illusory Nature of the Tathāgata*, sixty-six sheets; translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin. The above four scriptures comprise eleven fascicles in one volume.

*The Scripture on the Chapter of Delivering the World*, six fascicles (or five fascicles, or lacking the word "chapter"), one hundred and twenty sheets; translated by Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin. *The Lomaga Scripture*, three fascicles, seventy-two sheets; translated by the Śramaṇa Shi Shengjian of the Qifu Qin. *The Continuation of the Dharmadhātu Chapter of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, one fascicle (or lacking the word "continuation"), eight sheets; translated by Divākara of the Tang. These three scriptures comprise ten fascicles in a single volume.

*Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra*, forty fascicles (or thirty-six fascicles), four bundles, seven hundred and thirty sheets. Translated at Guzang by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmakṣema of India during the Northern Liang dynasty. The *Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra: Post-translation Section on Cremation* (*Dāvī-bhāga*), two fascicles—also called the *Section on Cremation* (*Jāvaī-bhāga*) or the *Later Section*. Translated in that country by the Śramaṇa Jñānabhadra of Puling in Nanhai, Tang China, together with the Śramaṇa Huìníng of Tang China; thirty-nine sheets. The *Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra*, six fascicles; the record states it is the *Vaipulya Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra* consisting of one hundred and forty-one sheets. Translated by the Śramaṇa Faxian of Pingyang during the Eastern Jin, together with Buddhabhadra. These two aforementioned scriptures comprise eight fascicles in a single bundle.

*The Vaipulya Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra*, two fascicles; also called *The Great Parinirvāṇa Sūtra*, or three fascicles and forty-five pages. Translated by Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin. *The Sūtra on the Samādhi of the Four Boys*, three fascicles; sometimes the word "samādhi" is omitted. Forty-four pages. Translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta and others of the Sui dynasty. *The Mahākaruṇā Sūtra*, five fascicles and eighty-seven pages. Translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Narendrayaśas together with Fazhi of the Northern Qi. These three sūtras comprise ten fascicles and are contained in the same volume.

*The Mahāvaipulya Buddhāvatamsaka Sūtra*, twelve fascicles; also known as *The Play of Supernatural Powers* or *The Great Vaipulya*, consisting of one hundred and fourteen sheets. Translated by the Tripitaka Master Divākara of Central India during the Tang Dynasty. *The Puyao Jing* (Sūtra of Universal Radiance), eight fascicles; also known as *The Vaipulya Origin of the Buddha*, consisting of one hundred and forty-three sheets. Translated by the Tripitaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin Dynasty. The above two sūtras comprise twenty fascicles in two volumes.

*Fahua sanmei jing* (Sutra on the Samādhi of the Lotus), one fascicle, eleven sheets; translated by the Śramaṇa Shi Zhiyan of Liangzhou during the Song dynasty. *Wuliangyi jing* (Sutra of Immeasurable Meanings), one fascicle, seventeen sheets; translated by the Indian Śramaṇa Dhammagatayasha during the Southern Qi dynasty. *Sadam fentulijing* (Sutra of the White Lotus of the True Dharma), one fascicle, three sheets; the old catalogues call it *Sayun fentulijing*, and it is also simply called *Fentulijing*. The Sengyou Catalogue states that this was a work whose translator was lost during the time of Master Dao’an; it is now appended to the Western Jin records. *Miaofa lianhua jing* (The Lotus Sutra of the Wondrous Dharma), seven fascicles, one hundred fifty-two sheets; translated by Kumārajīva of Yaoqin during the Sengyou Catalogue period. These four sutras, totaling ten fascicles, are contained in the same volume.

*The Sutra of the Lotus of the True Dharma* (Zhengfahua jing), ten fascicles; alternatively called *The Vaipulya Sutra of the Lotus of the True Dharma*, or seven fascicles, one bundle, totaling one hundred and ninety sheets. Translated by the Western Jin Tripiṭaka Master Dharmarakṣa. *The Expanded Version of the Lotus of the Wonderful Dharma Sutra* (Tiānpǐn Miaofa lianhua jing), seven fascicles, twenty-seven chapters. The "Jeweled Stupa" chapter and the "Devadatta" chapter are joined as one, making eight fascicles in total, totaling one hundred and fifty-eight sheets. Translated by the Sui dynasty Indian Tripiṭaka Masters Kumārajīva and Jñānagupta together. *The Vimalakīrti-nirdeśa Sūtra* (Weimojie suoshuo jing), three fascicles; also known as *The Inconceivable Liberation* or simply *The Miscellaneous Vimalakīrti Sutra*. According to Sengyou’s Catalogue, this is the *New Vimalakīrti Sutra*, totaling sixty sheets. Translated by the Yao Qin Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva. The aforementioned two sutras comprise ten fascicles in a single bundle.

*Vimalakīrti-nirdeśa-sūtra*, two fascicles—also known as *The Inconceivable Dharma-gate of Vimalakīrti*, or alternatively titled *The Sūtra on the Buddha-dharma Universally Entering the Gate of the Path and Samādhi*; three fascicles, fifty-five sheets; translated by the Yuezhi Upāsaka Zhi Qian of the Wu dynasty. *Sūtra Spoken by the Stainless Renowned One* (*Vimalakīrti-nirdeśa-sūtra*), six fascicles, ninety-seven sheets; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang dynasty. *Mahāvaipulya Cūḍāmaṇi-rāja-sūtra*, one fascicle—also known as *The Sūtra of the Questions of Vimalakīrti’s Son*, or *The Sūtra of the Youth Sudhana*, or simply *Cūḍāmaṇi-rāja-sūtra*; twenty sheets; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin dynasty. *Mahāyāna Cūḍāmaṇi-rāja-sūtra*, one fascicle—also called *The Sūtra of Vimalakīrti’s Son*; sixteen sheets; translated by Prince Śubhakaravarman of the Kingdom of Ujjayinī during the Liang dynasty. The above four sūtras comprise eleven fascicles and are contained in the same volume.

*The Scripture on the Youth Subhūṣita*, two fascicles, twenty-one sheets; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta of India during the Sui Dynasty. *The Great Compassion Puṇḍarīka Scripture*, eight fascicles—also known as the *Mahāyāna Compassion Puṇḍarīka Scripture*—one hundred and sixty-eight sheets; translator lost, now appended to the Qin Records. These two scriptures, totaling ten fascicles, share one case.

*Beihua jing* (Sutra of the Compassionate Flower), ten fascicles, one set, one hundred and ninety sheets; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmakṣema of India during the Northern Liang dynasty at Guzang. *Jin guangming zuishengwang jing* (Suvarṇaprabhāsa-uttamarāja-sūtra), ten fascicles, one set, one hundred and forty-nine sheets; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Yijing during the reign of Empress Wu of the Tang dynasty. *Hebu jin guangming jing* (Combined Suvarṇaprabhāsa Sūtra), eight fascicles, twenty-four chapters, one hundred and twenty sheets; compiled by Baogui of Daxingshan Temple during the Sui dynasty. *Dunzhentuo suowen jing* (Sutra of the Questions of Candrāvatī), two fascicles; the first states it is the *Dunzhentuo suowen baorulai sanmei jing*, or alternatively called the *Dunzhentuo niwang jing*, or three fascicles, fifty-eight sheets; translated by Zhi Loujiachen of the Later Han dynasty. The above two sutras comprise eleven fascicles in a single set.

*Mahādruma-kinnara-rāja-paripṛcchā-sūtra*, four fascicles; also titled *Acintya-varga-nirdeśa* or simply *Mahādruma-kinnara-sūtra*; sixty-seven sheets. Translated by Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin dynasty. *Buddha-utpatti-trāyastriṃśa-deva-loka-mātṛ-dharma-deśanā-sūtra*, two fascicles; also called *Buddha-utpatti-trāyastriṃśa-deva-loka-varga-sūtra* or three fascicles; thirty-seven sheets. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin dynasty. *Mārgarddhi-vikurvāṇa-ananta-sūtra*, four fascicles; also known as *Mārgarddhi-samudgata-sūtra*; alternatively in two or three fascicles; forty-nine sheets. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master An Faqin of Parthia during the Western Jin dynasty. The above three sūtras comprise ten fascicles in one volume.

The *Ratnamegha Sūtra* (Jewel Rain Sūtra), ten fascicles, one set, one hundred forty-one sheets; translated during the era of Empress Wu of the Tang dynasty by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmaruci from South India and others. The *Ratnamegha Sūtra* (Jewel Cloud Sūtra), seven fascicles, one hundred two sheets; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Mandarasena of Funan together with Saṃghavarman during the Liang dynasty. The *Anuvyādha-ccheda Sūtra* (Sūtra on the Severing of Non-retrogression), three fascicles—or four fascicles without the character "che" (遮)—sixty-six sheets; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin dynasty. These two aforementioned sūtras comprise ten fascicles in a single set.

*The Sūtra on the Non-Retrogressive Wheel of Dharma* (Avaivartika-cakra-sūtra), four fascicles; also known as the *Sūtra on Non-Retrogression*. Seventy-three sheets. Sengyou’s Catalogue states that Master Dao’an recorded it as a distinct sūtra from the Liang region. The Northern Liang Catalogue lists the *Extensive and Pure Non-Retrogressive Wheel of Dharma Sūtra* in four fascicles, or six fascicles, or simply as the *Extensive and Pure Sūtra*, or simply as the *Non-Retrogressive Wheel of Dharma Sūtra*. Seventy-eight sheets. Translated by the Song dynasty śramaṇa Zhìyán of Liangzhou together with Bǎoyún. *Sūtra on Entering the Seal of Certainty and Uncertainty* (Samādhi-niyata-aniyata-mudrā-sūtra), one fascicle, twenty-one sheets. Translated by the Yuan Wei dynasty brahmin Gautama Prajñāruci. *Sūtra on Entering the Seal of Certainty and Uncertainty* (Samādhi-niyata-aniyata-mudrā-sūtra), one fascicle, sixteen sheets. Translated during the reign of Empress Wu of the Tang dynasty by Tripiṭaka Master Yìjìng. The above four sūtras comprise ten fascicles and are contained in the same volume.

*Samādhirājasūtra* (The Scripture on the Samādhi of the Equal Accumulation of All Virtues), three fascicles (or two fascicles; some versions omit the word "samādhi" or simply call it *Dengji jing*), fifty sheets. Translated by the Tripitaka Master Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin. *Sarvapuṇyasamuccayasamādhisūtra* (The Scripture on the Samādhi of the Collection of All Merits), three fascicles, fifty sheets. Translated by the Tripitaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin. *Brahmaviśeṣacintiparipṛcchāsūtra* (The Scripture on the Questions of Brahmā Viśeṣacinti), four fascicles—also called *Brahmaviśeṣacintiparipṛcchāsūtra*, alternatively titled *Zhuangyanfofajing* (Scripture on the Adornment of the Buddha-Dharma) or *Dengyuzhufa jing* (Scripture on the Equal Governing of All Dharmas)—consisting of seventeen chapters (or six fascicles, ninety-one sheets). Translated by the Tripitaka Master Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin. The above three scriptures comprise ten fascicles and are contained in the same volume.

The *Suvikrāntavikrāmī-paripṛcchā-sūtra* (also simply called the *Suyi jing*), four fascicles; the *Sengyou lu* records it as the *Suyi yi jing*, consisting of eighty-three sheets. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin dynasty. The *Suvikrāntavikrāmī-paripṛcchā-sūtra*, six fascicles, one hundred and one sheets. Translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci of the Northern Wei dynasty. These two aforementioned sūtras, totaling ten fascicles, are contained in the same volume.

*The Scripture of the Bodhisattva Dharanidhara* (持人菩薩經), four fascicles. The first fascicle states: "The Scripture on the Bodhisattva Dharanidhara’s Inquiry into the Aggregates, Elements, and Sense Bases for the Sake of Realizing the Wisdom of the Path. Alternatively, it exists in three fascicles and fifty-four sheets. Translated by the Tripitaka Master Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin dynasty. *The Scripture of Holding the World* (持世經), four fascicles—also known as the *Dharmamudrā-sūtra* (法印經)—or alternatively in three fascicles and seventy-eight sheets. Translated by the Tripitaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin dynasty. *The Scripture for Saving Those Who Study the Vaipulya* (濟諸方等學經), one fascicle. [The name includes] the Indian term *Vaibhāṣika-aśaikṣa* (和鞞曰僧迦無學). Fifteen sheets. Translated by the Tripitaka Master Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin dynasty. *The Mahāyāna Vaipulya Dhāraṇī Scripture* (大乘方廣總持經), one fascicle—or without the character "Mahāyāna" (無乘)—fourteen sheets. Translated by the Indian Tripitaka Master Vinitaruci of the Sui dynasty. These four preceding scriptures comprise ten fascicles in a single volume.

*The Scripture of Mañjuśrī Manifesting the Treasure Store* (Mañjuśrī-prabhāsa-ratnagarbha-sūtra), three fascicles, or two fascicles, or without the character "manifest" (xian), or simply titled *The Scripture of the Treasure Store*, forty-two sheets;

translated by the Tripitaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin. *The Great Vaipulya Scripture of the Precious Casket* (Mahāvaipulya-ratnakoṭi-sūtra), three fascicles, or two fascicles, forty-three sheets;

translated by the Indian Tripitaka Master Guṇabhadra of the Song dynasty. *The Mahāyāna Scripture on the Common Nature* (Mahāyāna-samatā-nirdeśa-sūtra), two fascicles, also titled *The Scripture Spoken from the Vairocana Treasury on Entering the Wisdom of All Buddha-Practices*, or alternatively titled *The Scripture on the Ten Stages of the Buddha* (Buddha-daśabhūmi-sūtra), four fascicles, thirty-eight sheets.

The *Mahāyānasamaya-sūtra* (also titled *Sarvabuddhaviṣayajñānāvatāravairocanagarbha*), two fascicles, translated by the Tripitaka Master Jñāyaśas of India during the Northern Zhou dynasty’s Yuwen clan, etc.; twenty-two sheets.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Divākara of Central India during the Tang dynasty. These four aforementioned sutras comprise ten fascicles in one volume.

*Saṃdhinirmocana-sūtra*, three fascicles, seventy-one pages; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci of India during the Northern Wei dynasty. *Saṃdhinirmocana-sūtra*, five fascicles, seventy-five pages; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang dynasty. These two sūtras comprise ten fascicles in one volume.
*Vibhaṅga-sūtra* (Sūtra on the Analysis of the Sections), one fascicle, ten sheets;

translated by the Chen dynasty Indian Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha. *Anupūrva-vimokṣa-bhūmi-pāramitā-nītārtha-sūtra* (Sūtra on the Ultimate Meaning of the Stages of Successive Liberation), one fascicle, or two fascicles; also titled *Vimokṣa-nītārtha-sūtra* or simply *Anupūrva-vimokṣa-sūtra*; eighteen sheets; translated by Guṇabhadra of the Song dynasty.

*Pratītyasamutpādādivibhaṅganirdeśa-dharmaparyāya-sūtra* (Sūtra on the Exposition of the Analysis of Dependent Origination and its Initial Superior Portion), two fascicles; also simply titled *Pratītyasamutpāda-sūtra*; twenty-three sheets.

The *Vibhaṅga-ādi-pratītyasamutpāda-dharmaparyāya-sūtra* in two fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmagupta of India during the Sui Dynasty (also simply titled *Vibhaṅga-pratītyasamutpāda-sūtra*, twenty-two pages);
and the *Laṅkāvatāra-ratna-sūtra* in four fascicles, ninety-two pages, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang Dynasty;
and the [same] translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Guṇabhadra of India during the Song Dynasty—these five sūtras, totaling ten fascicles, are contained in the same volume.

*Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra*, ten fascicles, one set, one hundred and seventy-four sheets; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci of the Northern Wei. *Mahāyāna Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra*, seven fascicles, one hundred and twenty-seven sheets; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan during the reign of Empress Wu of the Tang. *Bodhisattvacaryānirhāradharmatā-viṣaya-ṛddhivikurvāṇa Sūtra*, three fascicles, forty-seven sheets; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Guṇabhadra of India during the Song dynasty. These two aforementioned sūtras comprise ten fascicles in this single set.
*Mahāsāṃghika-śāṭhyaputra-nirgrantha-bhāṣita-sūtra*, ten fascicles, one volume; alternatively titled *Vyākaraṇa-anabhilāpya* (The Prediction of the Inexpressible), or seven or eight fascicles;

also known as *Bodhisattva-gocara-vikrīḍita-dharmamukha-sūtra*; 139 pages; translated by Dharmaruci of the Northern Wei. *Mahāvaipulya-mahāmegha-sūtra*, six fascicles; also known as *Mahāvaipulya-nimitta-mahāmegha-sūtra*, or *Mahāmegha-nimitta-sūtra*, or *Mahāmegha-madhyama-saṃbhāra-sūtra*;

alternatively five fascicles, 90 pages; translated by Dharmakṣema of the Northern Liang. *Mahāmegha-varṣa-prārthana-sūtra*, one fascicle; internal title reads *Mahāmegha-sūtra, Varṣa-prārthana-parivarta*, the sixty-fourth; 23 pages.
The *Mahāmegha-vṛṣṭi-saṃcodana-sūtra* (大雲輪請雨經), two fascicles, thirty-seven sheets, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Jñāyayaśas of Central India during the Northern Zhou dynasty;

the *Mahāvaipulya-mahāmegha-vṛṣṭi-saṃcodana-sūtra* (大方等大雲請雨經), one fascicle, twenty sheets, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Narendrayaśas of Central India during the Sui dynasty—the internal title of which reads *Mahāvaipulya-mahāmegha-sūtra*, Chapter Sixty-four: "The Vṛṣṭi-saṃcodana" (大方等大雲經請雨品第六十四);
and [the others] translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta of Central India during the Sui dynasty. These four sūtras comprise ten fascicles in a single volume.
*The Scripture on the Non-Activity of All Dharmas* (Zhūfǎ wúxíng jīng), two fascicles (or one fascicle), thirty-one pages;
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin dynasty. *The Scripture on the Original Non-existence of All Dharmas* (Zhūfǎ běnwú jīng), three fascicles, thirty-nine pages;

translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta and others of the Sui dynasty. *The Scripture on the Samādhi of the Ultimate Jewel* (Wújíbǎo sānmèi jīng), one fascicle (or without the word "Samādhi"), thirty pages.

*The Sūtra on the Samādhi of the Jewel Tathāgata*, two fascicles (also known as *The Sūtra on the Immeasurable Jewel Samādhi*), or one fascicle, thirty-eight sheets; translated by the Tripitaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin.

*The Sūtra on the Wisdom Seal Samādhi*, one fascicle (also known as *The Sūtra on the Jewel Field and the Wisdom Seal Samādhi*; commonly referred to simply as *The Wisdom Seal Sūtra*), twenty sheets; translated by the Tripitaka Master Gītamitra of the Western Regions during the Eastern Jin.
*The Sūtra on the Wisdom Seal of the Tathāgata*, one fascicle (also known as *The Dharma-body of All Buddhas*), nineteen sheets; translated by the Upāsaka Lokakṣema of Yuezhi during the Wu dynasty.
Among the scriptures of lost translators in Sengyou’s *Chu sanzang jiji*, six scriptures totaling eleven fascicles are now appended to the Song catalog in a single volume.

*The Great Scripture of Consecration* (Dà guǎngdìng jīng), twelve fascicles, one volume; alternatively, the catalog lacks the character "Great" (Dà), stating it is nine fascicles, the details of which are unknown; 118 sheets.

Translated by the Tripitaka Master Śrīmitra of the Western Regions during the Eastern Jin dynasty. *The Scripture on the Original Vows of the Medicine Master Tathāgata* (Yàośī rúlái běnyuàn jīng), one fascicle, twelve sheets.

*The Sūtra on the Merit of the Original Vows of the Tathāgata Bhaiṣajyaguru-vaiḍūryaprabha*, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmagupta of India during the Sui Dynasty; one fascicle, eleven pages.

*The Sūtra on the Merit of the Original Vows of the Seven Buddhas of the Bhaiṣajyaguru-vaiḍūryaprabha*, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang Dynasty; two fascicles, thirty-one pages.
*The Aśokarāja-sūtra*, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Yijing of the Tang Dynasty; two fascicles, fifty-five pages.

*Puchao sanmei jing* (Sūtra on the Samādhi of Universal Transcendence), translated by the Yuezhi Tripiṭaka Master Zhu Lokaṣema of the Later Han; three fascicles, or four fascicles, or with the title *Wenshushili puchao sanmei jing* (Mañjuśrī’s Sūtra on the Samādhi of Universal Transcendence) added, also simply called *Puchao jing*. Another name is *Ajātaśatru-rāja-piṇḍa*.
An Gong’s catalogue states that it was further issued as the *Ajātaśatru-rāja-sūtra* in sixty-eight sheets, translated by the Western Jin Tripiṭaka Master Dharmarakṣa.

*Fangbo jing* (Sūtra of the Alms Bowl), one fascicle, seven sheets. Sengyou’s catalogue states that it was among the scriptures of unknown translators in An Gong’s record; it is now appended to the Western Jin record. These six scriptures, totaling ten fascicles, are contained in the same volume.
*The Moon-Lamp Samādhi Sūtra*, eleven fascicles (or ten fascicles), one volume, 198 sheets;

translated by the Tripitaka Master Narendrayaśas of India during the Northern Qi dynasty. *The Moon-Lamp Samādhi Sūtra*, one fascicle—also known as *The Sūtra on the Ox-Deed of Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva* or *The Sūtra on the Samādhi of Established Wisdom*;
ten sheets; translated by the Śramaṇa Shi Xian-gong of the Song dynasty. *The Sūtra of No Expectation*, one fascicle—also known as *The Elephant-Step Sūtra*; twenty sheets.
*The Elephant’s Armpit Sūtra* (Xiangyi jing), one fascicle, sixteen sheets; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin.

*The Sūtra of the Great Purity Dharma-Gate* (Da jing famen jing), one fascicle; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmamitra of Jibin during the Song dynasty. Its title reads: *The First Part of the Sūtra of the Great Purity Dharma-Gate: The Questions of the Girl Suvarṇottamaprabhāśrī and the Exhortations of Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta*, twenty-four sheets;

translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin. *The Sūtra of the Great Adornment Dharma-Gate* (Da zhuangyan famen jing), two fascicles; also called *The Sūtra of Mañjuśrī’s Supernatural Powers* and *The Sūtra of the Girl Suvarṇavarṇaprabhāśrī*; twenty-six sheets.

*The Sūtra on the Tathāgata’s Adorned Wisdom Light Entering the Realm of All Buddhas*, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Narendrayaśas of India during the Sui Dynasty; two fascicles, also titled *The Sūtra on the Tathāgata Entering the Realm of All Buddhas*;
thirty-four sheets. Translated by Dharmaruci of the Northern Wei; one fascicle, twelve sheets. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Saṃghavarman et al. of Funan during the Liang Dynasty.
*The Sūtra of Verses on the Later Appearance of Amitābha Buddha*, one fascicle (sometimes without the word "sūtra"); one sheet.

*The Sutra on Contemplating the Buddha of Immeasurable Life*, one fascicle, translated during the Later Han dynasty with the translator lost; also titled *Contemplation of Immeasurable Life*, sixteen sheets.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śrīmitra of the Western Regions during the Song dynasty: *The Amitābha Sutra*, one fascicle, also titled *The Sutra of Immeasurable Life*, five sheets.

Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin dynasty: *The Sutra of the Buddha’s Acceptance of Praise for the Pure Land*, one fascicle, also simply called *The Sutra of Praise for the Pure Land*, ten sheets.
Translated by Tripitaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang Dynasty: the eleven preceding sutras, thirteen fascicles, in one volume.
*The Sutra on Contemplating Maitreya Bodhisattva’s Ascent to Tuṣita Heaven*, one fascicle—also called the *Maitreya’s Ascent Sutra*, eight sheets—translated by the Song layman Juqu Jingsheng.
*The Sutra on Maitreya Attaining Buddhahood*, one fascicle, seventeen sheets.
*The Sūtra on Maitreya’s Arrival*, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin dynasty;

one fascicle, three sheets; translator lost, now appended to the Eastern Jin catalog. *The Sūtra on Maitreya’s Descent*, also known as *The Sūtra on Maitreya Receiving the Prediction*, or *The Sūtra on Maitreya Attaining Buddhahood*; alternatively titled *He Shall Attain Buddhahood Hereafter*, or *He Has Already Attained Buddhahood*.

It begins with "The Great Wisdom Śāriputra. One fascicle, seven sheets; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin dynasty. *The Sūtra on Maitreya’s Descent and Attainment of Buddhahood*, five sheets.
*The Sūtra of the King of Valiantness of All Dharmas*, one fascicle, eighteen sheets; newly translated by the Tripitaka Master Yi Jing of the Tang dynasty.

*The Sūtra of the High King of All Dharmas*, one fascicle—also known as *The Sūtra of the King of All Meanings*, twenty sheets; translated by the Tripitaka Master Dhamamitra of Kasmira during the Song dynasty.
*The Sūtra of the Supreme Dharma of the Ultimate Truth*, one fascicle, fourteen sheets; translated by the Brahmin Gautama Prajñāruci of the Northern Wei dynasty.
*The Sūtra on the Questions of the Rishi Mahātejo’rcis*, translated by the Brahamana Gautama Prajñāruci of the Northern Wei; one fascicle, fifteen sheets.

*The Sūtra on Accordance with Expedient Means*, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta of India during the Sui dynasty; two fascicles. Also titled *The Sūtra on the Bodhisattva’s Transformation of Female Form*; alternatively called *The Sūtra on Accordance with Expedient Means*, *The Sūtra on Accordance with Expedient Means for Women*, or *The Sūtra on Following Expedient Means for Women*;

one fascicle, twenty-eight sheets. *The Sūtra on the Chapter of the Skillful Means of Adorning with Joyful Necklaces*, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin; one fascicle. Also called *The Sūtra on the Dialogue between the Bodhisattva and the Transformation of Female Form*.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmayaśas of Kaśmīra during the Yao Qin dynasty: the eleven sūtras above comprise twelve fascicles in one volume.

The *Ṣaḍpāramitā-saṃcaya-sūtra* (Six Perfections Collection Sūtra), eight fascicles—also titled the *Ṣaḍpāramitā-aparimita-sūtra*, the *Dù wújí jí* (Collection of the Unbounded), or the *Zá wújí jīng* (Miscellaneous Unbounded Sūtra)—translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kang Senghui of India during the Wu dynasty;
one fascicle, two hundred forty-seven pages. The *Sudāna-jātaka-sūtra* (Sūtra of Prince Sudāna), one fascicle—also called *Sudana*—sixteen pages.
*The Sūtra of the Bodhisattva Śyāma*, translated by the Qifu Qin śramaṇa Shi Shengjian. One fascicle; also called *The Sūtra of the Filial Son Śyāma*, or simply *The Sūtra of Śyāma*. Seven sheets.

Sengyou’s Catalogue states that it was among the "Translated-Unknown" sūtras in Master Dao’an’s catalogue; it is now appended to the Western Jin catalogue. *The Sūtra of the Filial Son Śyāma*: one name is *The Sūtra of the Filial Son Śyāma*, another is *The Sūtra of the Bodhisattva Śyāma*, another is *The Buddha-Spoken Sūtra of Śyāma*, another is *The Original Sūtra of Śyāma*, and another is *The Sūtra of the Hidden Filial Son*.
Six sheets. Translated by the Qifu Qin śramaṇa Shi Shengjian. *The Sūtra of the Prince’s Dream-Precious Spirit*: one fascicle. Six sheets.
*The Sūtra of Prince Mupò*, one fascicle (or three sheets), translated by the Tripiṭaka Master An Shigao of Parthia during the Later Han; also known as *Mùpò*.
*The Sūtra of the Nine-Colored Deer*, one fascicle (three sheets), translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin.
*The Sūtra of the Upāsaka Zhi Qian of Yuezhi*, translated during the Wu dynasty. These seven sūtras, totaling fourteen fascicles, are contained in the same volume.
*The Sutra of the Jewel Casket Without Letters*, one fascicle, six sheets;
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci of India during the Northern Wei dynasty. *The Mahāyāna Sutra of the Universal Radiance Treasury Free from Words and Letters*, one fascicle, five sheets;

translated at the Taiyuan Temple by the Tripiṭaka Master Śīlabhadra of Central India during the Tang dynasty. *The Mahāyāna Sutra of the All-Illuminating Radiance Treasury: The Dharma Door of Wordlessness*, one fascicle (also simply titled *The Mahāyāna Sutra of the All-Illuminating Radiance Treasury*), six sheets.

*The Scripture of the Old Woman*, one fascicle, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Divākara of Central India during the Tang Dynasty; it is also called *The Scripture of the Old Mother* or *The Scripture of the Old Girl*, consisting of two sheets.
Translated by the Upāsaka Zhi Qian of Yuezhi during the Wu Dynasty: *The Scripture of the Old Mother*, one fascicle, two sheets;

listed as a work of lost translation in Sengyou’s catalogue, now appended to the Song dynasty records. *The Scripture of Shenri*, one fascicle, five sheets. *The Scripture of the Six Virtues of the Old Mother*, one fascicle; also called *The Scripture of the Old Mother*, one sheet. The above was translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Guṇabhadra of India during the Song Dynasty.
*The Scripture of the Youth Candraprabha* (Candraprabhakumāra-sūtra), one fascicle—also titled *The Scripture of the Youth Candrāloka* or *The Scripture of Śunika*—nine sheets;

translated by the Tripitaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin. *The Original Scripture of Śunika’s Son*, one fascicle—also called *The Original Scripture of Śunika’s Son*; the catalog records it as *The Dō-bon*, which is an error; three sheets;
translated by the Indian Tripitaka Master Guṇabhadra of the Song dynasty. *The Scripture of the Elder Guṇapāla*, two fascicles—also titled *The Scripture of the Elder Śrīgupta*; twenty-eight sheets.

*Mañjuśrīparipṛcchā-bodhicitta-sūtra*, one fascicle. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Narendrayaśas of India during the Sui Dynasty. Also titled *Gayāśīrṣa-sūtra* or *Bodhyapracāra-sūtra*; also simply called *Bodhi-sūtra*. Seven pages.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin Dynasty. *Gayāśīrṣa-sūtra*, one fascicle; also called *Gayāśīrṣa-sūtra*. Ten pages.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci of India during the Northern Wei Dynasty. *Hastikṣaya-vihāra-sūtra*, one fascicle. Nine pages.
*Mahāyāna-gayāśīrṣa-sūtra*, one fascicle, nine pages; translated by the Indian Śramaṇa Vinītāruci during the Sui dynasty.

*Gṛhaputradharmasubhāṣita-sūtra*, one fascicle, four pages; translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci during the era of Empress Wu of the Tang dynasty (also simply titled *Dharmasubhāṣita*).
*Bodhisattvaparinirvāṇa-sūtra*, one fascicle, four pages; translated by An Shigao of the Han dynasty (also called *Pratijñā-kumāra-sūtra* or simply *Pari-nirvāṇa-sūtra*).

*The Sūtra of the Departing Child*, one fascicle, translated by the Śramaṇa Bái Fǎzǔ of the Western Jin; also titled *The Sūtra of the Elder’s Restriction*, or simply *The Sūtra of Restriction*; also titled *The Sūtra of the Bodhisattva’s Departure*, or simply *The Sūtra of Departure*. Three sheets. Translated by the Śramaṇa Zhī Fǎdù of the Western Jin.

*The Sūtra of the Girl Vimalā*, one fascicle; alternatively titled *The Sūtra of the Womb Matrix*. Three sheets. The two sūtras above were translated by the Tripitaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin.

*Fuzhong nü ting jing* (Sutra on the Woman in the Womb Listening to the Dharma), one scroll; also known as *Bu zhuangjiao nü jing*, three sheets. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmakṣema of India during the Northern Liang dynasty. *Zhuan nüshen jing* (Sutra on Transforming the Female Body), one scroll, nineteen sheets. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmamitra of Kaśmīra during the Song dynasty. The above twenty-one sutras comprise twenty-two scrolls in a single fascicle.
*Anuttaraśrayasūtra* (The Sutra on the Supreme Reliance), two fascicles, thirty-one pages;
translated by Paramārtha, the Tripitaka Master from India during the Liang Dynasty. *Adbhutasūtra* (The Sutra of Unprecedented Events), one fascicle, three pages;
translator lost during the Later Han Dynasty. *Atyadbhutasūtra* (The Sutra of the Most Rare and Wondrous), one fascicle, five pages.

*The Sutra of Decisive Compendium*, one fascicle, translated by Tripitaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang; also known as *The Sutra of Decisive Dhāraṇī* or *The Sutra of Decisive Compendium*, eight pages, translated by Tripitaka Master Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin.
*Sutra on the Slander of the Buddha*, one fascicle, seven pages, translated by the Indian Tripitaka Master Bodhiruci of the Northern Wei.

*Sutra of the Jewel-Heap Samādhi on Mañjuśrī’s Inquiry into the Dharma-body*, one fascicle—also titled *Sutra of the Jewel-Heap Samādhi Left Behind by the Sun on Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva’s Inquiry into the Dharma-body*—six pages.
*The Scripture on Entering the Essence and Nature of the Dharma-realm* (one fascicle), translated by An Shigao during the Later Han dynasty;
alternatively titled *The Scripture on Entering the Dharma-realm* (ten sheets), translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta and others during the Sui dynasty.

*The Scripture on the Tathāgata’s Lion’s Roar* (one fascicle, six sheets), translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Buddhayaśas during the Northern Wei dynasty. *The Mahāvaipulya Scripture on the Lion’s Roar* (one fascicle, five sheets). *The Mahāyāna Scripture on the Marks of the Hundred Merits* (one fascicle, seven sheets). The two scriptures above were translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Divākara during the Tang dynasty.
*Mahāyāna-satapuṇya-vyūha-lakṣaṇa-sūtra*, one fascicle, nine sheets;

retranslated by the Tripiṭaka Master Divākara of Central India during the Tang dynasty. *Mahāyāna-caturdharma-sūtra*, one fascicle; although the two names of the translators—Xuanzang and Śikṣānanda of the single-text edition—are the same, the content differs entirely in length, being only one sheet.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Divākara of Central India at Dongtao Yuan Temple during the Tang dynasty. *Bodhisattva-caryā-caturdharma-sūtra*, one fascicle, one sheet.

*The Sūtra on the Measurement of Merit of the Rare and Unprecedented*, one fascicle (six sheets), translated at Hongfu Monastery by the Tripiṭaka Master Divākara of Central India during the Tang Dynasty; also known simply as *The Sūtra on the Measurement of Merit of the Rare and Unprecedented*.

Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta and others of India during the Sui Dynasty. *The Sūtra of the Peerless*, one fascicle (twelve sheets), translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang Dynasty.
*The Sūtra of the Three Turnings of Previous Lives*, one fascicle (six sheets).
*The Sūtra of the Silver-Colored Woman*, one fascicle, seven pages; translated by the Śramaṇa Shi Faju of the Western Jin.
*The Sūtra of King Ajātaśatru Receiving the Prediction*, one fascicle, four pages; translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Buddhayaśas of the Northern Wei.

*The Sūtra of the King Who Plucked Lotus Flowers Going to the Buddha and Receiving the Prediction of the Name "Wonderful Flower"*, one fascicle; also simply titled *The Sūtra of the King Who Plucked Flowers*, two pages; translated by the Śramaṇa Shi Faju of the Western Jin.

*Zheng gongjing jing* (Sūtra on Right Reverence), one fascicle; translated by the Śramaṇa Zhú Tánwúlán of the Western Regions during the Eastern Jin dynasty. Also known as *Weide tuoluoni zhong shuo jing* (Sūtra Spoken within the Vīrya-dhāraṇī) or *Zhengfa gongjing jing* (Sūtra on Reverence for the True Dharma).

Five sheets. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Buddhayaśas of India during the Northern Wei dynasty. *Shan jing jing* (Sūtra on Good Reverence), one fascicle; also named *Shan gongjing jing* (Sūtra on Good Reverence) or *Shan gongjing shi jing* (Sūtra on the Teacher of Good Reverence).

Seven sheets. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta and others of India during the Sui dynasty. *Chengzan dasheng gongde jing* (Sūtra Praising the Merits of the Mahāyāna), one fascicle. Five sheets.
*The Sutra on the Definitive Karmic Obstructions Spoken by the Buddha*, translated by Xuanzang of the Tang Dynasty, one fascicle, three sheets.
Translated by the Śramaṇa Shi Zhiyan of Zhixiang Monastery during the Tang Dynasty. These twenty-three sutras, totaling twenty-four fascicles, are bound together in the same volume.
*The Scripture on Admonishing the King*, one fascicle; also titled *The Greater and Lesser Scriptures on Admonishing the King*, four sheets;
translated by the Song layman Juqu Jingsheng. *The Scripture on the Tathāgata’s Instruction to King Jayasena*, one fascicle;

also titled *The Scripture on King Jayasena*, ten sheets; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang. *The Scripture on the Buddha’s Explanation of the Royal Law to Devānām Indra*, one fascicle; also simply titled *The Scripture on Devānām Indra*, seven sheets.
*Mahāvaipulya-sūtra-rāja-sūtra*, one fascicle, translated by Tripiṭaka Master Yijing of the Tang;
alternatively, without the character "rāja" (king), two sheets, translated by Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci of India during the Northern Wei;
*Parivarta-sūtra*, one fascicle, three sheets, translated by Tripiṭaka Master Buddhasanta of India during the Northern Wei; *Mañjuśrī-caryā-sūtra*, one fascicle, five sheets.
*Mañjuśrī-caryā-sūtra*, one fascicle, eight sheets; translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci during the Northern Wei dynasty.
*Sūtra on Contemplating the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination under the Palm-leaf Tree*, one fascicle; also known as the *Sūtra on Hearing the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination in the City*;
four sheets; translated by the Yuezhi Upāsaka Zhi Qian during the Wu dynasty. *Sūtra on the Noble Path of Dependent Origination*, one fascicle, eight sheets.
*Śālistamba-sūtra*, one fascicle, seven pages; translated by Tripitaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang dynasty;
translator lost, now appended to the catalogue of the Eastern Jin. *Siddhārthasiddhi-sūtra*, one fascicle, five pages;

translated by the Upāsaka Zhi Qian of Yuezhi during the Wu dynasty. *Pratijñāsamādhi-sūtra*, one fascicle; a note beneath the title states: "The fourth chapter, 'Sole Realization,' extracted from the 'Pure Conduct of Bhikṣus' [section], eight pages."
