*The Sūtra of the Dragon King of the Ocean*, four fascicles (or three), seventy-three sheets;

translated by the Western Jin Tripiṭaka Master Zhu Fahu; two translations, one extant. *The Śūraṅgama Samādhi Sūtra*, three fascicles (or two); also simply called the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*. According to Sengyou’s catalogue, it is the *New Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, fifty-two sheets.

Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin dynasty; the ninth translation. *The Sūtra on the Method of Practice of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra* (also known as the *Sūtra on the Profound Merits*, or sometimes omitting the characters "Method of Practice";

also known as the *Samantabhadra Contemplation Sūtra*), one fascicle, sixteen sheets. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmamitra of Kasmira during the Song dynasty; the third translation. *The Sūtra on the Contemplation of the Two Bodhisattvas Bhaiṣajyarāja and Bhaiṣajyasamudgata*, one fascicle, nineteen sheets.

Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kuṅ-lāng-ye-she from the Western Regions during the Song dynasty; the third translation. Two translations are missing. *The Sūtra on the Questions of the Bodhisattva Acintyaprabha* (also known as the *Sūtra Spoken by the Bodhisattva Acintyaprabha*, or the *Sūtra of the Child-like Bodhisattva Acintyaprabha*), one fascicle, twelve sheets.

Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin Dynasty. Second translation; one of the two translations is missing. The first five scriptures, totaling ten fascicles, are in the same volume. *The Scripture on the Ten Abodes and Severing the Bonds* (Shí zhù duàn jié jīng), ten fascicles.

Also known as *The Scripture on the Bodhisattva’s Ten Abodes for Removing Defilements and Severing Bonds Spoken by the Most Victorious One* (Zuìshèng wèn púsà shí zhù chú gòu duàn jié jīng), or *The Samādhi of Ten Thousand Sunlight Rays* (Shí qiān rìguāng sānmèi dìng); also called *The Scripture on the Ten Grounds and Severing the Bonds* (Shí dì duàn jié jīng). It consists of either eleven or fourteen fascicles and contains two hundred fifty-four *qí*. Translated by the Śramaṇa Zhu Fonian of Liangzhou during the Yao Qin Dynasty. Second translation; one of the two translations is missing. *The Essential Collection of All Buddhas* (Zhū fó yào jí jīng), two fascicles. Also simply called *The Essential Collection* (Yào jí jīng). In Indic [language], it is called *Buddha-saṃgha-ṭī*; it consists of forty-three sheets.

Translated by the Tripitaka Master Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin Dynasty, the first translation; one of two translations, the other being missing: *The Sūtra on the Unprecedented Causes and Conditions*, three fascicles. [Preface] by the śrāmaṇera Dhararohu, forty sheets.

Translated by the Śramaṇa Shi Tanjing of the Xiao Qi Dynasty, the second translation; one of two translations, the other being missing. The aforementioned three sūtras comprise fourteen fascicles in a single volume.

*The Bodhisattva’s Necklace Sūtra* (Pusa yingluo jing), twelve fascicles—also known as *The Sūtra of Present Retribution*—alternatively in fourteen, sixteen, or thirteen fascicles, totaling three hundred and thirty-one sheets; translated by the Śramaṇa Zhu Fonian of Liangzhou during the Yao Qin dynasty. Second translation: [one of the two missing]. *The Sūtra of the Samādhi of Transcending the Sun’s Radiance* (Chaoriming sanmei jing), two fascicles—or simply called *The Sūtra of Transcending the Sun’s Radiance*—alternatively in three fascicles, forty-eight sheets; translated by the lay devotee Nie Chengyuan of the Western Jin dynasty. Second translation: [one of the two missing]. The above two sūtras comprise fourteen fascicles in two volumes.

*Xiánjié jīng* (Sūtra of the Auspicious Kalpa), thirteen fascicles; the title is given as *Báttuójié sānmèi* (Samādhi of the Auspicious Kalpa); translated during the Jin dynasty as the *Xiánjié dìngyì jīng* (Sūtra on the Concentration of the Auspicious Kalpa). Old catalogs list it as the *Xiánjié sānmèi jīng* (Sūtra of the Samādhi of the Auspicious Kalpa) in either ten or seven fascicles, comprising one bundle of one hundred and ninety-two sheets. Translated by the Tripitaka Master Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin. Of the two translations, one is missing. *Mahāyāna Sūtras Translated Individually*: One hundred and thirty-one works in two hundred and ninety-three fascicles, arranged in twenty-four bundles. *Mahādharma-ulka-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, twenty fascicles, two bundles, totaling three hundred and ninety-eight sheets. *Mahātejas-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, twenty fascicles, two bundles, totaling two hundred and sixty-eight sheets. The above two sūtras were translated by the Tripitaka Master Jñānagupta and others of India during the Sui dynasty.

*The Scripture on the Names of Buddhas*, twelve fascicles (alternatively stated as thirteen fascicles, or divided into twenty fascicles), totaling two hundred and fifty-three pages; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci of India during the Northern Wei dynasty. *The Scripture on the Names of Three Thousand Buddhas of the Three Kalpas*, three fascicles—comprising the Upper Section on the *Vyuṣṭa-kalpa*, the Middle Section on the *Bhadrakalpa*, and the Lower Section on the *Tārakakalpa*—totaling fifty-nine pages. Translator unknown; currently appended to the Liang dynasty catalog. The above two scriptures comprise fifteen fascicles in two volumes: the upper volume contains seven fascicles, and the lower volume contains eight.

*The Sutra of the Names of Five Thousand Five Hundred Buddhas*, eight fascicles, one hundred thirty-one pages; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta and others of Central India during the Sui Dynasty. *The Sutra on the Inconceivable Merits and the Protection of All Buddhas*, two fascicles—or alternatively titled simply *The Sutra of Inconceivable Merits*—or four fascicles, thirty-seven pages; translated during the Cao Wei period, the name of the Tripiṭaka Master being lost. These ten supplementary volumes are included with the aforementioned two sutras, totaling ten fascicles in a single bundle.

*Huashou jing* (Flower Hand Sūtra), thirteen fascicles—also titled *Shezhushangen jing* (Sūtra on Gathering All Roots of Goodness) or *Shezhufudejing* (Sūtra on Gathering All Merits)—alternatively in eleven, twelve, or ten fascicles; one volume, two hundred twenty-nine sheets;

translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin dynasty. *Dafangdeng tuoluoni jing* (Mahāvaipulya Dhāraṇī Sūtra), four fascicles—also titled *Fangdeng tanchi tuoluoni jing* (Mahāvaipulya Dāna-dhāraṇī Sūtra) or simply without the character "da" (great);

sixty-three sheets; translated by the monk Fakhuan of the Northern Liang dynasty at Gaochang Commandery. *Sengqiezhaji jing* (Saṃghāṭa Sūtra), four fascicles; fifty-one sheets; recorded in the *Baochang lu*.
*The Scripture on the Samādhi of the Array of Power*, translated by Prince Yueposhouna of the Kingdom of Ujjayinī during the Northern Wei dynasty, three fascicles, thirty-eight pages;

*The Scripture on the Definitive Meaning of the Mahāvaipulya Perfect Enlightenment Sūtra*, translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Narendrayaśas during the Sui dynasty, one fascicle, twenty-seven pages;

and *The Scripture on the Mahāvaipulya Perfect Enlightenment*, translated by the Śramaṇa Buddhatoṭara of Kaśmīra during the Tang dynasty, one fascicle. These four scriptures, totaling twelve fascicles, are bound together in the same volume.

*The Sutra on the Ocean-like Samādhi of Contemplating the Buddha*, ten fascicles (alternatively titled *The Sutra on the Samādhi of Contemplating the Buddha*, or eight fascicles), one bundle, 156 sheets; translated by the Tripitaka Master Buddhabhadra of India during the Eastern Jin dynasty. *The Sutra on the Great Expedient Means of the Buddha’s Requital of Kindness*, seven fascicles, 126 sheets; translator lost, included in the Later Han records. *The Sutra on the Original Acts of the Bodhisattva*, three fascicles, 47 sheets; translator lost, now appended to the Eastern Jin records. These two sutras, totaling ten fascicles, are contained in the same bundle as the preceding works.

*The Scripture on the Collection of Dharmas* (Dharmasaṃgīti-sūtra), six fascicles, or seven fascicles, or eight fascicles, totaling one hundred twenty-seven pages; translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci during the Northern Wei dynasty. *The Scripture on the Contemplation of the Practice of All Dharmas*, four fascicles, sixty-three pages; translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta and others during the Sui dynasty. These two scriptures comprise ten fascicles in a single volume.

The *Bodhisattva-uccha-tai-jing* (Sutra on the Bodhisattva Dwelling in the Womb) in five fascicles; the first states that the Bodhisattva descended from Tuṣita Heaven into his mother’s womb and preached the *Puguang jing* (Universal Extensiveness Sutra), also simply called the *Tai jing* (Womb Sutra). It exists in versions of eight fascicles or four fascicles, totaling one hundred and fifteen scrolls. Translated by the Śramaṇa Zhu Fonian of Liangzhou during the Yao Qin dynasty. The *Hongdao guangxian sanmei jing* (Sutra on the Samādhi of the Broad Manifestation of the Propagation of the Way) in four fascicles; also titled *Anouda Longwang Suowen Juezhu Xuyi Qingjing* (Pure Questions of the Dragon King Anavatapta Resolving All Doubts), or *Rujingang Wen Dingyi jing* (Entering the Diamond Questioning the Concentrated Mind Sutra). It consists of twelve chapters and is either in two fascicles or fifty-five sheets. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin dynasty. The *Shideng Gongde jing* (Sutra on the Merit of Offering Lamps) in one fascicle; also titled *Ran deng jing* (Lighting Lamps Sutra). Fifteen sheets. Translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Narendrayaśas of the Northern Qi dynasty. The above three sutras comprise ten fascicles and are contained in the same volume.

*The Aṅgulimālīya Sūtra*, four fascicles, seventy-eight pages; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Guṇabhadra of India during the Song dynasty. *The Sarvābhavasa Bodhisattva Sūtra*, four fascicles, sixty-two pages; translated by the Tripiṭaka Masters Jñānagupta and others of India during the Sui dynasty. *The Pañcāśatsāhasrikā-prajñāpāramitā-parīkṣā Sūtra*, two fascicles, forty pages (sometimes the title lacks "Prajñāpāramitā" or the characters "fifty"); translated by the Tripiṭaka Master An Shigao of Parthia during the Later Han dynasty. These three sūtras comprise ten fascicles in one volume.

*Zhongyin jing* (Sūtra on the Intermediate State), two fascicles, twenty-eight sheets; translated by the Śramaṇa Zhu Fonian of Liangzhou during the Yao Qin dynasty. *Dafagujing* (Great Dharma Drum Sūtra), two fascicles, thirty-one sheets; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Guṇabhadra of India during the Song dynasty. *Wenshushili wenjing* (Sūtra of Mañjuśrī’s Questions), also simply called *Wenwu wenjing*, two fascicles, fifty-one sheets; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Saṃghavarman of Funan during the Liang dynasty. *Yueyang nü jing* (Sūtra of the Girl Candrottarā), also known as *Weimojie zhi nü*, two fascicles, nineteen sheets; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta et al. of India during the Sui dynasty. *Tathāgataguhyakośasūtra* (Sūtra of the Tathāgata’s Secret Treasury), two fascicles, twenty-four sheets; translator lost, now appended to the records of the Qin dynasty. These five sūtras comprise ten fascicles and are contained in the same volume.

The *Mahāyāna-Ghanavyūha-sūtra* (Dense Array Sutra), three fascicles, fifty-six sheets; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Divākara. The *Sūtra on Examining the Retribution of Good and Evil Karma*, two fascicles, also titled the *Mahāyāna-Satyārtha-sūtra*; excerpted from the *Ṣaḍindriya-rāśi-sūtra* (Sutra on the Aggregate of the Six Faculties) or simply called the *Karma-Parīkṣā-sūtra*; also titled the *Kṣitigarbha-bodhisattva-sūtra*, twenty-eight sheets; translated by the foreign śramaṇa Bodhimitra. The *Padmavaktra-sūtra* (Lotus Face Sutra), two fascicles, twenty-three sheets; translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Narendrayaśas during the Sui dynasty. The *Mañjuśrī-paripṛcchā-bodhisattva-caryā-sūtra*, one fascicle, also known as the *Mañjuśrī-paripṛcchā-caryā-sūtra*, twenty sheets; translated by Lokakṣema. The *Mahāyāna-Buddhapratimā-lakṣaṇa-puṇya-sūtra* (Sutra on the Merit of Making Buddha Images), two fascicles, or one fascicle, twenty-one sheets; translated by Ti-yun Prajñā of Khotan. The above five sutras, totaling ten fascicles, are contained in the same volume.

The *Mahāvaipulya-mahāratna-kūṭāgāra-susthitaguhyadhāraṇī-sūtra* in three fascicles and forty sheets; the *Ekākṣara-uṣṇīṣacakravartin-tantra* in five fascicles—also known as the *Pañca-uṣṇīṣa-sūtra*—or in four fascicles and two hundred twenty-one sheets. These two aforementioned sūtras were translated by Bodhiruci.

*The Scripture on the One-Syllable Heart Mantra of the Great Dhāraṇī for the Age of Dharma*, one fascicle, fourteen pages; translated by Baosiwei. These three preceding scriptures comprise nine fascicles in a single volume.

The *Mahābuddhōṣṇīṣa-tathāgataguhyahetupratipattinirdeśa-sarvabodhisattvasamyaksaṃsiddhi-śūraṅgama-sūtra*, ten fascicles, one volume, one hundred and forty-three pages; translated by the śramaṇa Huaidi. The *Mahāvairocanābhisambodhi-vikurvāṇa-adhiṣṭhāna-sūtra*, seven fascicles, also called the *Mahāvairocanābhisambodhi-sūtra*, one hundred and thirty-five pages; translated by the śramaṇa Yi-hsing. The *Subāhuparipṛcchā-sūtra*, three fascicles, also called the *Subāhu-paripṛcchā*, or the *Subāhu-vinaya*, or simply the *Subāhu*, in two fascicles, forty-nine pages; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śubhakarasiṃha. The above two sūtras, totaling ten fascicles, are contained in the same volume.

*Susiddhikara Sūtra*, three fascicles, ninety-one sheets; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śubhakarasiṃha. *Mūlamandala-dhāraṇī Sūtra*, one fascicle (sometimes the word "sūtra" is omitted), thirty-three sheets; translator lost. *Kongōchō Yugasho Ryakushutsunenju-hō* (The Ritual for Recitation Briefly Extracted from the Vajraśekhara Yoga), four fascicles, also called a sūtra, eighty-one sheets; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Vajrabodhi. These three aforementioned sūtras comprise eight fascicles in a single volume.

*The Scripture on the Divine Spells Spoken by the Seven Buddhas*, four fascicles; the first fascicle states it is the *Great Dhāraṇī Divine Spell Scripture Spoken by the Seven Buddhas and Eleven Bodhisattvas*, seventy-three pages. Translated during the Jin dynasty, the name of the Tripiṭaka Master is lost. *The Scripture on the Great Auspicious Meaning Divine Spell*, two fascicles (or four fascicles), thirty-one pages. Translated by Tanyao. *The Mañjuśrī-ratnagarbha-dhāraṇī Scripture*, one fascicle. *The Vajrajvālā-wind-and-rain-stopping-dhāraṇī Scripture*, thirty-one pages. These two aforementioned scriptures were translated by Bodhiruci.

*The Āṭavaka Mahāyakṣasenāpati Buddha-dhāraṇī Sūtra*, one fascicle (also simply titled *The Āṭavaka Dhāraṇī Sūtra*), five sheets; *The Amitābha Dundubhisvara-rāja Dhāraṇī Sūtra*, one fascicle, four sheets; *The Great Samantabhadra Dhāraṇī Sūtra*, one fascicle, three sheets; *The Great Saptaratna Dhāraṇī Sūtra*, one fascicle, one sheet; *The Six-Syllable Great Dhāraṇī Mantra Sūtra*, one fascicle, two sheets. These five sūtras above were lost in translation and are now appended to the Liang dynasty catalog.

*Anzhai shenzhou jing* (Sutra of the Spirit-Mantra for Securing a Dwelling), one fascicle; also called *Anzhai zhufa* (Methods for Securing a Dwelling with Mantras), four sheets. Translated during the Later Han dynasty by an unknown translator. *Mani luodan jing* (Sutra of Maṇilabdha), one fascicle; also called *Mani luodan shenzhou jing* (Sutra of the Spirit-Mantra of Maṇilabdha), four sheets. *Huanshi bati suoshuo shenzhou jing* (Sutra of the Spirit-Mantra Spoken by the Illusionist Bhadra), one fascicle. The catalogue states that the character "wu" (no) should be read as "ba" (Bha); it is also written as "Ba" or "Bo. It was formerly called the *Lü huanwang badu jing* (Sutra of the Illusion-King Bhadra), two sheets. The above two sutras were translated by the śramaṇa Zhu Tanwulan.

*The Dhāraṇī Sūtra for Protecting All Boys*, one fascicle; also known as *The Dhāraṇī Sūtra for Requesting Sons and Daughters by Protecting All Boys*, four sheets. Translated by Bodhiruci of the Northern Wei. *The Dhāraṇī Sūtra of the Heart of All Buddhas*, one fascicle, three sheets. *The Dhāraṇī Sūtra for Deliverance from Suffering and Calamity*, one fascicle, three sheets. *The Dhāraṇī Sūtra of the Eight Names of Universal Secrecy*, one fascicle, two sheets. *The Dhāraṇī Sūtra of Sustaining the World*, one fascicle, four sheets. *The Dhāraṇī Sūtra of the Six Gates*, one fascicle, one sheet. The above five sūtras were translated by Xuanzang of the Tang dynasty.

*The Sutra of the Dhāraṇī of the Pure Avalokiteśvara Samantabhadra*, one fascicle. There is a mistaken version of this sutra which must be carefully examined; it consists of five sheets. Translated by the Tang monk Zhìtōng. The aforementioned nineteen sutras comprise twenty-three fascicles in a single volume.
The *Jñānolkā-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, one fascicle, three pages; the *Sarvabuddhasamāyoga-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, one fascicle, four pages. The two sūtras above were translated by Divākara during the Tang dynasty.

*The Sūtra of the Great Sovereign Dhāraṇī-Mantra for Attaining Whatever is Sought*, one fascicle; also titled *Attaining Whatever is Sought*, fourteen sheets. Translated by Baosiwei of the Tang Dynasty. *The Dhāraṇī of the Hundred Thousand Seals*, one fascicle, two sheets. *The Dhāraṇī-Mantra for Saving the Face-Burning Hungry Ghosts*, one fascicle; also titled *The Sūtra of the Mantra for Bestowing Food upon Hungry Ghosts*. This is followed by the *Mantra for Bestowing Water*, four sheets. These two aforementioned sūtras were translated by Śikṣānanda of the Tang Dynasty.

*The Dhāraṇī Sūtra of King Adornment*, one fascicle, four sheets; *The Dhāraṇī Sūtra of the Bodhisattva Gandharāja*, one fascicle, two sheets; *The Sūtra of the King Adorned with All Merits*, one fascicle, fourteen sheets; *The Dhāraṇī King Sūtra for Eradicating Karmic Obstructions*, one fascicle, three sheets; *The Sūtra of the Auspicious Night*, one fascicle, three sheets. The above five sūtras were translated by Yi Jing of the Tang dynasty.

*The Scripture on the Dhāraṇī of the Supreme Mind for Fulfilling All Vows of the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha and the Method for Seeking the Power of Hearing and Retention*, one fascicle; also titled *The Scripture on the Method for the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha to Seek the Power of Hearing and Retention*, four sheets. Translated by Śubhakarasiṃha of the Tang. *The Chapter on the Five-Syllable Heart Dhāraṇī of Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva from the Vajraśekhara Sūtra*, one fascicle, eleven sheets. *The Essential Yoga Methods of Avalokiteśvara and Cintāmaṇicakra Bodhisattva*, one fascicle, nine sheets. The two scriptures above were translated by Vajrabodhi of the Tang.
*The Sūtra on the Buddha Ground*, one fascicle, thirteen pages;

translated by Xuanzang of the Tang dynasty. *The Sūtra Briefly Explaining the Instructions Given by the Buddha as He Was About to Enter Parinirvāṇa*, one fascicle; also known as *The Sūtra on the Buddha’s Imminent Parinirvāṇa* or *The Sūtra of the Bequeathed Teaching*, six pages;
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin dynasty. *Sūtra on the Arising of the Bodhicitta*, one fascicle, eleven pages.
*The Sūtra on the Samādhi of the Buddha-Seal*, translated by Śikṣānanda and others of the Sui dynasty; one fascicle, three sheets.
*The Sūtra of Mañjuśrī’s Parinirvāṇa*, translated during the Han dynasty by An Shigao; one fascicle, four sheets.

*The Sūtra of the Extraordinary Account of the Bodhisattva’s Past Deeds*, translated by the layman Nie Daozhen of the Western Jin dynasty; one fascicle, eleven sheets (sometimes the character "past" [本] is omitted).
*Qianfo yinyuan jing* (Sūtra on the Causes and Conditions of the Thousand Buddhas), one fascicle, eighteen sheets; translated by Nie Daozhen of the Western Jin.
*Xianshou jing* (Sūtra of the Worthy Head), one fascicle—also titled *Xianshou furen jing* (Sūtra of the Worthy Head Lady)—three sheets; translated by Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin.

*Yueming pusa jing* (Sūtra of the Bodhisattva Moon-Brightness), one fascicle—sometimes the word "samādhi" is added [to the title], or it is called *Yueming tongzi jing* (Sūtra of the Youth Moon-Brightness), also known as *Yueming tongnan jing* (Sūtra of the Boy Moon-Brightness)—three sheets; translated by Shi Shengjian of the Qifu Qin.

*The Scripture on the Heart-Illumination* (Cixin jing), one fascicle, translated by the Yuezhi Upāsaka Zhi Qian of Wu; also known as *The Scripture on the Brahmin Woman’s Offering of Rice Gruel to the Heart-Illumination Maiden*, three sheets. *The Scripture on the Extinction of Darkness in the Ten Directions* (Mie shifang ming jing), one fascicle; also called *The Scripture on the Ten Directions’ Extinction of Darkness*, six sheets. *The Scripture on the Mother of the Deer* (Lumujing), one fascicle. There is another work, *The Scripture on the Fawn* (Luzijing), one fascicle, which is identical to this one, consisting of three sheets. *The Scripture on Māra’s Rebellion* (Mo ni jing), one fascicle, nineteen sheets. The above four scriptures were translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin.

The twenty-six scriptures above comprise twenty-six fascicles in one bundle. *The Scripture of Prince Śrīprabha* (1 fascicle), also known as *The Scripture on the Questions of Prince Śrīprabha by Rāṣṭrapāla*;

19 sheets. Translated by Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin. *The Scripture of the Great Meaning* (1 fascicle); 5 sheets. Translated by Guṇabhadra of the Song. *The Scripture of the Firm Woman* (1 fascicle), also known as *The Scripture of the Solid Woman*; 6 sheets. Translated by Narendrayaśas of the Sui. *The Scripture of the Questions of the Devaputra Śreṣṭhī* (1 fascicle), sometimes lacking the characters "Questions" (*wu suo wen*); 17 sheets. *The Scripture of the Supreme King of All Dharmas* (1 fascicle); 23 sheets. The two scriptures above were translated by Jñānagupta and others of the Sui.

*The Sūtra of the Questions of the Bodhisattva Siṃhavikrīḍitarāja*, one fascicle (also known as *The Eight Maṇḍalas*), five sheets; *The Sūtra of the Questions of the Bodhisattva Vimalamati on the Paying Homage to the Buddha Dharma*, one fascicle, six sheets. Both of the above sūtras were translated by Nadi during the Tang dynasty.

*The Sūtra on the Merit Arising from Upholding the Names of the Seven Buddhas*, one fascicle, four pages; *The Sūtra on the Buddha’s Record of the Dharma’s Abiding at the Time of His Parinirvāṇa* (sometimes titled with the character "parinirvāṇa" added), one fascicle, five pages; *The Sūtra on the Samādhi of Silent Illumination and Divine Transformation*, one fascicle, sixteen pages. The above three sūtras were translated by Xuanzang of the Tang dynasty.

*Chamapati-juriki-kyō* (Sūtra on the Prophecy for Chamapati), one fascicle, three pages; *Fuzōfugengyō* (Sūtra on Neither Increasing nor Decreasing), one fascicle—though some say it is two fascicles, which is an error—or seven pages and more. These two sūtras were translated by Bodhiruci during the Northern Wei dynasty.

*The Sūtra on the Merit of Constructing Stūpas*, one fascicle, two sheets; translated by Divākara of the Tang dynasty. *The Sūtra on the Merit of Circumambulating Buddha Stūpas*, one fascicle, also titled *The Sūtra on the Merit of Circumambulating Stūpas*, three sheets. *The Mahāyāna Sūtra of the Four Dharmas*, one fascicle, eight sheets; although the titles are identical to those found in the re-translated version by Dānapāla, the textual body is entirely different. These two sūtras above were translated by Śikṣānanda of the Tang dynasty.

*The Mahāyāna Sūtra on the Questions of the Virtuous Woman*, one fascicle. At one time there was a single copy consisting of eight or nine sheets; the text was erroneous and unfit for use [for four sheets]. Translated by Bodhiruci of the Tang dynasty. *The Mahāyāna Sūtra on the Flowing Through of All Existences*, one fascicle, three sheets. *The Sūtra on the Causes and Conditions of King Wondrous Color*, one fascicle, four sheets. *The Sūtra on the Seal of the Dharma Spoken by the Buddha for the Naga King Sāgara*, one fascicle, one sheet. The above three sūtras were translated by Yi Jing of the Tang dynasty.

*The Sūtra on King Siṃhasauḍasa’s Prohibition of Meat*, one fascicle, four pages; translated by the Tang dynasty monk Shi Zhiyan. *The Sūtra on the Offering of Wax after the Parinirvāṇa*, one fascicle—also titled *The Sūtra on the Offering of Wax for the Four Classes after the Parinirvāṇa*, or simply *The Sūtra on the Offering of Wax*—two pages; translated by Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin. *The Sūtra of the Names of Eight Buddhas*, one fascicle—also titled *The Sūtra of the Names of the Eight Buddhas*—three pages; translated by Prajñāruci of the Northern Wei. The above twenty-two sūtras comprise twenty-two fascicles in one volume.

*The Bodhisattva’s Internal Practice of the Six Pāramitās Sūtra*, one fascicle; alternatively titled *The Internal Six Pāramitās Sūtra*. Master An states it was extracted from the Vaipulya section. Three sheets. Translated by Yan Fotiao of the Han dynasty. *Bodhisattva Throws Himself to a Starving Tiger and Erects a Stūpa: The因缘 (nidāna) Sūtra*, one fascicle. Sengyou’s catalogue records it as *The Sūtra on Giving One’s Body to a Starving Tiger*, eleven sheets. Translated by Shi Fasheng of Northern Liang. *The Vajrasamādhi Sūtra on the Innate Purity, Indestructibility, and Non-extinction*, one fascicle; also titled *The Vajra-Purity Sūtra*. Eight sheets. *The Sūtra on the Past Life of Buddha Siṃhacandra*, one fascicle. Seven sheets. The two sūtras above were lost in translation and are now appended to the Qin records.
*The Sūtra on the Wife of the Elder Dharmakāla*, one fascicle, three sheets;
translator lost, now appended to the Liang catalogue. *The Sūtra of the Kingdom of Sālā*, one fascicle—also called *The Sūtra of the King of Sālā*—four sheets;
translator lost, now appended to the Eastern Jin catalogue. *The Sūtra of the Ten Auspiciousnesses*, one fascicle, two sheets.
*The Sūtra on the Lion’s Roar of the Meaning of Ultimate Truth by the Daughter of a Householder, Aṅgulimālā*, one fascicle, six pages; translator lost, now appended to the Qin records.
*The Sūtra on the Causes and Conditions of the Compassionate Heart of the Immortal Sarvajñāprabha and His Abstention from Eating Meat*, one fascicle, five pages;
translator lost, now appended to the Liang records. *The Vajrasamādhi Sūtra*, two fascicles (or one fascicle), twenty-seven pages; translator lost, now appended to the Qin records.

*The Sūtra on the Extinction of the Dharma*, one fascicle (or one fascicle, twenty-seven sheets), translated during the Northern Liang dynasty with the translator lost; *The Sūtra of the Profound and Great Dedication*, one fascicle, four sheets. These two sūtras above were lost translations and are now appended to the Song Catalogue.

*The Scripture of the Crown Prince Piluo of the Heavenly King*, one fascicle; also called *The Scripture of Crown Prince Piluo*, or lacking the characters "Heavenly King. Sengyou’s Catalogue states it consists of two sheets and was among the "extraordinary scriptures from Guanzhong" by Master Dao’an.

*The Scripture on the Dharma-Gate of Pure Conduct for Upāsikās*, two fascicles; also simply called *The Scripture on Pure Conduct*, or lacking the character "Scripture. It consists of thirty-two sheets.
Sengyou’s Catalogue states it was among the "extraordinary scriptures from Liangzhou" by Master Dao’an. *The Scripture on the Eight Great Persons’ Awakening*, one fascicle; one sheet.

*The Sutra on the Three Grades of Disciples*, one fascicle, translated during the Han dynasty by An Shigao; also titled *The Sutra on the Three Classes of Disciples’ Studies*, three sheets. Translated during the Wu dynasty by Zhi Qian of Yuezhi: *The Sutra on the Four Classes*, one fascicle;

also titled *The Sutra on the Four Classes of Disciples* or *The Sutra on the Four Classes of Studies*, three sheets. *The Sutra on Future Transformations*, one fascicle; also titled *The Sutra on Future Transformations and Cognition*, one fascicle. *The Sutra on the Almsround of Past Buddhas*, one fascicle; also titled *The Sutra on Past Ages*, two sheets. The above three sutras were translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin.

*The Scripture on the Twelve Dhūtas*, one fascicle—also known as *The Scripture on the Dhūtas of the Śramaṇa*—five sheets; *The Scripture on Jyotiṣka*, one fascicle—three sheets. Both of the above scriptures were translated by Guṇabhadra of the Song dynasty.

The *Rājarṣi-āyuṣmat-sūtra*, one fascicle, six sheets; the *Dharmasthititā-sūtra*, one fascicle, two sheets. These two sūtras above were lost to translation and are now appended to the Western Jin catalogue.
The twenty-three sūtras totaling twenty-five fascicles above are contained in the same volume.

Mahāyāna Vinaya: twenty-six works in fifty-four fascicles, arranged in five bundles. *Bodhisattvabhūmiviniścayasamgrahaṇī* (Treatise on the Stages of Bodhisattva Practice), ten fascicles—or without the word "sūtra"—also called a *śāstra*, or the *Bodhisattva-śīla-sūtra*; also known as the *Bodhisattvabhūmi*. It consists of eight fascicles in one bundle, totaling one hundred and eighty-six sheets. Translated by Dharmakṣema during the Northern Liang dynasty. *Bodhisattvabhadraśīla-sūtra*, nine fascicles; also titled the *Bodhisattvabhūmi*, ten fascicles, totaling one hundred and eighty sheets. Translated by Guṇavarman and others during the Song dynasty. *Śuddhakarmāvaraṇa-sūtra*, one fascicle, fifteen sheets. Translator lost; currently appended to the records of the Qin dynasty. The above two sūtras, totaling ten fascicles, share the same bundle.

The *Upāsaka-śīla-sūtra* in seven fascicles, or five, or six, or ten fascicles; the Bodhisattva precepts for laypeople, totaling one hundred thirty-one pages. Translated by Dharmakṣema of the Northern Liang. The *Brahmajāla-sūtra* in two fascicles, thirty-six pages. Translated by Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin. The *Sūtra on Receiving the Ten Good Precepts* in one fascicle, sixteen pages. Translated during the Han dynasty, translator lost. These three aforementioned sūtras comprise ten fascicles in a single volume.

*The Sutra on the Original Action of the Bodhisattva’s Diadem* (Bodhisattvamaṇḍadhyāna-mūlakarman-sūtra), two fascicles; alternatively titled simply *The Sutra on the Original Action of the Diadem*, thirty-nine sheets. Translated by Zhu Fonian of the Yao Qin dynasty. *The Buddha-treasury Sutra* (Buddhapiṭaka-sūtra), four fascicles—also known as the *Sutra on the Selection of All Dharmas*; alternatively three or two fascicles, seventy sheets. Translated by Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin dynasty. *Bodhisattva Precept Text* (Bodhisattva-śīla-mūla), one fascicle, eleven sheets. Translated by Dharmakṣema of the Northern Liang dynasty. *Bodhisattva Precept Karma Text* (Bodhisattva-śīla-karman-vinaya), one fascicle, six sheets. The above two sutras were translated by Xuanzang of the Tang dynasty.

*Bodhisattva-śīla-sūtra*, one fascicle; *Upāli-paripṛcchā-bodhisattva-upasaṃpadā-dharma*, fifteen sheets. Translated by Guṇavarman of the Song dynasty. These six sūtras, totaling ten fascicles, are contained in the same volume.

The *Bodhisattva-antarashīla-sūtra*, one fascicle, eighteen sheets; the *Upāsaka-pañcaśīla-vinaya-sūtra*, one fascicle, fifteen sheets. These two aforementioned sūtras were translated by Guṇavarman of the Song dynasty.
*Mañjuśrī-viśuddha-śīla-sūtra*, one fascicle (also simply titled *Viśuddha-śīla-sūtra*), thirteen sheets;
translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin. *Viśuddha-vinaya-vaipulya-sūtra*, one fascicle, seventeen sheets;
translated by Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin. *Prasannaruta-paripṛcchā-sūtra*, one fascicle—also known as the *Tathāgata-bhāṣita-viśuddha-vinaya-sūtra*—eighteen sheets.
*Mahāyāna Tri-saṃvara-pāpadeśanā Sūtra*, one fascicle, thirteen sheets; translated by the Song dynasty monk Fǎhǎi.
*Bodhisattva Pañca-dharma-pāpadeśanā*, one fascicle—also titled *Bodhisattva Pañca-dharma-pāpadeśanā Sūtra*, two sheets; translated by Jñānagupta and others of the Sui dynasty.
*Lost Translator*, now appended to the Liang dynasty catalog: *Bodhisattvapitaka Sūtra*, one fascicle, ten sheets.

*Samantabhadra-bodhisattva-sūtra*, one fascicle, three pages, translated by Saṃghavarman of the Liang dynasty. *Bodhisattva-śīla-upavāsa-sūtra*, one fascicle, three pages. The two sūtras above were translated by Nie Daozhen of the Western Jin dynasty.

*Mañjuśrī-paṭikarman-sūtra*, one fascicle—also titled *Mañjuśrī-pañcāṅga-sāgara-paṭikarman-sūtra*, twenty-one sheets; translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin. *Śāriputra-paṭikarman-sūtra*, one fascicle—also simply titled *Paṭikarman-sūtra*, five sheets; translated by An Shigao of the Han dynasty. *Dharmapada-samādhi-sūtra*, one fascicle—also simply titled *Dharmapada-sūtra*, seven sheets; translated by Zhi Qian of the Wu dynasty. *Daśakuśala-karmapatha-sūtra*, one fascicle, six sheets; translated by Śikṣānanda of the Tang dynasty. The above fourteen sūtras, comprising fourteen fascicles, are bound together in one volume.

Mahāyāna Treatises: 97 works, 518 fascicles, in 50 bundles; 11 works, 155 fascicles, which are commentaries on sūtras; 76 works, 363 fascicles, which are treatises collecting essential meanings. *Mahāprajñāpāramitā-śāstra*: 100 fascicles (alternatively said to be 110 fascicles or 70 fascicles), in 10 bundles, totaling 285 sheets.

The *Daśabhūmika-vibhāṣā-śāstra* (Treatise on the Ten Stages Sutra), translated by Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin dynasty, in twelve fascicles or fifteen fascicles, one volume, 246 sheets; the *Maitreya-paripṛcchā-sūtra-śāstra*, in five fascicles, six fascicles, seven fascicles, or eight fascicles, 128 sheets; and the *Mahāratnakūṭa-sūtra-śāstra*, in four fascicles, 84 sheets. The three aforementioned scriptures were translated by Bodhiruci of the Northern Wei dynasty.

*The Commentary on the Sūtra of the Four Dharmas of the Bodhisattva Ratnaśikhin*, one fascicle; translated by Vimokṣaprajña of the Northern Wei. The three preceding treatises comprise ten fascicles in one volume.

*Buddhabhūmi-sūtra-śāstra*, seven fascicles, one hundred and seventeen sheets; translated by Xuanzang of the Tang. *Vajracchedikā-prajñāpāramitā-sūtra-śāstra*, two fascicles, composed by Bodhisattva Asaṅga, thirty sheets; translated by Jñānagupta of the Sui. *Vajracchedikā-prajñāpāramitā-sūtra-śāstra-kārikā*, one fascicle—also known as the *Vajracchedikā-śāstra-kārikā*—four sheets; translated by Yijing of the Tang. The three preceding treatises comprise ten fascicles in one volume.
*Vajracchedikā-prajñāpāramitā-sūtra-śāstra*, three fascicles, composed by Bodhisattva Vasubandhu;
forty-eight sheets; translated by Bodhiruci during the Northern Wei dynasty. *Vajracchedikā-prajñāpāramitā-sūtra-śāstra-vyākhyā*, three fascicles, also known as *Vajracchedikā-śāstra-vyākhyā*;

thirty-three sheets; translated by Yijing during the Tang dynasty. *Vajracchedikā-prajñāpāramitā-sūtra-bhaṅga-grahaṇa-anabhiniveśa-akṣaya-prajñapti-śāstra*, two fascicles, also titled *Guṇaprabha-śāstra*; thirty-three sheets.
The *Mañjuśrīparipṛcchābodhicittabhūmi-sūtra-śāstra* in two fascicles, also titled *Mañjuśrīparipṛcchā-bodhicitta-sūtra-śāstra*, alternatively known as the *Gayāśīrṣa-sūtra-śāstra*, thirty sheets;
translated by Bodhiruci during the Northern Wei dynasty. The *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra-upadeśa* in one fascicle, titled *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra-upadeśa*, twenty-five sheets;
translated by Ratnamati together with Senglang and others during the Northern Wei dynasty. These five treatises, totaling eleven fascicles, are bound in the same volume.

The *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra-śāstra* in two fascicles; the initial homage verse may belong to a one-fascicle version, also titled *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra-upadeśa*, consisting of thirty sheets, translated by Bodhiruci of the Northern Wei together with Tanlin and others.
The *Ajātaśatru-paripṛcchā-brahma-deva-paripṛcchā-śāstra* in four fascicles (or three), fifty-nine sheets, translated by Bodhiruci of the Northern Wei.
The *Nirvāṇa-śāstra* in one fascicle (also called the *Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra-śāstra*), ten sheets.

*The Treatise on Verses Concerning "Originally Existing and Now Non-existent"* (Nirvāṇa-sūtra-bhava-abhava-gāthā-śāstra), one fascicle, also simply titled *The Treatise on Originally Existing and Now Non-existence*, six sheets;
translated by the Śramaṇa Dharmaprabha during the Liang dynasty. *The Treatise on the Sutra of the Bequeathed Teaching* (Śāsanānuśāsana-sūtra-śāstra), one fascicle, twenty-six sheets;

translated by Paramārtha during the Chen dynasty. *The Treatise on the Sutra of Immeasurable Life* (Amitāyus-sūtra-śāstra), one fascicle, titled *The Upadeśa of the Sutra of Immeasurable Life: Verses on the Vow for Rebirth*, seven fascicles.
*Tri-sampadā-sūtra-śāstra*, one fascicle, translated by Bodhiruci of the Northern Wei; titled *Tri-sampadā-upadeśa*, eighteen sheets. Translated by Vimokṣasena of the Northern Wei;
*Dharmacakra-pravartana-sūtra-śāstra*, one fascicle, titled *Dharmacakra-pravartana-sūtra-upadeśa*, ten sheets. Translated by Vimokṣasena and others of the Northern Wei.

These eight treatises, totaling twelve fascicles, are contained in the same volume. The above are commentaries on the sūtras (*sūtra-vyākhyāna-śāstra*); the following are compendia of meaning (*artha-saṃgraha-śāstra*).

The *Yogācārabhūmi-śāstra*, one hundred fascicles, ten bundles, one thousand eight hundred and seventeen sheets; the *Prakaraṇāryavācā-śāstra*, twenty fascicles, two bundles, three hundred and twenty-seven sheets; the *Yogācārabhūmi-bhāṣya*, one fascicle, nineteen sheets; the *Prakaraṇāryavācā-kārikā*, one fascicle, nineteen sheets; and the *Rājadharmasamyak-nirdeśa-śāstra*, one fascicle, twenty sheets; the *Mahāyānābhidharma-samuccaya-śāstra*, seven fascicles, one hundred and three sheets—these six works above were translated by Xuanzang of the Tang dynasty.
The four aforementioned treatises comprise ten fascicles in one volume.

The *Mahāyānābhidharmasamuccayavyākhyā* in sixteen fascicles is also called the *Abhidharma-śāstra*, totaling 255 sheets; translated by Xuanzang of the Tang dynasty. The *Mūlamadhyamakakārikā* in four fascicles—also known as the *Madhyamaka-śāstra* or in eight fascicles—totaling 98 sheets; translated by Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin dynasty. The two aforementioned treatises comprise twenty fascicles in two volumes.

The *Prajñāpradīpa-śāstra* (Exegesis on the Lamp of Wisdom), fifteen fascicles, two hundred fifty-one sheets; translated by Prajñāruci of the Tang dynasty. The *Dvādaśamukha-śāstra* (Treatise on the Twelve Gates), one fascicle, twenty-four sheets; translated by Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin dynasty. The *Aṣṭādaśaśūnyatā-śāstra* (Treatise on the Eighteen Emptinesses), one fascicle, twenty sheets; translated by Paramārtha of the Chen dynasty. The *Śata-śāstra* (Treatise in One Hundred Verses), two fascicles, forty-three sheets; translated by Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin dynasty. The *Viśeṣaṇa-śata-śāstra-mūla* (Root Text of the Extended Treatise in One Hundred Verses), one fascicle, eight sheets; translated by Xuanzang of the Tang dynasty. The aforementioned five treatises comprise twenty fascicles in two volumes.

The *Mahāyāna-śataka-vṛtti* (Commentary on the Hundred Verses of the Mahāyāna), ten fascicles, one set, one hundred and ninety sheets; translated by Xuanzang of the Tang dynasty. The *Daśabhūmika-vibhāṣā-śāstra* (Treatise on the Exposition of the Ten Stages), fourteen fascicles—sometimes titled with the character "lun" [treatise], sometimes twelve fascicles, or fifteen fascicles—two hundred and seventy-six sheets; translated by Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin dynasty. The *Bodhicaryāvatāra-saṃgraha-śāstra* (Treatise on the Provisions for Enlightenment), six fascicles, sixty-seven sheets; translated by Dharmagupta of the Sui dynasty. The aforementioned two treatises comprise twenty fascicles and two sets.

*Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra-śāstra*, thirteen fascicles (or fifteen fascicles), one set, two hundred and five sheets; translated by Paramārtha of the Tang dynasty. *Mahāyāna-saṃgraha-śāstra*, fifteen fascicles (or without the word "sūtra," or ten fascicles), two hundred and nine sheets; translated by Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin dynasty. *Madhyamaka-anupraveśa-śāstra*, two fascicles, titled *Madhyamaka-anupraveśa-śāstra-artha-praveśa-devatā-prajñāpāramitā-sūtra-prathama-parivarta-dharmaparyāya*, thirty-two sheets; translated by Prajñāruci of the Northern Wei dynasty. *Mahāyānasaṃgraha-bhāṣya*, three fascicles, fifty-nine sheets; translated by Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha. The above three treatises comprise twenty fascicles in two sets.

*Mahāyānasaṃgraha-śāstra*, two fascicles, forty-four sheets; translated by Buddhayaśas. *Mahāyānasaṃgraha-bhāṣya*, three fascicles, sixty-one sheets; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang. *Mahāyānasaṃgraha-bhāṣya-vyākhyā* (also called *Vyākhyā*), fifteen fascicles—or twelve fascicles—three hundred twenty-seven sheets; commentary by Vasubandhu, translated by Paramārtha. The above three treatises comprise twenty fascicles in two volumes.

*Mahāyānasaṃgrahabhāṣya* (Commentary on the Compendium of the Great Vehicle), ten fascicles, one set, one hundred and fifty-six sheets; translated by Paramārtha from the commentary of Vasubandhu. *Mahāyānasaṃgrahabhāṣya*, ten fascicles, one set, one hundred and seventy-six sheets; translated by Xuanzang from the commentary of Vasubandhu. *Mahāyānasaṃgrahabhāṣya*, ten fascicles, one set, two hundred and sixteen sheets; translated by Xuanzang from the commentary of Asvabhāva. *Tathāgatagarbhaśāstra* (Treatise on Buddha-nature), four fascicles, eighty-three sheets; translated by Paramārtha of the Chen dynasty. *Niyatāniyatagotravibhāgaśāstra* (Treatise on the Distinction of the Definite and Indefinite Lineages), three fascicles, fifty-two sheets; translated by Paramārtha of the Liang dynasty. *Madhyāntavibhāgakārikā* (Verses on the Discrimination of the Middle and the Extremes), one fascicle, five sheets; translated by Xuanzang of the Tang dynasty. *Madhyāntavibhāga-bhāṣya* (Commentary on the Discrimination of the Middle and the Extremes), two or three fascicles, fifty-eight sheets; translated by Paramārtha of the Chen dynasty. The above four treatises comprise ten fascicles in a single set.

*Madhyāntavibhāga-bhāṣya* (Discrimination of the Middle and the Extremes), three fascicles, thirty-nine sheets; translated by Xuanzang of the Tang dynasty. *Ratnagotravibhāga-mahāyānottaratantra-śāstra* (Treatise on the Ultimate One Vehicle Jewel Nature), four fascicles—also known as *Ratnagotra-vibhāga*, *Mahāyānottara-tantra*, or *Śāstra on the Superiority of the One Vehicle*—alternatively in three or five fascicles, eighty sheets; translated by Ratnamati of the Northern Wei dynasty. *Karmasiddhi-prakaraṇa* (Treatise on the Achievement of Karma), one fascicle, twelve sheets; translated by Vimokṣaprajña and others of the Northern Wei dynasty. *Karmasiddhiprakaraṇa* (Treatise on the Establishment of Karma in the Mahāyāna), one fascicle, seventeen sheets; translated by Xuanzang of the Tang dynasty. *Nyāyamukha-śāstra* (Treatise on the Gateway to Logic), one fascicle, fifteen sheets; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang. The above five treatises comprise ten fascicles and are contained in the same volume.
*Hetuvidyānyāyamukhaśāstra*, one fascicle, sixteen sheets;
translated by Tripiṭaka Master Yijing. *Hetuvidyāpraveśanyāyaśāstra*, one fascicle, six sheets;

translated by Xuanzang of the Tang dynasty. *Vijñaptimātratāsiddhi-śāstra*, one fascicle, titled "Chapter on Manifesting Consciousness" (*Vijñaptiprakaraṇa*), extracted from the *Nirākāra-śāstra*; nineteen sheets.
*Vijñaptimātratāsiddhi-śāstra*, one fascicle, three sheets; translated by Paramārtha of the Sui dynasty.
Also known as *Pò sèxīn* (Refutation of Matter and Mind). The opening states: "Consciousness-only, without external objects," or alternatively:

*Vijñaptimātratā-nirālambana-śāstra*. Nineteen sheets. Translated by Prajñāruci of the Northern Wei dynasty. *Vijñaptimātratā-śāstra*, one fascicle. The opening states: "The uncommon path of cultivation for others. Ten sheets.
*Viṃśatikā-vijñaptimātratāsiddhi-śāstra*, one fascicle, ten sheets; translated by Paramārtha of the Chen dynasty.
*Vijñaptimātratāsiddhi-ratnasambhava-śāstra*, five fascicles, also titled *Viṃśatikā-vijñaptimātratāsiddhi-anuvyākhyāna-śāstra*, sixty-five sheets; translated by Xuanzang of the Tang dynasty.
*Triṃśikā-vijñaptimātratāsiddhi-śāstra*, one fascicle, two sheets; translated by Yijing of the Tang dynasty.
Translated by Xuanzang of the Tang Dynasty: the aforementioned nine treatises comprise thirteen fascicles in one volume.

*Vijñaptimātratāsiddhi-śāstra* (Cheng weishi lun), ten fascicles, one volume, 175 sheets; translated by Xuanzang of the Tang Dynasty. *Mahāpuruṣa-śāstra* (Dafangdun lun), two fascicles, 34 sheets; *Mahāyānasaṃparigraha-śāstra* (Rudacheng lun), two fascicles, 41 sheets. The above two scriptures were translated by Shi Daotai of the Northern Liang Dynasty.

*Mahāyāna-lakṣaṇāloka-śāstra*, two fascicles, thirty-three pages; translated by Xuanzang of the Tang dynasty. *Mahāyāna-pañcaskandhaka-śāstra*, one fascicle, eight pages; composed by Vasubandhu, translated by Xuanzang. *Mahāyāna-vistara-pañcaskandhaka-śāstra*, one fascicle—a different version from the preceding treatise (or lacking the character "vistara" [broad]), composed by Sthiramati, thirteen pages; translated by Divākara of the Tang dynasty. *Ratnagotravibhāga-mahāyānottaratantra-śāstra*, one fascicle, nineteen pages; translated by Paramārtha of the Chen dynasty. *Mahāyāna-śraddhotpāda-śāstra*, one fascicle, twenty-five pages; translated by Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha. The above seven treatises, totaling ten fascicles, are contained in the same volume.
*Mahāyāna-śraddhotpāda-śāstra*, two fascicles, twenty-four sheets;
translated by Śikṣānanda. *Bodhicittotpāda-śāstra*, two fascicles, alternatively titled *Bodhicittotpāda-sūtra-śāstra*, twenty-eight sheets;
translated by Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin dynasty. *Tri-niḥsvabhāva-śāstra*, two fascicles; titled *Tri-niḥsvabhāva-śāstra-pariccheda*, excerpted from the *Nirākāra-śāstra*, thirty-five sheets.
*Upāyahṛdaya-śāstra* (Treatise on the Heart of Expedient Means), one fascicle or two fascicles, in four chapters and seventeen sheets; translated by Paramārtha during the Chen dynasty.

*Yathābhūta-śāstra* (Treatise on Reality), one fascicle, titled *Yathābhūta-śāstra: Chapter on Counter-Interrogation*; twenty-three sheets; translated by Kiṅkara and Tanyao during the Northern Wei dynasty.

*Nirākāravijñaptimātra-śāstra* (Treatise on the Non-existence of Mental Objects), one fascicle, or simply titled *Sicen lun* (Treatise on Mental Objects); three sheets; translated by Paramārtha during the Liang dynasty.
*Ālambanaparīkṣā-śāstra*, one fascicle, three pages, translated by Paramārtha of the Chen dynasty;
*Ālambanaparīkṣā-vyākhyā*, one fascicle, thirteen pages, translated by Xuanzang of the Tang dynasty;
and *Ālambanaparīkṣā-ṭīkā*, translated by Yijing of the Tang dynasty. These eight treatises comprise eleven fascicles and are contained in the same volume.
*Vigrahavyāvartanī-śāstra*, one fascicle, twenty-five sheets;
translated by Vimokṣasena and others of the Northern Wei. *Pratītyasamutpāda-śāstra*, one fascicle, eleven sheets;
translated by Guṇabhadra of the Chen. *Pratītyasamutpādādivibhaṅganirdeśa-śāstra*, one fascicle, four sheets.
*Ekaslokika-śāstra*, one fascicle (alternatively titled *Yishu Sanzhi*), translated by Bodhiruci of the Northern Wei;

*Mahāyāna-śatadharma-viśada-mukha-śāstra*, one fascicle, titled *Mahāyāna-śatadharma-viśada-mukha-śāstra: A Brief Record of Enumerations from the Mūla-bhāga*, two sheets, translated by Prajñāruci of the Northern Wei;
*Śata-akṣara-śāstra*, one fascicle, eight sheets, translated by Xuanzang of the Tang.
*Vigraha-vyāvartanī-śāstra*, one fascicle, three sheets; translated by Bodhiruci of the Northern Wei.

*Karaṇa-prakriyā-śāstra*, one fascicle, three sheets; translated by Paramārtha of the Chen. *Kāraṇa-parikalpa-upādāna-śāstra*, one fascicle, nine sheets. *Sāmānya-lakṣaṇa-parīkṣā-kārikā*, one fascicle, two sheets. *Śamatha-vipaśyanā-mukha-śāstra-kārikā*, one fascicle, four sheets. *Danda-śāstra*, one fascicle, seven sheets. *Ṣaṭ-dvāra-upadeśa-samādhi-bhāvanā-śāstra*, one fascicle, nine sheets. The above six scriptures were translated by Yi Jing of the Tang.

*Mahāyāna-dharmadhātu-aviśeṣa-śāstra*, one fascicle, six sheets; translated by Ti-yun-banruo (Jñānagupta) of the Tang dynasty. *Bāhyaka-hīnayāna-catur-nikāya-bhaṅga-śāstra*, one fascicle, six sheets. *Bāhyaka-hīnayāna-nirvāṇa-bhaṅga-śāstra*, one fascicle, five sheets. The two treatises above were translated by Bodhiruci of the Northern Wei dynasty.
The sixteen treatises above comprise sixteen fascicles in one volume.

In total, the Mahāyāna sūtras, vinayas, and śāstras included in the canon number six hundred and thirty-eight works, totaling two thousand seven hundred and forty-five fascicles, arranged in two hundred and fifty-eight volumes. As for the discrepancies between these figures and those in the previous *Guǎnglù* (Extensive Record), the former combined various sections of the *Mahāratnakūṭa-sūtra* into forty-nine separate works; here, they are consolidated into a single work, thus accounting for a difference of forty-eight works.

*The Catalogue of Buddhist Teachings Compiled during the Kaiyuan Era*, Scroll Nineteen, Upper Part of the Upper Section of the Canon Record (*Ruzang Lu*). *The Catalogue of Buddhist Teachings Compiled during the Kaiyuan Era*, Scroll Twenty, Lower Part of the Canon Record.

Compiled by the Śramaṇa Zhisheng of Chongfu Monastery in the Western Capital of Tang. **Canon Record for the Hīnayāna (Smaller Vehicle)** **Lower Section of the Hīnayāna Canon Record:** A total of three hundred and thirty works in one thousand seven hundred and sixty-two fascicles, arranged in one hundred and sixty-five bundles (*zhi*), including the collected biographies of sages and saints appended at the end of this scroll. This section lists the titles of the scriptures directly and provides their designations.
The remaining number of sheets is as recorded in the *Guǎlù* (Extended Record). There are 240 sections of Hīnayāna sūtras, totaling 618 fascicles in 48 bundles;
54 sections of Hīnayāna vinaya, totaling 446 fascicles in 45 bundles; and 36 sections of Hīnayāna śāstras, totaling 698 fascicles in 72 bundles.
