*Wǔkǔ zhāngjù jīng* (Sūtra on the Verses of the Five Sufferings), one fascicle—also titled *Zhūtiān wǔkǔ jīng* (Sūtra on the Five Sufferings of the Gods), *Wǔdào zhāngjù jīng* (Sūtra on the Verses of the Five Paths), or *Jìngchú zuìgài yuèlè fófǎ* (Purifying the Veil of Sin and Delighting in the Buddha-Dharma)—translated by the Shi Faju of the Western Jin;

thirteen sheets. Translated by Zhu Tanwulan of the Eastern Jin: *Jiànyì jīng* (Sūtra on Resolute Intention), one fascicle—also titled *Shùxīn zhèngyì jīng* (Sūtra on Upright Mind and Right Intention) or *Jiàn xīn jīng* (Sūtra on Firm Mind)—two sheets.

Translated during the Han dynasty by An Shigao: *Jìngfàn wáng nièpán jīng* (Sūtra on the Parinirvāṇa of King Śuddhodana), one fascicle—or with the character "bān" (pari-) added—seven sheets. *Jìn xué jīng* (Sūtra on Advancing in Learning), one fascicle—or titled *Quànjìn xuédào jīng* (Sūtra on Exhorting the Advancement of the Path of Learning)—one sheet. The above two sūtras were translated by Jing Sheng of the Song dynasty.

*Jiedao ticheng xizhang jing* (Sutra on the Ladder for Attaining the Way and the Alms-staff), one fascicle; the title reads *Jiedao ticheng jing*, "Chapter Twelve: The Alms-staff," or simply *Xizhang jing* (Alms-staff Sutra); three sheets. Translator lost; now appended to the Eastern Jin catalogue. *Pinqiong laogong jing* (Sutra of the Poor Old Man), one fascicle; also known as *Pinlao jing*; three sheets. Translated by the Song dynasty monk Huìjiǎn. *Sāmājīya jing* (Sutra of Sāmājīya), one fascicle; also known as *Sumati nǚ jing* (Sutra of the Girl Sumati), *Nán guówáng jing* (Sutra of King Nanda), or *Shuhétuánduānwáng jing* (Sutra of King Śuddhodana); eight sheets. Translated by Zhú Lùyán of the Wu dynasty. *Bīngshāwáng wùyuàn jing* (Sutra of King Piṃśa’s Five Vows), one fascicle; also known as *Fúshājiāwáng jing* (Sutra of King Puṣyaka) or written with the character "bīng" (flask); seven sheets. Translated by Zhīqián of the Wu dynasty. *Lúlíwáng jing* (Sutra of King Virūḍhaka), one fascicle; also written with the character "bīng" or "liúlí"; seven sheets. The above fifteen sutras, totaling seventeen fascicles, are contained in the same volume.
*Sheng jing* (Sūtra on Birth), five fascicles or four fascicles, one hundred and nine sheets. The above two sūtras were translated by Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin.
*Yizu jing* (Sūtra on the Fulfillment of Meaning), two fascicles, forty sheets, translated by Zhi Qian of the Wu. The above two sūtras, totaling seven fascicles, are contained in the same volume.

Small Vehicle Sūtras Translated Individually: Eighty-seven works in two hundred twenty-four fascicles, comprising seventeen bundles. *The Sūtra on the Stations of Mindfulness of the True Dharma* (Saddharmasmṛtyupasthāna-sūtra), seventy fascicles, seven bundles, one thousand two hundred five sheets. Translated by Prajñāruci during the Northern Wei dynasty. *The Compendium of the Buddha’s Past Deeds* (Buddhacarita-saṃgraha), sixty fascicles, also titled *The Compendium of All [Deeds]*, six bundles, eight hundred eighty-seven sheets. Translated by Jñānagupta and others during the Sui dynasty. *The Sūtra on Previous Lives* (Mūlasarvāstivāda-vinaya-kṣudraka-vastu), seven fascicles, ninety-five sheets. Translated by Xuanzang during the Tang dynasty. *The Sūtra on the Arising of Conduct*, also titled *The Sūtra on the Strict Admonitions of Past Causes*, two fascicles, thirty-one sheets. Translated by Kang Mengxiang during the Han dynasty. *The Sūtra on the Differentiation of Karmic Retribution*, one fascicle, fifteen sheets. Translated by Gautama Fazhi during the Sui dynasty. The above three sūtras comprise ten fascicles and are contained in the same bundle.
The *Dà ān bān shǒu yì jīng* (Sūtra on Great Ānāpāna-smṛti) in two fascicles; it is also simply called the *Dà ān bān jīng*, or sometimes lacks the character "Dà" (Great).

Master An stated that it is the *Xiǎo ān bān jīng* (Sūtra on Small Ānāpāna), or it consists of one fascicle and thirty sheets. The *Yīn chí rù jīng* (Sūtra on the Bases of Mindfulness and Entrances) in two fascicles;

some say "Chú chí rù" (Eliminating the Bases of Mindfulness and Entrances), which is an error. Or it is one fascicle, also titled *Zhù yīn chí rù* (Abiding in the Bases of Mindfulness and Entrances), consisting of thirty-two sheets. It appears in various locations.
*Sūtra* (in one fascicle, fifteen sheets): *Māyi-sūtra* (in one fascicle, fifteen sheets). *Vibhaṅga-kuśalākuśala-samudaya-sūtra* (in one fascicle, fifteen sheets).
*Pravrajyā-pratyaya-sūtra* (in one fascicle; also titled *Pravrajyā-hetu-pratyaya-sūtra*, two sheets).
*Aśvajit-samyak-caryā-sūtra* (in one fascicle; also titled *Samyak-mati*, four sheets). *Aṣṭādaśa-niraya*... [text fragment].
*The Plow Sūtra*, one fascicle (alternatively titled *The Sūtra on the Eighteen Hells*), six sheets; *The Sūtra on Dharmas Receiving Dust*, one fascicle, one sheet;
*The Sūtra on the Dhyāna Practice of Mental Conception*, one fascicle, one sheet;

*The Sūtra on the Elder’s Son’s Grief at Three Places*, one fascicle—also known as *The Sūtra on the Elder’s Son’s Distress at Three Places* or *The Sūtra on Distress at Three Places*—three sheets; [The Sūtra from] the Kingdom of Gandhāra.
*The King Sūtra*, one fascicle (alternatively without the character for "king," two sheets). The twelve sūtras above were translated by An Shigao during the Han dynasty.

*The Sūtra of the Householder Sumati*, one fascicle—also known as *The Assembly Before All Buddhas* or *The Manifestation Taught by the Tathāgata to Reveal to Sentient Beings*, eight sheets. *The Sūtra of Ānanda’s Four Matters*, one fascicle, four sheets. *The Sūtra of Ajātaśatru*, one fascicle, four sheets. *The Sūtra of the Four Vows*, one fascicle, three sheets. *The Sūtra of the Brahmin Kṛṣṇa*, one fascicle, three sheets. *The Sūtra of the Mad Dog*, one fascicle; Dao’an states it is identical to the *Sūtra of the Hyena Dog*, two sheets. The six sūtras above were translated by Zhi Qian of the Wu dynasty.

*Fenbie jing* (Discrimination Sutra), one fascicle, five sheets; translated by Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin. *Baguanzhai jing* (Sutra on the Eight Precepts of Abstinence), one fascicle, two sheets; translated by Jing Sheng of the Song. *Ajiuliu jing* (Ajiravatī Sutra), one fascicle, four sheets; translator lost, now appended to the Han record. *Xiaozijing* (Sutra on Filial Sons), also known as *Xiaozibao'en jing* (Sutra on Filial Sons Repaying Kindness), one fascicle, two sheets; translator lost, now appended to the Western Jin record. These twenty-two sutras, totaling twenty-four fascicles, are contained in the same volume.

*The Sutra of the Five Hundred Disciples’ Own Narration of Their Past Lives*, one fascicle; alternatively titled *The Sutra of the Buddha’s Five Hundred Disciples’ Own Narration of Their Past Lives*, also titled *The Sutra of the Five Hundred Disciples’ Own Narration of Their Origins and Ends*, or *The Sutra of the Five Hundred Disciples’ Past Lives*, twenty-one sheets. *The Sutra of Mahākāśyapa’s Past Life*, one fascicle; sometimes the character "Great" (Da) is omitted, five sheets. *The Sutra of the Four Who Harmed Themselves*, one fascicle, five sheets. These three sutras above were translated by Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin.

*The Sūtra on Rāhula’s Endurance of Insult*, one fascicle (also simply titled *The Sūtra on Endurance*), three sheets; *The Sūtra on the Buddha’s Teaching of Proper Conduct to a Young Bhikṣu*, one fascicle, two sheets; *The Sūtra on the Merits of the Bhikṣu Śaha*, one fascicle, three sheets. These three sūtras were translated by the Western Jin monk Shi Faju.

The *Śīla-aśīla-sūtra* (Sūtra on Timeliness and Untimeliness), one fascicle; also simply called the *Śīla-sūtra*, two sheets. Translated by the foreign Dharma Master Yeluo Yan (Yaropāṇa); its imperial era is unknown. The *Ātmavatsala-sūtra* (Sūtra on Loving Oneself), one fascicle; alternatively titled the *Ātmavatsalānātmavatsala-sūtra*, five sheets. The *Madhyacitta-sūtra* (Sūtra on the Central Mind), one fascicle; also called the *Madhyacitta-samyakcaryā-sūtra*, or the *Mahāhṛdaya-sūtra*, or the *Kṣudrahṛdaya-sūtra*, five sheets. The *Dṛṣṭasatya-sūtra* (Sūtra on Seeing the Truth), one fascicle; also named the *Saṃsāravijñānapariṇāma-sūtra*, eight sheets. The *Mahāmatsyavastu-sūtra* (Sūtra on the Matter of the Great Fish), one fascicle, two sheets. The *Ānanda-saptasvapna-sūtra* (Sūtra on Ānanda’s Seven Dreams), one fascicle; also called the *Saptasvapna-sūtra*, two sheets. The *Kokālika-anāgāmin-sūtra* (Sūtra on Kokālika the Non-returner), one fascicle; also named the *Hekālika*, or written with the character "ke" (苛), two sheets. The above six sūtras were translated by Zhu Tanwulan during the Eastern Jin dynasty.

*The Scripture on the Causes and Conditions of the Lamp-Finger*, one fascicle, nine pages; translated by Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin. *The Scripture on a Woman Meeting with Calamity*, one fascicle—also titled *The Scripture on a Woman Meeting with Retribution*, two pages; translated by Shi Shengjian of the Qifu Qin. *The Scripture of the Four Heavenly Kings*, one fascicle, three pages; translated by Shi Zhiyan of Liangzhou together with Baoyun of the Song dynasty. *The Scripture of Mahākāśyapa Saving the Poor Mother*, one fascicle, four pages, twelve chapters. *The Scripture of Birth and Death*, one fascicle, one page. *The Scripture on the Retribution of Sin and Merit*, one fascicle—also titled *The Scripture on the Retribution of Sin and Merit in the Five Paths of Transmigration*, also called *The Scripture on the Five Paths of Transmigration*, or *The Scripture on the Wheel of the Five Paths*; four pages. The above three scriptures were translated by Guṇabhadra of the Song dynasty.

*Wǔ wǎnfǎn jīng* (Sūtra on the Five Non-Reciprocities), one fascicle; also titled *Wǔ fǎnfù dàyì jīng* (Sūtra on the Great Meaning of the Five Reversals) or with the character "fù" (attached); two sheets. *Fó dà sēng dà jīng* (Sūtra of the Buddha’s Great Assembly), one fascicle; two sons [as title]; seven sheets. *Yéqí jīng* (Yaṅkī Sūtra), one fascicle; two sheets. *Mólówáng jīng* (King Malla Sūtra), one fascicle; two sheets. *Módá guówáng jīng* (King Madra Sūtra), one fascicle; sometimes without the character "guó" (king); two sheets. *Zhāntuōyuè guówáng jīng* (King Caṇḍavatsa Sūtra), one fascicle; sometimes without the character "guówáng" (king); two sheets. *Wǔ kǒngbù shì jīng* (Sūtra on the Five Terrifying Worlds), one fascicle; also called *Wǔ kǒngbù jīng* (Sūtra of the Five Terrors); two sheets. *Dízǐ sǐ fùshēng jīng* (Sūtra of the Disciple Who Dies and is Reborn), one fascicle; also called *Sǐwáng gèngshēng jīng* (Sūtra of Death and Rebirth); six sheets. The above eight sūtras were translated by Sheng of the Song capital.

*The Sūtra on the Lazy Plowman*, one fascicle; alternatively titled *The Sūtra on the Lazy Plowman’s Son*, two sheets. Translated by the Song dynasty monk Huìjiǎn. *The Sūtra on the Elder’s Son Biànyì*, one fascicle; alternatively titled *The Sūtra on the Elder Biànyì*, or with the words "Questioned by" (*suǒwèn*) added at the beginning, nine sheets. Translated by the Northern Wei dynasty monk Fǎcháng. *The Sūtra on the Inquiry of the Upright Upāsikā*, one fascicle, three sheets. Translated by the Northern Wei dynasty monk Bōrěliúzhī. The above thirty sūtras comprise thirty fascicles and are contained in the same volume.

*The Sūtra on the Five Blessings of the Wise*, one fascicle, one page; translated by Bai Fazǔ of the Western Jin. *The Sūtra of Questions from Heaven*, one fascicle, two pages; translated by Xuanzang of the Tang. *The Sūtra of Saṃgharakṣita*, one fascicle—also called *The Sūtra on the Causes and Conditions of Saṃgharakṣita* or *The Sūtra of the Causes and Conditions of Saṃgharakṣita*—twenty pages. *The Sūtra on Purifying the Body*, one fascicle, two pages. *The Sūtra on the Bodhi Tree Seed* (alternatively written with the characters 患 or 檈), two pages. *The Sūtra on the Unsurpassed State*, one fascicle, one page. *The Sūtra on the Causes and Conditions of the Elder Lu Zhì*, one fascicle, ten pages. *The Sūtra of the Five Kings*, one fascicle, five pages. The above six sūtras were lost in their original translations and are now appended to the catalog of the Eastern Jin.

*Chujia Gongde Jing* (Sutra on the Merits of Leaving Home), one fascicle; not extracted from the *Xianyu Jing*, five sheets. Translator lost; now appended to the Qin Records. *Zhantan Shu Jing* (Sutra of the Sandalwood Tree), one fascicle, three sheets. Appended to the Han Records as a classical text by Master Dao'an. *Eduo Heduo Ji Jing* (Sutra of Eldara and Ajita), one fascicle, two sheets. *Putuo Wang Jing* (Sutra of King Pūrṇa), one fascicle, four sheets. *Fomie Du Hou Guanlian Zangsong Jing* (Sutra on the Enshrouding and Burial after the Buddha’s Parinirvāṇa), one fascicle; also titled *Biqiu Shi Jing* or *Shi Biqiu Jing*, three sheets. *Guizi Mu Jing* (Sutra of Hārītī), one fascicle, four sheets. *Fanmo Nan Guo Wang Jing* (Sutra of King Brahmadatta), one fascicle, two sheets. The above five sutras were lost translations by Master Dao’an; they are now appended to the Western Jin Records.

*Fùmǔ ēnnánbào jīng* (Sutra on the Difficulty of Repaying Parental Kindness), one fascicle; also called *Qín bào* (Diligently Repaying), two sheets. Translated by An Shigao of the Han dynasty. *Sūnduōyēzhì jīng* (Sutra of Sundarika), one fascicle; also called *Fànzhì Sūnduōxiēzhì jīng* (Sutra of the Brahmin Sundarika), three sheets. Translated by Zhi Qian of the Wu dynasty. *Xīnsuì jīng* (Sutra of the New Year), one fascicle, six sheets. Translated by Zhu Tanwulan of the Eastern Jin dynasty. *Qúnniū pì jīng* (Sutra of the Parable of the Herds of Cows), one fascicle, two sheets. Translated by Shi Faju of the Western Jin dynasty. *Jiǔhéng jīng* (Sutra of the Nine Untimely Deaths), one fascicle, two sheets. *Cánxíng sānshíqī jīng* (Sutra of the Thirty-Seven Practices of Dhyāna); also called *Cánxíng sānshíqīpǐn jīng* (Sutra of the Thirty-Seven Categories of Dhyāna Practice), three sheets. These two sutras were translated by An Shigao of the Han dynasty.

*The Sūtra on a Bhikṣu Attempting Suicide to Avoid a Woman’s Ill Repute*, one fascicle, one page; translated by Shi Faju of the Western Jin. *The Sūtra on the Bhikṣu Accepting Alms*, one fascicle (also titled *The Sūtra on the Bhikṣu Accepting Alms*), three pages; translated by Zhu Tanwulan of the Eastern Jin. *The Sūtra on Contemplating the Body*, one fascicle, two pages; translated by Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin. *The Sūtra on Impermanence*, one fascicle (also titled *The Sūtra of the Three Invocations*), three pages. *The Sūtra on the Eight Inopportune Births and the Opportune Birth*, one fascicle, seven pages. *The Sūtra on the Questions of the Brahmacārin Dīrghanakha*, one fascicle, three pages. *The Sūtra of Parables*, one fascicle, two pages. *The Sūtra of Brief Exhortations*, one fascicle, two pages. *The Sūtra on Healing Hemorrhoids*, one fascicle (also titled *The Sūtra on Healing Fistulas and Hemorrhoids*), two pages. The above six sūtras were translated by Yi Jing of the Tang dynasty.
The thirty *sūtras* above comprise thirty fascicles in one bundle. Regarding the Hīnayāna Vinaya:

there are fifty-four works totaling four hundred and forty-six fascicles in forty-five bundles. The *Mahāsāṃghika-vinaya* consists of forty fascicles (some say thirty), comprising four bundles and nine hundred and ninety-seven sheets; it was translated by Buddhabhadra together with Faxian during the Eastern Jin dynasty. The *Sarvāstivāda-vinaya* consists of sixty-one fascicles in six bundles and one thousand four hundred and thirty sheets.

Translated by Puṇyatāra and Kumārajīva during the Yao Qin dynasty: *Vinaya of the Mūlasarvāstivāda* (50 fascicles, 5 bundles, 875 sheets). *Vinaya of the Bhikṣuṇīs of the Mūlasarvāstivāda* (20 fascicles, 2 bundles, 359 sheets). *Vinayakṣudrakavastu of the Mūlasarvāstivāda* (40 fascicles, 4 bundles, 611 sheets). *Nidāna and Muktaka of the Mūlasarvāstivāda* (10 fascicles; the first five fascicles are *Nidāna* and the latter five are *Muktaka*, or alternatively 8 fascicles, 1 bundle, 125 sheets). The above four scriptures were translated by Yi Jing of the Tang dynasty.
The *Pañcavargika-vinaya* (Five-Part Vinaya), thirty fascicles, also called the *Mahīśāsaka-vinaya*, or alternatively in four fascicles;

three bundles; five hundred and ninety-seven sheets; translated by Buddhayaśas and Zhu Daosheng during the Song dynasty. The *Dharmaguptaka-vinaya* (Four-Part Vinaya), sixty fascicles—or forty-five, seventy, or forty-four fascicles; six bundles; one thousand three hundred and fifteen sheets; translated by Buddhayaśas and Zhu Fonian during the Yao Qin dynasty.
The *Mahāsāṃghika-bhikṣu-pratimokṣa-sūtra* (Sengqi Bhikṣu Jieben), one fascicle; also called the *Mahāsāṃghika-pratimokṣa-sūtra*; twenty sheets.

*Mahāsāṃghika Bhikṣuṇī Prātimokṣa Sūtra*, one fascicle; also titled *Mahāsāṃghika Bhikṣuṇī Vinaya Prātimokṣa*, thirty-five sheets. Translated by Buddhabhadra during the Eastern Jin dynasty. *Daśabhāṇavāra Bhikṣu Prātimokṣa Sūtra*, one fascicle;

also titled *Daśabhāṇavāra Vinaya Prātimokṣa*, twenty-six sheets. *Daśabhāṇavāra Bhikṣuṇī Prātimokṣa Sūtra*, one fascicle; also titled *Daśabhāṇavāra Bhikṣuṇī Vinaya Prātimokṣa*, twenty-six sheets. These two scriptures were translated by Kumārajīva during the Yao Qin dynasty.

The *Mūlasarvāstivāda-śīla-sūtra*, one fascicle, twenty-eight sheets; the *Mūlasarvāstivāda-bhikṣuṇī-śīla-sūtra*, one fascicle, thirty-four sheets. These two sūtras were translated by Yi Jing of the Tang dynasty.

The *Bhikṣu-prātimokṣa-sūtra of the Five-Part Vinaya* (Mūlasarvāstivāda), one fascicle, also known as the *Mi-sha-se Jieben*, eighteen sheets; translated by Buddhayaśas and others of the Song dynasty. These seven scriptures, totaling seven fascicles, are contained in the same volume.

*The Bhikṣuṇī Prātimokṣa Sūtra of the Mahīśāsaka School*, one fascicle; also called *The Bhikṣuṇī Prātimokṣa Sūtra of the Mahīśāsaka School*, twenty-nine sheets. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Buddhayaśas of Kapiśī during the Song dynasty and others. *The Bhikṣu Prātimokṣa Sūtra of the Dharmaguptaka School*, one fascicle. Compiled by the śramaṇa Huaisu according to the Vinaya; titled *The Dharmaguptaka Prātimokṣa Sūtra*, twenty-four sheets. *The Bhikṣuṇī Prātimokṣa Sūtra of the Dharmaguptaka School*, one fascicle. Compiled by the śramaṇa Huaisu according to the Vinaya; titled *The Dharmaguptaka Bhikṣuṇī Prātimokṣa Sūtra*, thirty sheets. The above two scriptures were compiled and issued by the Tang dynasty śramaṇa Huaisu.

*The Monastic Precepts for the Fourfold Community* (Sifen seng jieben), one fascicle—sometimes omitting the word "monastic" (seng)—also known as *The Precepts of the Dharmaguptaka School*, thirty-three pages;
translated by Buddhayaśas during the Yao Qin dynasty. *The Prātimokṣa Sūtra*, one fascicle, derived from the Kāśyapīya school, thirty-two pages;
translated by Prajñāruci during the Northern Wei dynasty. *The Dharma and Ritual of the Ten Śrāmaṇera Precepts*, also known as *The Śrāmaṇera Ritual Precepts*, one fascicle, twenty-one pages.
*Śrāmaṇera-Ācāra* (One Scroll), translated by an unknown translator; now appended to the Eastern Jin catalog. Also known as the *Śrāmaṇera-Ācāra Sūtra*, nine sheets.
Translated by Guṇavarman of the Song dynasty. *Śrāmaṇerikā-Vinaya-kṣudraka-vastu* (One Scroll), four sheets.
Translated by an unknown translator; now appended to the Eastern Jin catalog. *Śrāmaṇerikā-Pratimokṣa-sūtra* (One Scroll) [or without the word "sūtra"], five sheets.

The *Śāriputra-paripṛcchā-sūtra* (Śāriputra-asked Sūtra), one fascicle, eleven pages; translator lost, recorded in the Han catalog, now appended to the Eastern Jin catalog. These ten sūtras, totaling ten fascicles, are contained in the same volume.
*Fundamental Sarvāstivāda-vinaya-ekottara-karman* (Mūlasarvāstivāda-ekottara-karman), ten fascicles, one volume, 146 pages;

translated by the Tang dynasty master Yijing. *Dharma of the Hundred and One Karmans of the Great Śramaṇa*, one fascicle; excerpted from the *Daśabhāṇavāra-vinaya*. Also known as the *Dharma of the Karma of the Great Śramaṇa*.

24 pages; translator lost; currently appended to the Song Catalogue. *Essential Use for Bhikṣus: The Daśabhāṇavāra-karman*, one fascicle; excerpted from the *Daśabhāṇavāra-vinaya*. Also known as the *Abridged Essential Karma-dharma*. Alternatively, two fascicles. Sengyou’s catalogue states it consists of 24 pages.
The *Upāli’s Questions to the Buddha Sūtra* (Yōubārī monbutsu kyō), one fascicle, compiled and produced by the Song dynasty śramaṇa Sengqu;

alternatively titled the *Upāli Vinaya*, thirty-three pages; lost translation, recorded in the Later Han catalog. The *Pañcavargika Karmavācanā* (Bunbun karmama), one fascicle, titled the *Mūlasarvāstivāda Karmavācanā Original*, thirty-one pages.

The *Caturvarga Saṃkīrṇa Karmavācanā* (Shibun zatsu karmama), one fascicle, compiled and produced by the Tang dynasty śramaṇa Aitong; titled the *Dharmaguptaka Vinaya Section: Miscellaneous Karmavācanā*, beginning with the establishment of the *sīmā-maṇḍala*, twenty-four pages.
*The Dharmaguptaka Karma*, one fascicle, translated by Kāṅsēngkǎi of the Cao Wei dynasty;
the title reads *Karma*, one fascicle, extracted from the *Dharmaguptaka Vinaya*. It begins with the "Binding of the Great Boundary" (*mahā-sīmā-bandha*) and consists of thirty-seven pages.

Translated by the Sramana Tandi of the Cao Wei dynasty. *The Dharmaguptaka Bhikṣuṇī Karma-dharma*, one fascicle. Sengyou states: "The *Dharmaguptaka Karma* is also called the *Miscellaneous Karma* (*Za-jie-mo*)," consisting of fifteen pages.
Translated by Guṇavarman of the Song Dynasty, the seven aforementioned scriptures comprise seven fascicles in one volume.

*The Random Karman for the Four-Part Vinaya (Dharmaguptaka-vinaya-karman-saṃkṣepa-vistara-yathā-pratyaya)*, one fascicle; its preface title reads *Tánwúdébù sìfēnlǜ shānbǔ suíjí jiémó*, forty-seven pages. Compiled by the Tang monk Dàoxuān, *The Karman for the Four-Part Saṃgha*, three fascicles; its title reads *Jiémó juànshàng*, extracted from the *Sìfēnlǜ*, eighty pages. *The Karman for the Four-Part Nuns*, three fascicles; its title reads *Níjiémó juànshàng*, extracted from the *Sìfēnlǜ*, seventy pages. These two latter scriptures were compiled by the Tang monk Huáisù.
The three aforementioned scriptures comprise seven fascicles in one volume.
The *Mahāprajāpatī Bhikṣuṇī Sūtra* in two fascicles—also titled the *Mahāprajāpatī Ordination Sūtra* or simply the *Mahāprajāpatī Sūtra*—consists of thirty-one sheets;

its translator is lost, and it is now appended to the Northern Liang catalog. The *Kāśyapa Prohibitory Precepts Sūtra* in one fascicle—also known as the *Mahābhikṣu Sūtra* or the *Sūtra on Authentic and Spurious Śramaṇas*—consists of three sheets.

*The Sūtra on the Light and Heavy Retributions for Violating the Precepts*, one fascicle, translated by Song Jingsheng; also known as the *Sūtra of Maudgalyāyana’s Questions on the Vinaya*, or alternatively as the *Sūtra on the Retribution of Sins*, or simply the *Sūtra of Maudgalyāyana’s Questions*, consisting of two sheets, translated during the Han dynasty by An Shigao.

*The Sūtra on the Precepts for Eliminating Calamities*, one fascicle; alternatively titled the *Sūtra on the Precepts for Subduing and Eliminating Calamities*, consisting of four sheets, translated by Zhi Qian of the Wu dynasty.
*The Sūtra on the Characteristics of the Five Lay Precepts*, one fascicle; also known as the *Brief Treatise on the Five Lay Precepts*, consisting of fourteen sheets.

*Vinaya-sūtra* (Fundamental Verses on the Sarvāstivāda Vinaya) in five fascicles (or two), translated by Guṇavarman of the Song dynasty; seventy-one pages. *Vinayakṣudrakavastu-saṃgraha-gāthā* (Verses Comprising the Miscellaneous Matters of the Sarvāstivāda Vinaya) in one fascicle; six pages. *Vinayanidāna-mātṛkā-saṃgraha-gāthā* (Verses Comprising the Introduction and Supplements to the Sarvāstivāda Vinaya) in one fascicle; eight pages. The *Nidāna-gāthā* precedes and the *Mātṛkā-gāthā* follows. The above three scriptures were translated by Yijing of the Tang dynasty.

*Wǔbǎiwènshì jīng* (Sūtra of Five Hundred Questions), one fascicle, thirty-three pages; translator lost, now appended to the Eastern Jin catalogue. [These] nine sūtras, fourteen fascicles, are in the same case.
*Gēnběn sāpótǒubù lǜshè* (Vinaya-saṃgraha of the Mūlasarvāstivāda School), twenty fascicles (or fourteen fascicles), two cases, two hundred seventy-seven pages;
translated by the Tang dynasty Yìjìng. *Píní módelèqié* (Vinayamātṛkā), ten fascicles; the first fascicle states: *Sāpótǒubù píní módelèqié*. One case, one hundred eighty-eight pages.

*Pinaiye Lü* (The Vinaya of the Mūlasarvāstivāda), ten fascicles; translated by the Song dynasty monk Saṃghavarman. Also titled *Ji Yinyuan Jing* (Sutra on the Causes and Conditions of Precepts), or *Jie Gu Yinyuan Jing* (Sutra on the Causes and Conditions of the Fruits of Precepts), or simply *Pinaiye Jing*.

One bundle, one hundred fifty-five pages. Translated by Zhu Fonian of the Yao Qin dynasty. *Shanjian Lü Piposha* (The Vinayavibhāṣā of the Well-Seen Vinaya), eighteen fascicles; also called *Piposha Lü*, or simply *Shanjian Lü*. Three hundred fifty-eight pages.
Translated by Saṃghabhadra of the Xiao Qi dynasty. *Buddha Abhidharma Sutra*, two fascicles; also called *Buddha Abhidharma Treatise*. Forty-five pages.
Translated by Paramārtha of Chen: the aforementioned two sūtras, twenty fascicles in two volumes.

*Vinayamātṛkā-sūtra*, eight fascicles; also called the *Vinayamātṛkā-śāstra*, one hundred and fifty-six sheets. Translator lost; now appended to the Qin Records. *Mahābhikṣu-trisahasra-vidhi-sūtra*, two fascicles; also called the *Mahāsāṃghika-vidhi-sūtra* or four fascicles, forty-two sheets. Translated during the Han dynasty by An Shigao: the aforementioned two sūtras, ten fascicles in one volume.
The *Sarvāstivādavinayavibhāṣā* in nine fascicles and one hundred eighty-seven sheets; the translator is lost, now appended to the Qin records.
The *Vinaya-viṃśati-prakaraṇa-vidyud-uttara-śāstra* (also called the *Vidyud-uttara-śāstra*) in one fascicle and twenty-four sheets, translated by Paramārtha of the Chen dynasty.

The above two scriptures comprise ten fascicles in one bundle. **Treatises of the Hīnayāna:** Sixty-three treatises, totaling six hundred ninety-eight fascicles in seventy-two bundles. The *Abhidharma-aṣṭagrantha-śāstra* in thirty fascicles (sometimes omitting the character "lun" [treatise], sometimes called the *Kātyāyanābhidharma*, or the *Abhidharma-aṣṭagrantha-sūtra*; alternatively in twenty fascicles), comprising three bundles and four hundred sixty-two sheets.

The *Abhidharma-jñānaprasthāna-śāstra* (Treatise on the Foundation of Knowledge), twenty fascicles in two volumes, translated by Saṃghadeva and Zhu Fonian under the Fu Qin; composed by Kātyāyanīputra, totaling three hundred and fifty-eight sheets. The *Abhidharma-dharmaskandha-pāda-śāstra* (Treatise on the Bases of the Aggregates of Phenomena), twelve fascicles in one volume, composed by Mahāmaudgalyāyana, totaling one hundred and eighty-nine sheets. The *Abhidharma-saṃgītiparyāya-pāda-śāstra* (Treatise on the Enumeration of the Collection of Phenomena), twenty fascicles in two volumes, composed by Śāriputra, totaling one hundred and seventy-eight sheets. The *Abhidharma-vijñānakāya-pāda-śāstra* (Treatise on the Body of Consciousness), sixteen fascicles, totaling two hundred and sixty-five sheets. The *Abhidharma-dhātukāya-pāda-śāstra* (Treatise on the Body of Elements), three fascicles, totaling thirty-nine sheets. The above two treatises comprise nineteen fascicles in two volumes.
The *Abhidharma-prakaraṇapāda-śāstra* in eighteen fascicles, totaling three hundred and fifty-five pages; the above six treatises were translated by Xuanzang of the Tang dynasty.

The *Saṃgītiparyāya-abhidharma-śāstra* in twelve fascicles (or with the character "lun" [treatise] omitted), totaling two hundred and eight pages; translated by Guṇabhadra of the Song dynasty. The above two treatises comprise thirty fascicles in three bundles.

*Abhidharma-vibhāṣā-śāstra*, sixty fascicles, in six bundles; alternatively titled with the characters *bā-jiàn-dù* (Eight *Khandas*), or eighty-four fascicles, or one hundred and nine fascicles, totaling one thousand two hundred and ninety-three sheets. Translated by the Northern Liang śramaṇa Buddhavarman together with Daotai. *Abhidharma-mahāvibhāṣā-śāstra*, two hundred fascicles; alternatively called the *Abhidharma-jñānaprasthāna-mahāvibhāṣā*, totaling three thousand and sixty-nine sheets. Translated by Xuanzang of the Tang dynasty. *Abhidharma-kośa-bhāṣya*, twenty-two fascicles; alternatively without the character *shì* (commentary), totaling four hundred and seventy-one sheets. Translated by Paramārtha of the Chen dynasty. *Abhidharma-kośa-kārikā*, one fascicle; alternatively three fascicles, totaling twenty-three sheets. The aforementioned two treatises comprise twenty-three fascicles in three bundles: the first bundle contains seven fascicles, while the middle and lower bundles each contain eight fascicles.

The *Abhidharmakośa-śāstra*, thirty fascicles, three bundles, four hundred and sixty-five sheets; the *Abhidharma-jñānaprasthāna-śāstra* (or *Nyāyānusāra*), eighty fascicles, eight bundles, one thousand three hundred and ninety-four sheets; the *Abhidharma-prakaraṇapāda-śāstra* (or *Abhidharmasamaya-pradīpikā*), forty fascicles, four bundles, six hundred and fourteen sheets. These four treatises were translated by Xuanzang of the Tang dynasty.

*Abhidharmahṛdaya-śāstra*, four fascicles (or omitting the character "lun" [treatise]), sixty-nine sheets; translated by Gautama Saṃghadeva during the Eastern Jin dynasty. *Dharmottara-abhidharmahṛdaya-sūtra*, six fascicles (or omitting the character "jing" [sūtra], or omitting the name "Dharmottara," or seven fascicles, or titled *Dharmottara-abhidharma-śāstra*, or adding the characters "separately translated"), one hundred five sheets; translated by Ratnamati together with Narendrayaśas during the Northern Qi dynasty. These two treatises, totaling ten fascicles, are bound in the same volume.

*Saṃyuktābhidharmahṛdaya-śāstra*, eleven fascicles (or without the word "śāstra"), also called *Saṃyuktābhidharma-sūtra* or *Saṃyuktābhidharma-vibhāṣā*, or fourteen fascicles, two hundred and seventy-nine sheets; translated during the Song dynasty by Saṃghavarman and others. *Abhidharmāmṛta-rasa-śāstra*, two fascicles (or called *Amṛtarasa-abhidharma* or without the word "śāstra"), forty-six sheets; translated during the Cao Wei period, the name of the Tripiṭaka Master lost. *Anu-dharma-lakṣaṇa-śāstra*, one fascicle (or called *Guṇamati-anudharmalakṣaṇa-śāstra*), thirty-four sheets; translated by Paramārtha of the Chen dynasty. The above three treatises comprise fourteen fascicles in two volumes.

The *Ācārya Vasumitra-bodhisattva-saṃgīti-śāstra* (尊婆須蜜菩薩所集論), ten fascicles, or twelve fascicles, or fourteen fascicles; also called the *Vasumitra-sūtra*; 362 sheets. Translated by Saṃghabhūti and others during the Fu Qin dynasty. The *Tri-dharmaka-śāstra* (三法度論), two fascicles; sometimes without the character "lun" (論); sometimes called a "lun" or a "jing" (經); alternatively three fascicles or ten fascicles; 49 sheets. Translated by Gautama Saṃghadeva during the Eastern Jin dynasty. The *Abhidharma-praveśa-śāstra* (入阿毘達磨論), two fascicles; 28 sheets. Translated by Xuanzang during the Tang dynasty. The above three treatises comprise fourteen fascicles in two volumes.

*Satyasiddhi-śāstra*, twenty fascicles, comprising two hundred and two chapters; alternatively in twenty-seven fascicles, or fourteen fascicles, or sixteen fascicles; two volumes, totaling three hundred and ninety-eight sheets;

translated by Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin dynasty. *Lokasthiti-abhidharma-śāstra*, ten fascicles; one volume; alternatively without the character "lun" (treatise) in the title, titled *Lishi-pitan-zang* (Abhidharma-piṭaka of the World’s Establishment), or stated to be fifteen fascicles; also known as the *Tiandi-ji-jing* (Sutra on the Record of Heaven and Earth); one hundred and sixty-four sheets; translated by Paramārtha of the Chen dynasty.
*Vimuktimārga-śāstra*, twelve fascicles; alternatively thirteen fascicles; one hundred and ninety-seven sheets.

The *Śāriputrābhidharma-śāstra*, translated by Saṃghavarman of the Liang dynasty, in twenty-two fascicles (alternatively titled with or without the character "lun," or in twenty fascicles, or in thirty fascicles, totaling six hundred and four sheets);
and the *Pañcavastu-vibhāṣā-śāstra*, translated by Dharmayaśas and Dharmagupta of the Yao Qin dynasty, in two fascicles (also called the *Abhidharma-pañcavastu-śāstra*, totaling twenty-four sheets).
Translated by Xuanzang of the Tang dynasty, these two treatises comprise twenty-four fascicles in three bundles.

The *Vibhāṣā-śāstra* in fourteen fascicles—also called the *Vibhāṣā-abhidharma-śāstra*; the latter title is followed by "extensive exposition" (*pṛthuvyākhyāna*)—is in fifteen or nineteen fascicles, or sometimes lacks the word "treatise" (*śāstra*). It comprises three hundred and thirty-five sheets. Translated by Saṃghabhūti during the Fu Qin dynasty. The *Sammitīya-nikāya-śāstra* in three fascicles—sometimes lacking the word "school" (*nikāya*)—or in four fascicles, comprising thirty-six sheets. Translator lost; currently appended to the Fu Qin records. These two treatises total seventeen fascicles in two volumes: the first volume contains eight fascicles, and the second volume contains nine.

*Fenbie gongde lun* (Treatise on the Analysis of Merit), four fascicles; alternatively titled *Fenbie gongde jing* (Sutra on the Analysis of Merit), three or five fascicles, seventy-one sheets. Translator lost; included in the Han Records. *Sidi lun* (Treatise on the Four Noble Truths), four fascicles, seventy-five sheets. Translated by Paramārtha of the Chen dynasty. *Bishoufo yinyuan lun* (Treatise on the Causes and Conditions of Pratyekabuddhas), two fascicles, twenty sheets. *Babu lun* (Treatise on the Eighteen Schools), one fascicle, eight sheets. These latter two treatises have lost translators and are now appended to the Qin Records.

*Samayabhedoparacanacakra-śāstra* (Treatise on the Different Tenets of the Schools), one fascicle; also titled *Bheda-samaya-śāstra*, nine sheets. Translated by Paramārtha of the Chen dynasty. *Samayabhedoparacanacakra-śāstra*, one fascicle, eight sheets. Translated by Xuanzang of the Tang dynasty. The above six treatises, totaling thirteen fascicles, are contained in the same volume.

The *Collection of the Sages* (*Xian-sheng ji*) consists of one hundred and eight sections and five hundred and forty-one fascicles, arranged in fifty-seven bundles; it comprises sixty-eight sections totaling one hundred and seventy-three fascicles translated from Sanskrit originals, forty sections of which total three hundred and sixty-eight fascicles. Compiled in this land, there is the *Praise of the Buddha’s Deeds* (*Fo-suoxing-zan jing*) in five fascicles—some editions omit the character "zhuan" (tradition/biography), while others omit "jing" (sūtra); it is also called the *Sūtra on the Original Deeds of the Buddha* (*Fo-benxing-jing*), consisting of ninety sheets. Translated by Dharmakṣema of the Northern Liang dynasty, the *Sūtra on the Original Deeds of the Buddha* (*Fo-benxing-jing*) consists of seven fascicles, also known as the *Biography of the Praise of the Buddha’s Original Deeds*, totaling one hundred and thirteen sheets. Translated by the Song dynasty monk Baoyun, these two collections comprise twelve fascicles in a single bundle.

*Zhuanjibaiyuan jing* (Compendium of One Hundred Avadānas), ten fascicles, one bundle, 150 sheets; translated by Zhi Qian of the Wu dynasty. *Chuyao jing* (Sūtra of the Exalted Utterances), also called *Chuyao lun*, twenty fascicles—or nineteen fascicles—484 sheets; translated by Zhu Fonian of the Yao Qin dynasty. *Xianyu jing* (Sūtra of the Wise and the Foolish), thirteen fascicles—or fifteen, sixteen, or seventeen fascicles—also called *Xianyu yinyuan jing*, 283 sheets; translated by the Śramaṇa Huijue and others of the Northern Wei dynasty. The above two collections comprise thirty-three fascicles in four bundles: the first three bundles each contain eight fascicles, and the fourth bundle contains nine fascicles.

*Daodi jing* (Sūtra on the Stages of the Path), one fascicle; alternatively called *Dadaodi jing*. An excerpt from the *Xiuxing jing*; originally a foreign text in eleven sections, now eight pages. Translated by An Shigao during the Han dynasty. *Xiuxing daodi jing* (Sūtra on the Stages of the Path of Practice), six fascicles. The title of the first fascicle reads *Yuchajia fumi jing*, which is here termed *Xiuxing daodi* or simply *Xiuxing jing*. Alternatively, it consists of seven fascicles and one hundred thirty-five pages. Translated by Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin. *Sengqieluocha suoji jing* (Saṃgharakṣa’s Compendium Sūtra), three fascicles; alternatively called *Sengqieluocha ji*. Alternatively, five fascicles and eighty-five pages. Translated by Saṃghabhūti and others of the Fu Qin. The above three collections comprise ten fascicles and are contained in the same case.

*The Sutra of One Hundred Parables* (Bai yu jing), four fascicles, or five fascicles, or said to be ten fascicles; its details are unknown. Also called *The Sutra of One Hundred Sentences of Parables*, forty-six pages. Translated by Guṇavidi during the Xiao Qi dynasty. *The Sutra on the Original Conditions of the Bodhisattva* (Pusa benyuan jing), three fascicles; also called *The Collected Sutra on the Original Conditions of the Bodhisattva*. Either two or four fascicles, fifty-four pages. Translated by Zhi Qian during the Wu dynasty. *The Essential Collection of Various Sutras on the Gate of Practice for Mahayana Bodhisattvas* (Dacheng xiuxing pusa xingmen zhu jing ya ji), three fascicles, eighty-one pages. Translated by the Tang monk Shi Zhiyan. The above three collections comprise ten fascicles in a single volume.

*Fofazang yinyuan zhuan* (Biographies of the Causes and Conditions of the Dharma-treasury Transmission), six fascicles; alternatively, it lacks the characters "yinyuan" (causes and conditions) and is also called *Fofazang jing* (Sutra of the Dharma-treasury Transmission), in either four or three fascicles, totaling eighty-two sheets.

Translated by Jikaya (Kālaya) together with Tanyao during the Northern Wei dynasty. *Zuochan sanmei jing* (Sutra on the Samādhi of Seated Meditation), three fascicles; also titled *Pusa chanfa jing* (Sutra on the Bodhisattva’s Methods of Meditation), or simply *Chan jing* (Meditation Sutra), or *Aranaya xichanfa jing* (Sutra on the Methods of Practicing Meditation in Aranya).

Alternatively, it is in two fascicles, totaling fifty sheets. Translated by Kumārajīva during the Yao Qin dynasty. *Foyi jing* (Sutra of the Buddha-Medical Doctor), one fascicle; also called *Foyiwang jing* (Sutra of the Buddha-Medical King). Five sheets.
*The Sūtra of Miscellaneous Difficulties of the Sun*, translated by Zhu Lüyán of Wu together with Zhīyuè; one fascicle, fifteen sheets.
*The Sūtra of Mahākāśyapa’s Journey to the Buddha’s Parinirvāṇa*, translated by Zhīqiān of Wu; one fascicle, also titled *The Sūtra of Kāśyapa’s Journey to the Buddha’s Parinirvāṇa*; two sheets.
*The Dharma of the Bodhisattva’s Reproach of Form and Desire*, translated by Zhu Tánwúlán of the Eastern Jin; one fascicle, one sheet.

*The Scripture on the Fourfold Training in the Dharma*, translated by Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin dynasty; one fascicle, or alternatively without the word "scripture," consisting of two sheets. Translated by Guṇabhadra of the Song dynasty:
*The Scripture on the Buddha’s Entry into Nirvāṇa and the Secret Trace Vajrapāṇi’s Sorrowful Attachment*, one fascicle, six sheets.

Translator lost; currently appended to the Yao Qin catalog. *The Scripture on Kātyāyana Preaching the Verses on the Exhaustion of Phenomena*, one fascicle; the title reads *The Buddha’s Bhikṣu Kātyāyana Preaching the Verses on the Exhaustion of Phenomena in One Hundred and Twenty Chapters*, or simply *The Verses of Kātyāyana*; five sheets. *The Scripture on the Buddha’s Treatment of the Body*, one fascicle; also called *The Scripture on Treating the Body*; one sheet. *The Scripture on Treating the Mind*, one fascicle; also called *The Buddha’s Treatment of the Mind*; one sheet. These three collections have lost translators and are now appended to the Western Jin catalog.
The first eleven collections comprise eighteen fascicles in one volume.

*Saṃyukta-ratnapiṭaka-sūtra*, eight fascicles (alternatively said to be thirteen fascicles), 152 sheets; translated by Kiṅ-kia-ye and T’an-yao during the Northern Wei dynasty. *Nāgasena-bhikṣu-sūtra*, two fascicles (alternatively called the *Nāgasena-sūtra* or three fascicles), 31 sheets; translator lost, now appended to the catalogue of the Eastern Jin. The above two collections comprise ten fascicles in one volume.

*The Essential Methods for the Five-Gate Dhyāna Sūtra*, one fascicle, thirty-one sheets; translated by Dharmamitra of the Song dynasty. *Dharmatrāta’s Dhyāna Sūtra*, two fascicles—also titled *Yogācārabhūmi* (translated as *The Stage of Cultivating the Path*) or *The Sūtra on the Contemplation of Impurity*, also known as *The Sūtra on the Expedient Means of Cultivation*; Sengyou states it is the *Sūtra on the Expedient Means of Cultivation* from the Dhyāna section, fifty-one sheets; translated by Buddhabhadra of the Eastern Jin dynasty. *An Explanation of the Essentials of Dhyāna Methods*, two fascicles—also titled *The Sūtra on the Essentials of Dhyāna*, thirty-four sheets; translated by Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin dynasty. *Sūtra on the Essentials of Dhyāna and the Reproach of Desire*, one fascicle—the title reads "Chapter on the Reproach of Desire from the Sūtra on the Essentials of Dhyāna," four sheets. *Sūtra on the Verses of the Contemplation of the Internal Body*, one fascicle—also called *The Wordless*, two sheets. The above two collections were lost to translation during the Han period.

*Faguān jīng* (Sūtra on the Contemplation of Dharmas), one fascicle, six sheets; translated by Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin. *Sīwù lüyào fǎ* (The Essential Dharma of Brief Contemplation), one fascicle—also called *Sīwù yàolüè fǎjīng* or simply *Sīwù jīng*—ten sheets; translated by Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin. *Shí'èryóu jīng* (Sūtra of the Twelve Wanderings), one fascicle, six sheets; translated by Kālodaka of the Eastern Jin. *Jiúzá pìyù jīng* (Old Sūtra of Miscellaneous Parables), two fascicles—also called *Zá pìyù jí jīng*—thirty-seven sheets; translated by Kang Senghui of the Wu. *Zá pìyù jīng* (Miscellaneous Parables Sūtra), one fascicle, nine sheets; translated by Lokakṣema of the Han. The above ten collections comprise thirteen fascicles in one volume.

*Zapiyujing* (Sutra of Miscellaneous Parables), two fascicles; also titled *Pusa du ren jing* (Sutra on the Bodhisattva Saving Humans), twenty-five sheets. Translator lost; included in the Han Records. *Zapiyujing* (Sutra of Miscellaneous Parables), one fascicle, twenty-eight sheets. Translated by Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin. *Ayuwang piyujing* (Sutra of Parables of King Aśoka), one fascicle, seven sheets. The title reads *Tianzun shuo Ayuwang piyujing* (The Sutra of Parables of King Aśoka Spoken by the Celestial Honored One). Since ancient times, the Buddha was called the "Celestial Honored One" (*Tianzun*); thus, this is a discourse by the Buddha himself. *Ayuwang jing* (Sutra of King Aśoka), ten fascicles, one hundred and eleven sheets. Translated by the Liang Tripiṭaka Master Saṃghavarman. The above four collections comprise fourteen fascicles and are contained in the same volume.

*The Biography of King Aśoka* (A-yü-wáng-chuàn), seven fascicles—sometimes with the character "Great" (Dà) prefixed—or five fascicles; also called *The Great Sūtra of King Aśoka* (Dà-ā-yü-wáng-jīng); one hundred sheets. Translated by An Fǎqīn during the Western Jin dynasty. *Sūtra on the Causes and Conditions of King Aśoka’s Son Losing His Sight* (Ā-yù-wáng-xī-huài-mù-yīnyuán-jīng), one fascicle; the title of the preface reads *Sūtra on the Causes and Conditions of King Aśoka’s Crown Prince Dharmavivardhana Losing His Sight*, also called *Sūtra on the Causes and Conditions of King Aśoka’s Crown Prince Losing His Sight* (without the character for "sūtra"); twenty-six sheets. Translated by Dharmanandi during the Fu Qin dynasty. *Excerpts from the End of the Four Āgamas* (Sì-āhán-mù-chāo-jie), two fascicles; also called *Sūtra of Excerpts from the End of the Four Āgamas*; forty-six sheets. Translated by Kumārabuddhi and others during the Fu Qin dynasty. The above three collections comprise ten fascicles and are contained in the same volume.
The *Dharmapada-sūtra*, two fascicles; also called the *Dharmapada-saṃgraha* or the *Dharma-triṃśat*.

Thirty-four sheets. Translated by the Wu dynasty śramaṇas Veṅgīṣeṇa and others. The *Dharmapada-avadāna-sūtra*, four fascicles; also named the *Dharmapada-mūla-prakaraṇa-sūtra*, or the *Dharmapada-upamā-sūtra*. It consists of either five or six fascicles and ninety-five sheets.
Translated by the Western Jin monk Dharmayaśas together with Dharmaghoṣa. The *Kāśyapa-saṃnipāta-sūtra*, one fascicle. Eight sheets.

One fascicle of the *Biographies of the Translation and Compilation of the Tripiṭaka and the Miscellaneous Piṭaka* by An Shigao of the Han dynasty; also titled *Compilation of the Tripiṭaka Sūtras and the Miscellaneous Piṭaka Sūtras*, eight sheets;
translator lost, now appended to the Eastern Jin catalogue. One fascicle of the *Sūtra of the Three Wisdoms*, twelve sheets;

the Master Dao’an’s “Different Scripture from the Liang Territory,” now appended to the Northern Liang catalogue. One fascicle of the *Abhidharma Pañcadharmaprakāra Sūtra*, also titled *Abhidharma Duḥkhaprajñā Sūtra* or *Abhidharma Pañcadharma Sūtra*, eleven sheets.

*The Oral Explanation of the Āgamas on the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination*, one fascicle, translated during the Han dynasty by An Shigao; also titled *The Sutra on Severing the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination* or *The Oral Explanation of the Āgamas*, eight sheets.
*The Minor Stages of the Path*, one fascicle, four sheets, translated during the Han dynasty by Zhi Yao.
*The Sutra of Mañjuśrī’s Aspiration*, one fascicle, or with the word "verse" (*ge*) added [to the title], two sheets.

*Names of Six Bodhisattvas*, one fascicle, translated by Buddhabhadra during the Eastern Jin; recorded as included in the canon, it states that these names of bodhisattvas should also be recited and maintained (one sheet).
*One Hundred and Fifty Verses in Praise of the Buddha*, one fascicle, six sheets; translator lost in China.
*Verses in Praise of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva*, one fascicle, four sheets; translated by Yijing of the Tang dynasty.
Translated by the Tang Dynasty monk Huizhi: The *Shang shi'er ji* (Twelve Collections Above), sixteen fascicles, in one volume.

The *Wuming luocha ji* (Collection on the Rakshasa of Ignorance), also called the *Wuming luocha jing* (Sutra on the Rakshasa of Ignorance), in one fascicle or two fascicles and twenty-three sheets; translator lost, now appended to the *Qin Maoming pusa zhuan* (Biography of Bodhisattva Aśvaghoṣa of the Qin), one fascicle and two sheets; the *Longshu pusa zhuan* (Biography of Bodhisattva Nāgārjuna), one fascicle and three sheets; the *Tipo pusa zhuan* (Biography of Bodhisattva Āryadeva), one fascicle and four sheets. These three collections were translated by Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin.
*The Biography of the Dharma Master Vasubandhu*, one fascicle; here called *Devaputra*, ten pages;
translated by Paramārtha of the Chen dynasty. *A Verse Summary of the Essential Teachings on the Dharma Spoken by Bodhisattva Nāgārjuna for King Śāntaka*, one fascicle, nine pages;
translated by Guṇavarman of the Song dynasty. *A Verse Summary Exhorting All Kings to Generate Resolve*, one fascicle, six pages.
*The Verses of Advice to the King by Bodhisattva Nāgārjuna*, translated by the Song dynasty monk Saṃghavarman, one fascicle, six sheets.

*The Sūtra on Piṇḍola Bharadvāja Preaching the Dharma for King Udayana*, translated by the Tang dynasty monk Yijing, one fascicle; also titled *The Sūtra on Piṇḍola Preaching the Dharma for the King*, eight sheets.
*The Method for Inviting Piṇḍola*, translated by the Song dynasty monk Guṇabhadra, one fascicle; also titled *The Sūtra on the Method for Inviting Piṇḍola*, two sheets.

*Fenbie yebao lüe* (A Brief Analysis of Karmic Retribution), one fascicle, translated by the Song dynasty śramaṇa Huìjiǎn; alternatively titled *Dayǒng púsà fenbie yebao jīng* (Sūtra on the Analysis of Karmic Retribution by Bodhisattva Mahavira) or *Fen yebao lüejí* (Brief Collection on the Analysis of Karmic Retribution), eight sheets, translated by the Song dynasty Saṃghavarman.

*Kāding biqiu shuo danglai bian jing* (Sūtra Spoken by the Bhikṣu Kātyāyanīputra on Future Transformations), one fascicle; alternatively simply titled *Kāding biqiu jing*, nine sheets, translator lost;
now appended to the Song dynasty catalog. *Dafalühan nántimiduol suoshuo fǎzhù jì* (Record of the Persistence of the Dharma Spoken by the Great Arhat Nandimitra), one fascicle, seven sheets.
*The Seventy Stanzas on Sāṃkhya* (Sāṃkhyakārikā), translated by Xuanzang of the Tang dynasty, in three fascicles—also known as the *Sāṃkhya-śāstra*—or in two fascicles, fifty-two pages;
translated by Paramārtha of the Chen dynasty, *The Treatise on the Ten Categories of the Superior Doctrine* (Daśapadārthī), one fascicle, eleven pages.

The above fifteen collections comprise seventeen fascicles in this single volume. Those listed above are translations from Indic originals; those listed below are compilations produced in this land [China].

*Shijia pu* (The Genealogy of Śākyamuni), ten fascicles; there is also a separate five-fascicle version differing in length from this one, totaling 238 sheets. Compiled by Shi Sengyou of the Xiao Qi dynasty. *Shijia shi lüe pu* (A Brief Genealogy of the Śākya Clan), one fascicle; some editions omit the character "lue" (brief), totaling 43 sheets. *Shijia fangzhi* (Topography of the Śākya Clan), two fascicles, 84 sheets. The above two collections were compiled by Shi Daoxuan of the Tang dynasty.
The first collection consists of thirteen fascicles in two volumes: the upper volume contains seven fascicles and the lower volume contains six fascicles.

*Jinglü yixiang* (Diverse Phenomena of Sūtras and Vinaya), fifty fascicles in five volumes, totaling eight hundred twenty-seven sheets; compiled by the Liang dynasty śramaṇa Baochang and others. *Tuoluoni zají* (Miscellaneous Collection of Dhāraṇīs), ten fascicles in one volume, totaling one hundred eighteen sheets; the compiler is unknown. *Zhu jing yaoji* (Essential Collection from Various Sūtras), twenty fascicles totaling five hundred eighty-two sheets; compiled by the Tang dynasty śramaṇa Xuanyun. The aforementioned first collection consists of twenty fascicles divided into three volumes: the upper and lower volumes each contain seven fascicles, and the middle volume contains six fascicles.

The *Chusanzangjiji* (Collection of Records Concerning the Translation of the Tripitaka), fifteen fascicles, three hundred and fourteen sheets, compiled by the Liang dynasty śramaṇa Shi Sengyou; the *Zhongjingmulu* (Catalogue of All Scriptures), seven fascicles, sixty-three sheets, compiled by the Sui dynasty śramaṇas Fajing and others. These two collections comprise twenty-two fascicles in two volumes: the first volume contains ten fascicles, and the second volume contains twelve fascicles.

The *Kaihuang Sanbao Lu* (Record of the Three Jewels of the Kaihuang Era), fifteen fascicles; its internal title reads *Lidai Sanbao Ji* (Chronicle of the Three Jewels Through the Dynasties), consisting of three hundred and eight sheets, compiled by the Sui scholar Fei Changfang. The *Zhongjing Mulü* (Catalogue of All Scriptures), five fascicles, compiled by the Śramaṇas and scholars engaged in translating scriptures by imperial decree in the second year of the Renshou era of the Sui dynasty, totaling eighty-four sheets. The aforementioned two collections comprise twenty fascicles in two bundles.

The *Dàtáng nèidiǎn lù* (Record of Buddhist Scriptures of the Great Tang), ten fascicles, one bundle, three hundred and twenty sheets; compiled by the Tang monk Daoxuan. The *Xù dàtáng nèidiǎn lù* (Continued Record of Buddhist Scriptures of the Great Tang), one fascicle, twenty-two sheets; compiled by the Tang monk Zhisheng. The *Gōngjīn yìjīng tújì* (Illustrated Account of the Translation of Scriptures from Past and Present), four fascicles, sixty sheets; compiled by the Tang monk Jingmai. The *Xù gōngjīn yìjīng tújì* (Continued Illustrated Account of the Translation of Scriptures from Past and Present), one fascicle, sixteen sheets; compiled by the Tang monk Zhisheng. The *Dà zhōu kāndìng zhòngjīng mùlù* (Great Zhou Catalogue of All Translated Scriptures), fifteen fascicles, three hundred and ninety-seven sheets; compiled by the Tang śramaṇa Mingquan and others. These four collections comprise twenty-one fascicles in two bundles: the first bundle contains eleven fascicles, and the second bundle contains ten fascicles.

*The Kaiyuan Catalogue of Buddhist Teachings*, twenty fascicles in two volumes, totaling five hundred and forty-five sheets; compiled by the Tang dynasty monk Zhisheng. *Phonetics and Meanings of the Entire Canon*, twenty-five fascicles (or thirty fascicles), totaling seven hundred and sixty-eight sheets; compiled by the Tang dynasty monk Xuanying. *Phonetics and Meanings of the Newly Translated Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, two fascicles, forty-nine sheets; compiled by the Tang dynasty monk Huiyuan. The above two collections comprise twenty-seven fascicles in four volumes: the first volume contains six fascicles, and each of the remaining three volumes contains seven fascicles.

*Da Tang Xi Yu Ji* (Records of the Western Regions of the Great Tang), twelve fascicles, 234 sheets; translated by Xuanzang of the Tang dynasty. *Jin Gu Fo Dao Lun Heng* (A Balanced Discourse on Buddhism and Daoism from Antiquity to the Present), four fascicles—or three fascicles—99 sheets; compiled by Shi Daoxuan of the Tang dynasty. *Xu Ji Jin Gu Fo Dao Lun Heng* (Continued Collection of A Balanced Discourse on Buddhism and Daoism from Antiquity to the Present), one fascicle, 23 sheets; compiled by Shi Zhisheng of the Tang dynasty. The above three collections comprise seventeen fascicles in two volumes: the first volume contains eight fascicles, and the second volume contains nine fascicles.

*The Record of the Responsive Manifestations of the Triple Gem in the Eastern Lands*, three fascicles (also titled *The Record of the Responsive Manifestations of the Triple Gem in the Divine Land*), ninety-seven sheets; compiled by the Tang Dynasty monk Daoxuan. *The Ritual for Śramaṇas Not Bowing to the Laity*, six fascicles, ninety-seven sheets; compiled by the Tang Dynasty śramaṇa Shi Yancong. These two collections comprise nine fascicles in one volume.

The *Biographies of the Tripitaka Master of Ci’en Monastery of the Great Tang*, ten fascicles, one bundle, one hundred and seventy sheets; compiled by the Tang monk Huili and others. The *Biographies of Eminent Monks Who Sought the Dharma in the Western Regions of the Great Tang*, two fascicles, thirty-five sheets; compiled by the Tang monk Yijing. The *Record of Faxian* (also titled *An Account of Travels through India*), one fascicle, twenty-nine sheets; compiled by Faxian. The *Biographies of Eminent Monks*, fourteen fascicles, one fascicle being a table of contents, totaling three hundred and eleven sheets; compiled by the Liang monk Huijiao. The above three collections comprise seventeen fascicles in two bundles: the first bundle contains nine fascicles, and the second bundle contains eight fascicles.

*Continued Biographies of Eminent Monks*, thirty fascicles, eight hundred and thirty sheets; compiled by the Śramaṇa Shi Daoxuan of Ximing Monastery in Jingzhao during the Tang Dynasty. The first collection consists of thirty fascicles, divided into four bundles (*zhì*): the first and second each contain eight fascicles, while the third and fourth each contain seven fascicles.

*Biànzhèng lùn* (Discourse on Distinguishing Orthodoxy), eight fascicles, one bundle, one hundred and seventy-eight pages; *Pósxià lùn* (Discourse on Refuting Heresies), two fascicles or one fascicle, forty-five pages. These two collections were compiled by the Tang dynasty monk Fali.

*Zhēnzhènglùn* (Discourse on Discerning the Correct), three fascicles, thirty-six sheets; composed by the Tang dynasty monk Xuanyi. *Shí mén biànhuò lùn* (Treatise on Dispelling Delusions through Ten Gates), two or three fascicles, twenty-seven sheets; composed by the Tang dynasty śramaṇa Fuli. *Hóngmíng jí* (Collection for the Propagation and Clarification [of Buddhism]), fourteen fascicles, two hundred and eighty-nine sheets; compiled by the Liang dynasty monk Sengyou. Regarding the five preceding collections, the number of fascicles, volumes, and paper counts may be known from these records.

The *Guang hongming ji* (Collected Works on the Propagation and Clarification of the Dharma) consists of thirty fascicles and seven hundred and seventy sheets, compiled by the Tang dynasty monk Daoxuan. The first collection comprises thirty fascicles, divided into four bundles: the first bundle contains ten fascicles; the second bundle contains seven fascicles; the third bundle contains seven fascicles; and the fourth bundle contains six fascicles.

*Jí zhū jīng lǐchàn yí* (Ritual for Chanting and Repentance Based on Various Sutras), two fascicles, fifty-seven sheets; compiled by the Tang monk Zhìshēng. *Dàtáng Nánhǎi jìguī nèifǎ zhuàn* (Great Tang Record of the Inner Dharma Sent from the South Seas), four fascicles, eighty-seven sheets; compiled by the Tang monk Yìjìng. *Bǐqiūní zhuàn* (Biographies of Bhikṣuṇīs), four fascicles, forty-two sheets; compiled by the Liang *śramaṇa* Bǎochàng. *Biéshuō zuìyào xíngfǎ* (Essential Methods for the Practice of Confessing Sins), one fascicle—or without the character "bié"—totaling four sheets. *Shòuyòng sānshuǐ yào fǎ* (Essential Methods for the Use of the Three Waters), one fascicle—or titled *Yàoxíngfǎ*—four sheets. *Hùmìng fāngshēng guǐyí* (Ritual Procedures for Saving Lives to Protect One’s Life), one fascicle—or titled *Guǐyífǎ*—two sheets. The above three collections were translated by the Tang monk Yìjìng.
Volume 13 of the *Shang* (Upper) section constitutes one fascicle.
In total, this comprises the Sūtras, Vinayas, and Śāstras of the Hīnayāna,
as well as the biographies of worthies and sages.
The works seen entered into the canon total four hundred and thirty-eight sections,
comprising two thousand three hundred and three fascicles.
Two hundred and twenty-two bundles.
*Kaiyuan Shijiao Mulü*, Volume Twenty.
